title: Spec: Governance visibility, advisor office location, and student rules (client)
description:
## Problem Statement

The VP's scorecard shows faculty metrics but not who leads each Faculty. The Dean can view the plan funnel only by School and Department — never per Advisor. The Advisor has no place to publish an office location, so the Student card shows availability but not where to go. The Student cannot read the University Rules the Admin writes. The product name is misspelled "Advaisor" across the UI.

## Solution

A reusable faculty stats component on the VP scorecard shows each Faculty's KPIs with its Deans named. The Dean overview gains filter controls and a second view toggle: the same data grouped By advisor instead of By school/department. A new advisor profile page records the office location; the Student's advisor card displays it like the availability rows. A new student page reads the University Rules. The product name reads "Advisor" everywhere it is visible (English and the Arabic brand أدفايزر); persisted storage keys stay untouched.

## User Stories

1. As a VP, I want a stats component per Faculty that shows its KPIs and names its Deans, so that I can see each faculty's standing and leadership at a glance.
2. As a VP, I want the scorecard to span every Faculty, so that no faculty is missing from my view.
3. As a Dean, I want to filter the faculty data, so that I can focus on the school, department, or metric I care about.
4. As a Dean, I want a second view that groups the same data per Advisor, so that I can review advisors the way I review schools.
5. As a Dean, I want school/department grouping to stay the default, so that my existing overview is unchanged.
6. As an Advisor, I want a profile page where I set my office location, so that Students know where to find me.
7. As a Student, I want my advisor's office location shown with their availability hours, so that I know where meetings happen.
8. As a Student, I want a page listing the University Rules, so that I can read the regulations my plan must honor.
9. As any user, I want the product name to read "Advisor", so that the misspelling does not undermine trust.
10. As a reader of Arabic, I want the brand string corrected in Arabic too, so that both languages agree on the name.

## Implementation Decisions

- The governance API contract is pinned by the paired backend spec: faculty nodes gain `deans: [{id, name}]`; the dashboard accepts `group_by=advisor` (Dean scope) returning advisor-level child nodes with the same metric shape; the advisor profile gains `office_location`; `GET /rules` lists the University Rules.
- FacultyStats is a shared governance component rendering one faculty's KPIs (existing KPI card and rate-band styling) plus its Deans; the VP scorecard renders it per faculty. Bilingual labels and RTL-aware charts follow the design system.
- The Dean overview keeps its current grouping as default and adds a toggle (By school/department / By advisor) plus filter controls; the advisor grouping queries the dashboard with `group_by=advisor`. MSW mocks cover both modes.
- The advisor area gains a profile page and nav entry with an office-location form; the student advisor card renders `office_location` as a row like the availability rows, with an empty state.
- The student area gains a rules page and nav entry listing bilingual rule titles with rendered markdown bodies; MSW mocks cover it.
- The rename touches user-visible strings only: document title and meta, the SEO title suffix, the i18n app name in English and Arabic, and the repo's agent docs. Persisted storage keys (`advaisor.token`, `advaisor.theme`, `advaisor.language`) and mock token formats stay as-is, so existing sessions survive.

## Testing Decisions

- Component and route tests through Testing Library with MSW mocks — the existing seams; no new seams. Prior art: the governance route tests, the advisor-hours and profile tests, the admin rules tests.
- Good tests assert what the user sees: deans render per faculty, the toggle switches grouping, the office location renders for the student, rules render bilingually, and the brand string reads "Advisor".

## Out of Scope

- Renaming persisted storage keys or mock token formats; announcements; per-student drilldowns; changes to admin rules CRUD; backend behavior (covered by the backend spec).

## Further Notes

- Backend contract spec lives in the backend repo's tracker.
close_reason: FacultyStats with deans lands on the VP scorecard; dean toggle, advisor profile, office location, student rules, and the Advisor rename verified in place

title: Mock server generated from the OpenAPI contract
description:
## Question

How does the team generate MSW 2 handlers and demo data from `../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json` so the client develops before the backend is reachable?

## Context

- MSW 2 and `@mswjs/data` are already dependencies.
- The contract has SSE endpoints, pagination, and stable error slugs.
- The six screen states must be demoable: loading, empty, error, permission denied, stale SIS, window closed.
- Search the web for openapi-to-msw generators (for example openapi-msw), their MSW 2 support, and SSE mock feasibility.

## Record

A recommendation: generator or hand-written handlers, how scenario seeds cover the six states, how SSE is mocked, and how the mock server runs (npm script). Name the runner-up.
notes:
# Resolution: Mock server generated from the OpenAPI contract

Ticket: acad-abl.7 (wayfinder:research). Question: how does the team generate MSW 2 handlers and demo data from the OpenAPI contract so the client develops before the backend is reachable?

## Local facts

- The repo already runs MSW 2.15.0, @mswjs/data 0.16.2, and @mswjs/http-middleware 0.10.3 (package.json). The mock layer lives in `src/testing/mocks/` with `browser.ts` (worker), `server.ts` (vitest), `db.ts` (@mswjs/data with JSON persistence), and per-domain handlers.
- `mock-server.ts` boots the same handlers as a real HTTP server with express via `createMiddleware`, run by `npm run run-mock-server` (vite-node, port `APP_MOCK_API_PORT`, default 8080). `npm run test-e2e` starts it with pm2 before Playwright.
- `src/config/env.ts` validates `ENABLE_API_MOCKING`; `src/testing/mocks/index.ts` calls `worker.start()` before React mounts.
- The current db and handlers model the bulletproof-react demo domain (teams, discussions, comments), not the Advaisor domain. The Advaisor work replaces these models.
- Contract: `/home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json`, OpenAPI 3.0.3, 84 schemas, 61 operations by method count (31 POST, 21 GET, 4 DELETE, 3 PUT, 2 PATCH; the ticket cites 58).
- Envelopes: single resources wrap in `{ data }`; collections add `meta` and `links` (`UserList`, `AdvisorCaseloadStudentList`); `NotificationList` also carries `unread_count`. Errors are `ErrorResponse { message }` and `ValidationError { message, errors: Record<string, string[]> }` with stable slugs in the `errors` map.
- The two AI turn endpoints POST and return `text/event-stream` with named frames: `token`, `tool.applied`, `submit.suggested`, `submit.result`, `turn.completed`, `error`, and one `submit.armed` frame on the submit-arm endpoint. Turn quota exhaustion is a 429 with `QuotaExceededError`.

## Evaluated options

### 1. openapi-msw (typed wrapper, hand-written resolvers)

`openapi-msw` 2.1.0, published 2026-09-30. Zero runtime dependencies. Peer dependency `msw ^2.10.5 || ^3.0.0`, so it fits the installed MSW 2.15.0 with no upgrade. It is not a code generator for handlers. You generate TS types with `openapi-typescript` (7.13.0) from openapi.json, then write handlers through `createOpenApiHttp<paths>()`. Path params, query params, status codes, and response bodies type-check against the contract; `response.untyped(...)` is the escape hatch. Handlers stay ordinary MSW `HttpHandler` instances, so `browser.ts`, `server.ts`, and the express middleware keep working unchanged.

Sources: https://www.npmjs.com/package/openapi-msw, https://github.com/christoph-fricke/openapi-msw, https://www.npmjs.com/package/openapi-typescript

### 2. msw-auto-mock (full generator, random data)

`msw-auto-mock` 0.32.1, published 2026-04-18. CLI generates handler files with faker-driven random data from the spec, peer `msw >= 2`, and carries heavy dependencies including AI SDKs for optional LLM-generated fixtures. Random data cannot pin the six deterministic screen states, and generated files hide the envelope and 422 slug contract inside generated code.

Source: https://www.npmjs.com/package/msw-auto-mock

### 3. @stoplight/prism-cli (contract mock server, not MSW)

Prism 5.16.0 serves a live mock from openapi.json with request validation. It sits outside the MSW setup, so it shares no state model with vitest, cannot express scenario seeds as code, and duplicates the mock layer.

Source: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stoplight/prism-cli

### 4. Hand-written plain MSW handlers (current state)

What the repo does today for the demo domain. Full control, zero new packages, but every path, status, and payload shape drifts from the contract with no compiler signal.

## Recommendation: hybrid, generator only for types

Generate types from the contract, hand-write resolvers through openapi-msw. This is a hybrid, not a full generator.

1. Add `openapi-typescript` and `openapi-msw` as dev dependencies.
2. Generate `src/testing/mocks/schema.d.ts` from `../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json`. Re-run when the backend contract changes. Contract drift becomes a type error in handler code.
3. Write handlers per domain with `createOpenApiHttp<paths>({ baseUrl: env.API_URL })`. Keep @mswjs/data as the stateful store with Advaisor models (user, plan, planned_course, plan_conversation, plan_conversation_message, academic_record, course_attempt, availability_window_row, notification). Resolvers read and mutate the db, exactly like `discussions.ts` does today.
4. Sixty-one operations is small enough for hand-written resolvers, and the states that matter (envelope shape, `meta` and `links`, 422 slug maps, quota 429) need exact payloads that random generation cannot promise.

Why not a full generator: the six screen states must be deterministic per scenario. msw-auto-mock produces random faker payloads, which forces post-hoc patching of generated files and defeats the purpose on every regeneration.

Runner-up: msw-auto-mock, as a one-shot scaffolder for low-traffic GET endpoints, deleted after real handlers land. Do not keep generated handlers in the tree long term.

## Scenario switching for the six states

Add a scenario concept at the mock layer, keyed by seed functions over @mswjs/data:

- One seed function per state: `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `permission-denied`, `stale-sis`, `registration-closed`. Each seeds the db and sets a scenario module (plain module or zustand store in `src/testing/mocks`).
- Browser dev: read `?scenario=stale-sis` in `enableMocking()` (src/testing/mocks/index.ts) before `worker.start()`, fall back to `VITE_APP_MOCK_SCENARIO`, default to the happy path. This needs no router change and survives refresh via `sessionStorage`.
- E2E and standalone server: expose `POST /__mocks/scenario { name }` on the express app in `mock-server.ts`. Playwright calls it before navigation, so one pm2 process serves all scenarios.
- Handlers consult the scenario only for failure injection: `error` returns `ValidationError` with the agreed 422 slug, `permission-denied` returns 403 `ErrorResponse`, `registration-closed` returns the domain 422 or 409 slug from the contract. `loading` is `networkDelay()` with a large delay. `empty` and `stale-sis` are pure data seeds (no records; `Staleness` fields set on `AcademicRecord`).

## SSE mock for the AI turn stream

MSW 2.12.0 (2025-11-05) added first-class SSE with `sse()` from `msw/sse`; fixes landed through 2.15.0, the installed version. `sse<FrameMap>()` accepts a typed event map, so the contract frames map directly: `token`, `tool.applied`, `submit.suggested`, `submit.result`, `turn.completed`, `error`, `submit.armed`. The resolver calls `client.send()` per frame on a timer for token cadence, then `client.close()` after `turn.completed`.

Caveats from the docs: the `sse` namespace intercepts `EventSource` connections and is browser-first ("The EventSource API isn't currently supported in Node.js, limiting the SSE interception to the browser"). The contract endpoints are POST, which matches the repo's request shape; MSW handles this (issue 2712 closed 2026-04-14 added POST SSE support). If the client uses a fetch stream instead of `EventSource`, mock it with `http.post(...)` returning a `ReadableStream` of `data: {...}\n\n` frames with `text/event-stream` headers, which the docs cover under streaming responses. The express standalone server path (pm2 e2e) bypasses MSW anyway, so add two small express routes in `mock-server.ts` that write the same frame sequences with `res.write`; quota state can return 429 `QuotaExceededError` before the stream opens.

Sources: https://mswjs.io/blog/server-sent-events-are-here, https://mswjs.io/docs/sse/, https://mswjs.io/docs/sse/intercepting-sources/, https://github.com/mswjs/msw/issues/2712, https://mswjs.io/docs/http/mocking-responses/streaming

## npm script wiring

No new runner. Keep the two existing surfaces and add one codegen script:

- `"mock:types": "openapi-typescript ../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json -o src/testing/mocks/schema.d.ts"` and run it as part of `prepare` or before `check-types`.
- Dev in the browser: `ENABLE_API_MOCKING=true npm run dev` with `?scenario=` on the URL. Unchanged.
- Standalone server for e2e or API-only work: `npm run run-mock-server` (vite-node mock-server.ts). SSE gets two express routes there.
- Vitest: `server.ts` uses the same handlers with the `loading`/`error` scenarios set per test through `server.use(...)` overrides.

## Verdict in one line

Hybrid: openapi-typescript for types plus openapi-msw for typed hand-written handlers over @mswjs/data, scenario seeds switched by `?scenario=` query param in the browser and `POST /__mocks/scenario` on the standalone server, SSE frames mocked with `sse()` from msw/sse in the browser and plain express streams in the standalone server. Runner-up: msw-auto-mock for throwaway scaffolding only.
close_reason: Hybrid: openapi-typescript types + openapi-msw typed hand-written handlers over @mswjs/data; scenarios via ?scenario= and POST /__mocks/scenario; SSE via msw/sse or express streams; runner-up msw-auto-mock

title: SSE streaming pattern for AI chat
description:
## Question

What pattern should the client use to consume the AI turn stream (`text/event-stream`) with TanStack Query 5?

## Context

- Contract: `POST /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}/turns` is SSE; the frame types are spelled out in the operation description in `../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json`.
- Stack: React 19, TanStack Query 5, MSW 2.
- Search the web for current patterns: fetch ReadableStream vs EventSource (POST body rules out native EventSource), abort handling, retry, react-query integration, mocking SSE with MSW.

## Record

A recommended pattern with a short code sketch, cancellation behavior, error and mid-stream failure handling, and how MSW will mock it. Name the runner-up.
close_reason: Use fetch+ReadableStream SSE reader inside useMutation, write frames to a zustand feature store, invalidate query caches on terminal frames; mock via MSW http.post returning a ReadableStream text/event-stream body

title: Charting library for governance dashboards
description:
## Question

Which charting library should the dean and VP dashboards use?

## Context

- Needs from design.md: funnel, scoreboard tables, heatmap quartile colors, crimson color ramp, dark mode, RTL, accessibility (DS-A rules). Candidates: recharts, visx, nivo, echarts, chart.js with react-chartjs-2.
- Bundle budget matters (Vite, route-level splitting).
- Search the web for current maintenance status, React 19 compatibility, RTL support, and bundle sizes.

## Record

A recommendation with reasons tied to the needs above, bundle-size numbers, and the runner-up. State whether tables (scoreboard) stay plain HTML with the chart library used only for funnel and trends.
notes:
# Resolution: charting library for governance dashboards (acad-abl.5)

Verdict: use recharts 3.x on the dean and VP dashboards, and use it only for the funnel chart and trend sparklines. Runner-up: visx. Scoreboard, scorecard, and drill-down stay plain HTML tables. The heatmap stays a hand-rolled token-styled grid, not a chart-lib component. recharts is a new dependency, so it needs explicit human approval under DS-G-07 and the repo AGENTS.md rule before anyone installs it.

## What the governance screens actually draw

Sources: design.md 5.2, 5.4, 6.2; docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md section 13; docs/product/03-DESIGN-PLAN.md section 2.

- FunnelChart (D1, dean): horizontal bars with stage labels and counts. design.md 5.4 defines it exactly this way, so no candidate needs a native funnel type.
- Trends: sparkline cells are optional in ScoreboardTable (design.md 5.4). A small line or area chart covers D2 advisor trends.
- Heatmap (D1, design.md 6.2 plus 3.5): quartile colors with exact light and dark bg/fg token pairs. A plain HTML grid with data-token classes renders it and doubles as the DS-C-10 text alternative.
- ScoreboardTable (D1, D2), FacultyScorecard (V1), DrilldownTable (V2): tables with tabular-nums and CSV export (design.md 5.4; foundation section 13, metrics locked by Q40). Confirmed: these stay plain HTML. No chart library touches them.

So the library serves exactly two jobs: one horizontal bar chart and one sparkline. This finding alone disqualifies heavyweight engines.

## Scorecard against repo constraints

| Criterion | recharts 3.10 | visx 4.0 | nivo 0.99 | echarts 6 + wrapper | chart.js 4 + react-chartjs-2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Funnel as horizontal bars | layout=vertical BarChart, direct | compose Bar + scales | layout=horizontal | bar series, direct | indexAxis=y, direct |
| Trend sparkline | AreaChart | LinePath/AreaClosed | ResponsiveLine | line series | Line |
| Dark mode as token flip (DS-C-03) | yes: SVG accepts fill=var(--token); shadcn charts prove the pattern | yes: raw SVG | no: JS theme object | no: JS option objects | no: canvas color parser rejects var() |
| Colors from 3.5 tokens (crimson ramp, data quartiles) | var() references to --color-data-* | var() references | JS palette copy | JS palette copy | JS palette copy |
| RTL (DS-L-03 to L-07) | no native RTL; explicit props; one open a11y bug | fully manual, nothing fights dir | open feature request since 2019 | open feature request | best nominal rtl/textDirection options, but canvas |
| Accessibility (DS-A-03, DS-C-10) | accessibilityLayer: roles, labels, keyboard | you build all of it | basic aria props | aria module | canvas: no DOM, fallback only |
| Bundle (gzip, measured, parts used) | 118 kB | 26 kB | 114 kB | 199 kB | 64 kB |
| React 19 (app pins ^19.3.0) | yes, peers ^19 | yes, peers ^18/^19 | yes, peers ^19 | wrapper peers >=16, loose | yes, peers ^19 |
| Maintenance (npm, checked 2026-10-01) | 3.10.1 on 2026-07-25, canaries into 2026-09 | 4.0.0 on 2026-06-11 | 0.99.0 on 2025-05-23, 17 months quiet | echarts active; wrapper tag trails, releases unpublished | both last published 2025-10, quiet year |

## Bundle sizes, measured

Method: esbuild 0.28.2, bundle, minify, ESM, funnel (horizontal bars) plus trend (area or line) plus tooltip and legend per stack; react and react-dom external. Measured 2026-10-01 in /tmp/chartsize against the latest published versions listed above. Gzipped:

- visx (scale, shape, axis, grid, tooltip, group): 26 kB
- chart.js with selective registration + react-chartjs-2: 64 kB
- nivo (@nivo/bar + @nivo/line): 114 kB
- recharts (vertical-layout BarChart + AreaChart + Tooltip + Legend + ResponsiveContainer): 118 kB
- echarts core (bar + line + grid + tooltip + legend + SVGRenderer) + echarts-for-react lib/core: 199 kB

## Why recharts wins

1. It is the only candidate whose theming matches the token architecture as a MUST. DS-C-01 bans raw hex in components; DS-C-03 makes dark mode a token flip. recharts renders SVG, and SVG presentation attributes accept var(--token) directly. shadcn/ui charts use this exact pattern: recharts under the hood, colors defined as CSS variables with .dark variants, passed as fill=var(--color-key). The repo already commits to the shadcn pattern (design.md 0.5). The 3.5 series and quartile tokens drop in as --color-data-* per Appendix B. See https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/chart
2. Accessibility has a supported path. The accessibilityLayer prop adds roles, aria labels, and arrow-key navigation (https://github.com/recharts/recharts/wiki/Recharts-and-accessibility, https://recharts.github.io/en-US/api). DS-C-10 still requires the text alternative table for every chart, and we ship it regardless.
3. React 19 is a peer and works. recharts 2.x had React 19 rendering problems (https://github.com/recharts/recharts/issues/4558); the 3.0 rewrite resolved them (https://github.com/recharts/recharts/wiki/3.0-migration-guide). The app pins react ^19.3.0.
4. Maintenance is strong. 3.10.1 shipped 2026-07-25 with canary releases into 2026-09-21 (npm registry).
5. The API fits two chart types with a small wrapper surface. FunnelChart becomes one vertical-layout BarChart with categorical-series fills; trends become one AreaChart. Both wrappers get a11y labeling, the token classes, and RTL props in one place.

## Why not the others

- visx (runner-up, 26 kB): smallest bundle, active (4.0.0, June 2026), raw SVG keeps var() theming, and explicit scales make RTL mirroring a deliberate choice rather than a fight. It loses because DS-C-10 obligations (tooltips, legends, keyboard access, focus) become per-chart hand work, which recreates the hand-rolled-SVG path DS-C-10 already permits, minus the framework recharts gives for free. Choose visx if the 118 kB cost is judged too high after real profiling.
- echarts + echarts-for-react (199 kB): heaviest by far even tree-shaken; the wrapper adds release-hygiene risk (latest tag 3.0.6 from 2026-01; versions 3.1.7 and 3.2.7 were published and then unpublished in May 2026 per the npm time log). RTL is an open feature request (https://github.com/apache/echarts/issues/19609). Theming is JS option objects, so a dark toggle means rebuilding options, which breaks the DS-C-03 token-flip model. The API surface (3D, gauges) covers ground DS-C-10 bans outright.
- nivo (114 kB): theming is a JS theme object, not CSS variables, and RTL remains an open issue from 2019 (https://github.com/plouc/nivo/issues/357); the documented workaround pins charts to dir=ltr, which violates the mirror-layout intent of DS-L-03. Slowest maintainer of the five: 0.99.0 on 2025-05-23.
- chart.js + react-chartjs-2 (64 kB): best nominal RTL options (plugins.legend.rtl and textDirection, https://www.chartjs.org/docs/latest/configuration/legend.html) and a healthy 64 kB, but it renders to canvas. Canvas text and colors are painted by a JS parser that does not resolve var(), so every token means a JS palette copy and a chart rebuild on theme flip. That fails DS-C-01 and DS-C-03 as written, and it loses the DOM that carries accessible labels.

## RTL plan under recharts

No candidate has true RTL. With recharts, the wrappers set direction explicitly: XAxis reversed plus YAxis orientation=right for the funnel in RTL, margins mirrored through logical properties in the container, and labels render as SVG text that follows the page font stack. Track recharts issue 4214 (accessibilityLayer arrow keys do not mirror in RTL, open, https://github.com/recharts/recharts/issues/4214); its user impact stays low because DS-C-10 and DS-A-03 require the table alternative, and the table carries reading order correctly in both directions.

## Risks and follow-ups

- 118 kB gzip is real but bounded. Route-level code splitting (design.md 0.5) loads it only on /dean and /vp; trends are tiny extra AreaChart instances, not new routes.
- Dependency approval: recharts enters the tree only after a human approves it (DS-G-07, repo AGENTS.md). This issue is the research input for that approval.
- Heatmap first: build the heatmap as a token-styled HTML grid with --color-data-* theme tokens (Appendix B note). It needs no library and validates the token plumbing before any chart lands.
- Implementation order after approval: approve dep, add --color-data-* tokens, build FunnelChart on BarChart, then the optional trend sparkline, each with story, test, and the DS-C-10 text alternative.

## Sources

title: i18n and RTL approach
description:
## Question

How does the client implement EN/AR i18n and RTL mirroring?

## Context

- design.md rules: Inter for EN, Cairo for AR, Latin numerals always, mirrored layout, bilingual surfaces per role.
- Stack: React 19, Vite, Tailwind v4 (Appendix B token block).
- Search the web for current library guidance: i18next (react-i18next), Lingui, Intlayer, or others; RTL via Tailwind v4 logical properties vs dir-based variants; Cairo font loading (self-host vs Google Fonts).

## Record

A recommendation: library, file organization, where translations live, how language preference persists (a LanguagePreference field exists in the API), RTL mechanics, font loading, and numeral handling. Name the runner-up.
notes:
# acad-abl.6 resolution: i18n and RTL approach

Question: how does the client implement EN/AR i18n and RTL mirroring?

## Recommendation

Use **react-i18next (v17, on i18next v26)** with typed EN/AR JSON namespaces, `dir` driven from `<html>`, Tailwind v4 logical properties as the mirroring mechanism, self-hosted Cairo through Fontsource, and centralized number/date helpers that force Latin numerals.

### Why react-i18next wins here

- Largest ecosystem and widest agent familiarity; react-i18next 17.0.15 is current on npm (registry.npmjs.org, May 2026).
- Typed keys via `CustomTypeOptions` module augmentation satisfy DS-L-06 ("typed EN/AR dictionaries"). Strict key checking needs `strictNullChecks` on, which this repo has (i18next.com/overview/typescript).
- `i18next.dir(lng)` returns `rtl` or `ltr` per language, so the dir switch is one call (i18next.com/overview/api).
- Runtime JSON namespaces fit the design's merge gate: a vitest unit test can iterate en keys and assert every key exists in ar, enforcing "every key exists in both languages before merge" (DS-L-06) mechanically.
- Namespaces load lazily per feature via dynamic import, matching route-level splitting.
- Two locales with small, fully known catalogs remove the main Lingui and Paraglide argument (bundle size). i18next's runtime cost is irrelevant at this scale.

### Comparison (primary sources)

| Library | Model | Fit for this repo |
|---|---|---|
| react-i18next 17 | Runtime JSON namespaces, typed via augmentation, lazy namespaces | Matches DS-L-06 central dictionaries, Vite SPA, trivial key-parity test. Chosen. |
| Lingui (lingui.dev) | Compile-time macros, ICU, PO catalogs, ~2 kB runtime | Strong runner-up. Needs a Vite/SWC plugin plus an extraction step in every copy change. Source-text IDs churn against the "bilingual copy is final before merge" gate. |
| Intlayer (intlayer.org) | Per-component `.content.ts` files, strict types, built-in CMS | Colocation contradicts DS-L-06's central dictionary seed. ICU support still work in progress. Youngest ecosystem. |
| Paraglide JS v2 (paraglidejs.com) | Compiler emits typed ESM functions, tree-shaken, up to 70% smaller bundles | Best when keys are known at build time; viable future migration, its docs note a compiler path from i18next files. Not needed for 2 locales. |

**Runner-up: Lingui.** Pick it if catalog size or ICU complexity grows past what i18next's syntax handles comfortably.

## File organization

```
src/lib/i18n/
  i18n.ts                # init: resources, supportedLngs ['en','ar'], fallbackLng 'en',
                         # interpolation: { escapeValue: false } (React escapes), returnNull: false
  i18next.d.ts           # declare module 'i18next' { interface CustomTypeOptions { ... } }
  locales/
    en/common.json       # shell, topbar, buttons, states, validation, errors
    en/auth.json
    en/plan.json
    en/advisor.json
    en/governance.json
    en/admin.json
    ar/...               # exact mirror of en keys
  format.ts              # formatNumber, formatDate, formatTime helpers (numeral rule below)
  dayjs-ar-latin.ts      # dayjs locale clone of 'ar' without Arabic-Indic postformat
```

Namespaces mirror features. Cross-cutting copy (state chips, buttons, validation) lives in `common`. Add one namespace per new feature. A key-parity vitest test in `src/lib/i18n/__tests__` fails the merge when en and ar keys diverge; this is the mechanical form of DS-W-01.

The prototype `translations.js` seed migrates into these JSON files; DS-L-06 names it as the seed and design.md's token block already carries `--font-arabic`.

## Language preference persistence and API sync

The API contract (backend `openapi.json`): `LanguagePreference` is the enum `'en' | 'ar'`. `User` carries `language_preference`, returned by `GET /api/me`. `RegisterInput` carries it for `POST /api/register`. No endpoint updates it after registration, so the server holds the registration-time preference and the client owns device-level toggles.

1. Store: `useLanguageStore` (Zustand + persist to localStorage, key `advaisor.language`), same pattern design.md prescribes for the theme toggle ("language toggles `dir` + dictionary, both persist").
2. Boot before login: initial language is the stored value, else `navigator.language` starts with `ar` -> `'ar'`, else `'en'`.
3. After login: `GET /api/me` returns `language_preference`. If the user has never toggled on this device, adopt the profile preference. A local toggle wins afterward, per device.
4. Registration sends `language_preference` from the signup form choice, since `RegisterInput` supports it.
5. Toggle: the `LanguageToggle` calls `i18next.changeLanguage`, updates the Zustand store, sets `document.documentElement.lang` and `dir` from `i18next.dir(lng)`, and switches `dayjs.locale`. One `language-effect` module owns the DOM side effects.
6. Backend gap to file: no `PATCH /api/me`, so toggles never sync back. If Advaisor wants the profile as source of truth across devices, file a backend ticket for a language_preference update endpoint; the client change is then one mutation.

## RTL mechanics

- **One source of truth:** `dir` on `<html>`, set from `i18next.dir()`. DS-L-03: no directional hardcoding.
- **Mirroring runs on logical properties, not dir variants.** Tailwind v4 ships `ps-*` / `pe-*` (`padding-inline-*`), `ms-*` / `me-*`, `start-*` / `end-*` (`inset-inline-*`), and `text-start` / `text-end`; the docs show them flipping with `dir` (tailwindcss.com/docs/padding). This is DS-L-03 verbatim; physical `pl-6` and `left-0` stay banned in shared components.
- **`rtl:` / `ltr:` variants are the exception path,** for what logical properties cannot express: directional icon flips (DS-L-04). Example: `rtl:-scale-x-100` on a lucide chevron. lucide marks flip-ables; flip when unclear.
- **Bidi isolation:** port the prototype `.bidi-code` pattern (`unicode-bidi: isolate`) as a utility or small `BidiCode` component; wrap course codes like `CS 101` wherever they sit inside Arabic sentences (DS-L-05).
- **Font switch:** the token block already maps `[dir='rtl'] body { font-family: var(--font-arabic) }` (design.md appendix B), which is DS-T-02.
- Layout direction mirrors automatically; numbers, dates, and course codes stay Latin (DS-L-07). Acceptance in design.md section 0 requires both directions to render correctly in review.

## Font loading

- **Self-host both families through Fontsource.** Add `@fontsource-variable/inter` and `@fontsource-variable/cairo`, import in `src/main.tsx`, and drop the `rsms.me` link tag from `index.html`. DS-T-01 requires self-hosting (or the existing link) with `font-display: swap` and bans new Google Fonts links.
- Verified from the `@fontsource-variable/cairo` CSS: `font-display: swap`, family `'Cairo Variable'`, weight range 200 to 1000, and three `unicode-range` subsets (arabic, latin, latin-ext), so a browser only downloads the subset the page actually renders. Vite fingerprints the woff2 files.
- **font-display consequence:** `swap` shows a fallback system font first, then swaps to Cairo when loaded. Arabic first paint in the fallback is the visible jolt, because Cairo metrics differ from system sans. Mitigation that stays inside DS-T-01: `<link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>` for the arabic subset file in `index.html` to start the fetch earlier, and a size-adjusted fallback `@font-face` if layout shift shows up in review. Never block render on the font (that would be `font-display: block`, a DS-T-01 deviation).
- Update `--font-sans` to the Fontsource family name and keep `--font-arabic` as is, aligning `'Cairo'` to `'Cairo Variable'`.

## Numeral handling (DS-T-03: Latin numerals in both locales)

Three traps, all verified:

1. **`Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG')` emits Arabic-Indic digits** (`١٢٣٤٥٦٫٧٨٩`, MDN). Never call it bare. The central helper uses the `nu` extension: `new Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG-u-nu-latn')`, which keeps Arabic separators and grouping while rendering Latin glyphs. `format.ts` is the only place that formats numbers; i18next `formatting` hooks stay unused for numbers so the rule has one enforcement point. Charts keep `tabular-nums` (DS-C-11).
2. **dayjs `ar` locale converts digits in `postformat`** (source: dayjs `src/locale/ar.js` replaces `0-9` with `٠-٩` and commas with `،`). A custom locale clone in `dayjs-ar-latin.ts` copies the `ar` month and weekday names and drops the digit postformat, so `DD MMM YYYY` renders `15 يناير 2026`, not `١٥`. This satisfies DS-L-07 (dayjs per locale) and DS-T-03 together.
3. **Raw string interpolation:** numbers passed into i18next interpolation go through `format.ts` first.

Time renders as timezone-neutral 24h (DS-W-06); course codes pass through `BidiCode`.

## Enforcement summary

- Key parity test: en and ar namespaces hold identical key sets (DS-L-06, DS-W-01).
- ESLint guard idea: flag `pl-|pr-|ml-|mr-|left-|right-|text-left|text-right` in shared components (`src/components/**`), giving DS-L-03 a mechanical gate.
- Design review per section 0: both themes, both directions, bilingual copy final.

## Sources

- https://registry.npmjs.org/react-i18next/latest (version 17.0.15)
- https://www.i18next.com/overview/typescript (CustomTypeOptions, strict key types)
- https://www.i18next.com/overview/api (dir())
- https://github.com/i18next/i18next-browser-languageDetector (persistence options)
- https://lingui.dev/introduction (compile-time macros, PO catalogs, ~2 kB runtime)
- https://intlayer.org/doc/why (per-component content, ICU work in progress)
- https://paraglidejs.com/ (compiler, tree-shaking, i18next compat)
- https://tailwindcss.com/docs/padding (logical properties flip with dir; rtl:/ltr: variants)
- https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fontsource-variable/cairo@latest/index.css (font-display: swap, subsets, weight 200-1000)
- https://fontsource.org/docs/getting-started/introduction (self-hosting rationale)
- https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/NumberFormat (ar-EG default digits, -u-nu-latn)
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/iamkun/dayjs/dev/src/locale/ar.js (postformat digit conversion)
- Backend contract: /home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json (LanguagePreference enum, User.language_preference, RegisterInput, GET /api/me, no update endpoint)
- design.md: DS-T-01..03, DS-L-03..07, DS-W-01/06, DS-C-11, section 4 component table, appendix B token block
close_reason: Recommend react-i18next v17 with typed EN/AR JSON namespaces under src/lib/i18n, Zustand-persisted language synced from GET /api/me language_preference, dir on html driven by i18next.dir, Tailwind v4 logical properties for mirroring, self-hosted Cairo via Fontsource, Latin numerals forced via ar-EG-u-nu-latn and a dayjs ar locale clone without postformat; runner-up Lingui

title: Wayfinder map: Advaisor React client v1 decisions
description:
## Destination

Every product, UX, and technical decision the Advaisor React client needs is settled and recorded on this map. Done means the follow-up spec effort can start without asking the owner another question.

## Notes

Domain: Advaisor is the E-JUST academic plan platform with an AI advisor inside it. Five roles: student, advisor, dean, VP, admin. The academic plan has the settled 8-state lifecycle. Rules V1–V6 validate plans. AI helps students only; humans own every decision.

Truth precedence: `docs/product/` (product truth), then `design.md` (design truth, rule IDs `DS-*`), then vendored skills. AGENTS.md's bulletproof-react demo overview is stale boilerplate; ignore it.

Backend baseline: the API contract lives at `../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json` (bearer Sanctum tokens, `data` envelope, pagination meta, SSE `text/event-stream` for AI turns, error slugs on 422, 503 SIS outage). The backend map "Wayfinder map: Advaisor v1 system decisions and features" holds the settled system decisions. This map never reopens them; contract changes go back to the backend effort.

Skills: grilling and domain-modeling open every grilling ticket. HITL tickets resolve only with the map owner, except where the owner delegated: on 2026-10-01 the owner delegated the remaining tickets, so design questions are decided by the agent against design.md and the skills, and feature questions are answered from the backend map's settled decisions (cite the decision number). Grilling sessions open with the setup in `docs/agents/grilling-session.md` (see the ticket "Restore docs/agents workflow files" until it exists). UI-shaping tickets consult ui-ux-pro-max and impeccable per design.md section 10, announced per DS-AI-01. Grilling sessions on UI surfaces may call the prototype skill to raise fidelity with a cheap artifact.

Standing preferences: trusted package installs are authorized (owner, 2026-10-01), each with a stated reason. One ticket resolves per session, research excepted. Research digests live in ticket notes, not new doc files. Refer to tickets by name, never by bare id. This map decides and specifies; it does not build the client.

## Decisions so far

- [Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions](acad-abl.1): The client honors 8 plan states (the contract adds a ninth terminal `discarded`), 3 SIS-parameterized validation checks keyed off four 422 slugs, a 17-permission matrix, 9 notification slugs, 6 SSE turn frames plus submit.armed, a never-blocking staleness banner, an SIS-owned window with no client-visible dates, and a 100-turns-per-term AI quota that returns 429.
- [Client API inventory from the OpenAPI contract](acad-abl.2): All 61 operations mapped to hooks, query keys, and invalidations; 9 contract gaps flagged, including no refresh endpoint, no page param, and no quota endpoint.
- [Auth token storage for the SPA](acad-abl.3): Bearer token in localStorage behind an axios interceptor with one global 401 handler; switch to Sanctum SPA cookies if the backend shares a domain or adds refresh.
- [SSE streaming pattern for AI chat](acad-abl.4): Raw fetch ReadableStream reader as an async generator of zod-typed frames, driven by useMutation into a zustand store; mock in MSW with a ReadableStream body.
- [Charting library for governance dashboards](acad-abl.5): Recharts 3 for funnel and trends only; scoreboard and heatmap stay plain HTML on the token grid. Runner-up: visx.
- [i18n and RTL approach](acad-abl.6): react-i18next with typed EN/AR namespaces, dir-driven Tailwind v4 logical properties, self-hosted Inter and Cairo, Latin numerals via Intl plus a dayjs override.
- [Mock server generated from the OpenAPI contract](acad-abl.7): Hybrid openapi-typescript types plus hand-written openapi-msw handlers over @mswjs/data; scenarios switch via a query param in the browser and a POST endpoint for Playwright.
- [App skeleton and demo demolition](acad-abl.8): Keep the scaffold (api client, query, ui primitives, MSW, storybook, plop, gates); delete the demo features and routes; 12 Advaisor feature folders; five lazy role sections with RoleRoute guards; four env vars; plop generators extended.
- [API and state conventions](acad-abl.13): 41 rules: one axios instance with envelope unwrap and request-id capture; an error taxonomy mapping every status to a fixed UX; the inventory's query-key scheme; 60s staleness default; optimism only on notification reads; RHF+zod feature schemas; one MSW handler set with scenario switching.
- [Component primitive gap list](acad-abl.9): Add card, badge, chip, banner, skeleton, empty-state, avatar, confirm-dialog, kpi-card plus Radix-backed tabs, tooltip, popover, combobox, progress; defer the time grid, command palette, accordion, breadcrumb, radio group; PlanStateChip maps the 9-value status onto the 8 token pairs.
- [Design workflow bindings](acad-abl.10): design.md stays the single truth; ui-ux-pro-max stays advisory with --persist banned; impeccable PRODUCT.md at kickoff and DESIGN.md after the first screens; one surface brief per role group; mockups on the superdesign canvas; mandatory stories with a11y; design-audit batched before UI tickets close.
- [Restore docs/agents workflow files](acad-abl.11): Five files restored into docs/agents/ from the harness templates; AGENTS.md now describes the Advaisor client; grilling-session.md has no template and its AGENTS.md pointer is flagged.
- [Auth and account UX](acad-abl.12): Login redirects per role with a sanitized redirectTo; signup binds the student ID, gates on the university domain, and ends at a check-your-inbox state; the verification link lands on /verify-email/:id/:hash with four states; forgot password ends at a sent confirmation because the contract has no reset screen; 401 redirects to login with a session-ended notice.
- [Contract gaps and contradictions](acad-abl.20): 19 stances: 5 workarounds, 4 handoffs (SPA verification link, a student visit-request list endpoint, registration window dates, plan credit totals), 10 accepted and documented; deep_link ships as an object, not the string the contract claims.
- [Cross-cutting UX system](acad-abl.19): Shared state components (skeletons, EmptyState, ErrorState, PermissionDenied, StaleSisBanner, WindowClosed), a toast policy where 401/403/429/5xx never toast, confirmation only for irreversible actions, one slug-to-route table as the only deep_link consumer, two-density tables, class-flip dark mode with density as a shell property, logical-property RTL, and axe over the six mock scenarios in CI.
- [Student surfaces S1-S6](acad-abl.14): 39 decisions: the builder is a single-scroll document with live server-applied mutations and an honest pre-submit validation panel; S1 is one state-driven PlanCard with no metrics; S2 shows the return reason as a top banner with Seen as the primary confirm; S4 is read-only; the window countdown is cut.
- [AI chat surface](acad-abl.15): 35 decisions: streaming transcript with per-frame anatomy (token append, tool.applied system row, error rows with retry); the submit-arm moment is a two-step confirm then send with no draft artifact; quota 429 disables the composer for the session with no meter in v1.
- [Advisor surfaces A1-A5](acad-abl.16): 32 decisions: the queue is server-ordered oldest first with an is_aging badge; one shared review drawer (approve confirms, return demands the reason inline); the explorer opens the same drawer as the detail destination; office hours are a form-rows editor over naive wall times labeled Africa/Cairo, never converted.
- [Dean and VP surfaces](acad-abl.17): One recharts vertical funnel over the nine counts, KPI cards and the faculty scorecard table stay HTML; the advisor detail and student explorer routes are cut for lack of any backing endpoint; VP drill-down walks one cached payload; export streams governance-{term}.csv.
- [Admin surfaces M1-M5](acad-abl.18): 40 decisions: account actions with one-way-door confirms, CSV import with an honest ImportSummary and row-numbered 422 report, rules limited to text-and-parameters CRUD, staff creation with an admin-set initial password; the structure surface stays removed and M5 system log is accepted-and-deferred (no endpoint).
- [Design.md correction pass from ticket flags](acad-abl.21): 18 edits applied to design.md and the design plan: lifecycle reset to 8 states plus discarded, state-confirmed tokens dropped, DraftPlanCard replaced by the submit-suggestion flow, X1 routes completed, dean detail rows and admin structure/system-log surfaces cut, aging copy keyed to is_aging; nothing rejected.

## Not yet specified

The frontier is resolved. The items below decide during the spec effort, without owner questions, from sources already on record: spec document structure and how implementation tickets get cut (the to-spec effort decides; every decision it needs sits in the closed tickets); E2E verification scope (derives from product foundation section 16: J1 happy loop, J2 return loop, one advisor review); performance and bundle-split budget per role shell (inputs: the skeleton, charting, and conventions resolutions); Arabic string inventory and translation workflow (mechanics settled by the i18n resolution; strings are spec and implementation work); Storybook story inventory (per-component stories are mandatory per the design workflow bindings; the enumerated list is build work).

## Out of scope

- Writing the frontend spec. It is a follow-up effort (the owner plans it after this map; the to-spec skill fits).
- Building any part of the client. Implementation tickets come after the spec.
- Reopening backend settled decisions or changing the API contract. Delivering the four contract handoffs recorded in "Contract gaps and contradictions" (SPA verification link, student visit-request list, registration window dates, plan credit totals) belongs to the backend effort.
- Redoing design tokens or visual direction. Deviations amend design.md, not this map.
notes: Owner approvals (2026-10-02): installs approved for recharts, openapi-typescript, openapi-msw, @storybook/addon-a11y, and Fontsource Inter and Cairo (to land when the spec's implementation begins); the new base folder src/components/domain/ is approved; the DS-G-02 proposal for a dedicated discarded token pair is approved to draft during the spec effort (interim mapping stays state-closed with a slate dot). Handoffs live at docs/backend-contract-handoffs.md.
close_reason: Destination reached: every client decision is settled across 20 resolved tickets; the spec effort can start without asking another question

notes:
# Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions

Resolution for acad-abl.1. Sources: backend wayfinder map acad-9s3 and children acad-9s3.1 to acad-9s3.18 (resolutions in ticket notes), the API contract `/home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json`, backend message catalogs `lang/en/*.php`, the role-permission seed migration `database/migrations/2026_10_01_500003_seed_roles_permissions_and_migrate_users.php`, product docs `docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md`, `02-PROJECT-PLAN.md`, `03-DESIGN-PLAN.md`, and the glossary in the backend `CONTEXT.md` (the frontend copy is a placeholder). Ticket IDs in parentheses point at backend wayfinder children.

Precedence used throughout: settled backend decisions beat the product docs where they amended them (acad-9s3.3, acad-9s3.5, acad-9s3.13, acad-9s3.15 all say so explicitly).

## 1. Plan lifecycle: 8 states

The settled count is 8 states (acad-9s3.3): Draft, Submitted, Under Review, Returned, Approved and Locked, Closed, Expired, Withdrawn. The product doc's Registration Confirmed and Verification Failed states died: the platform never registers anyone and never verifies registration (map settled decisions and acad-9s3.3 rationale). Advisor approval is the final human stage and locks the plan permanently. `03-DESIGN-PLAN.md` still sizes `PlanStateChip` for 9 states with a teal Confirmed color; acad-9s3.3 flags it stale and assigns the correction to the frontend effort.

The contract's `PlanStatus` enum carries a ninth value, `discarded`, and the governance funnel counts it (openapi.json PlanStatus, GovernanceFunnel; POST /api/plan/discard with 409 `plan.not_discardable` outside draft or returned). Decision 10 treats discard as an operation on a draft or returned plan, not a lifecycle stage, so the UI renders 8 chip states and may treat `discarded` as a terminal record state the chip layer must still accept. Treat the chip as 8 semantic states plus a discarded terminal state from the API.

Transitions and the role that triggers each:

| Transition | Role | Guard | Contract surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| Create Draft | Student | Advisor assigned (else 409 `plan.advisor_missing`); one active plan (else 409 `plan.already_active`); term available (else 503 `plan.term_unavailable`) | POST /api/plan (acad-9s3.3, decision 3) |
| Draft to Submitted | Student | Window open (else 422 `window`); fresh SIS pull (503 `plan.sis_unavailable` on failure); three checks pass (422, see section 2) | POST /api/plan/submit |
| Submitted to Under Review | Advisor | Assigned advisor opens it (else 409 `plan.not_openable`) | GET /api/advisor/plans/{plan} |
| Under Review to Returned | Advisor | Mandatory reason (ReturnPlanInput requires reason, max 2000); plan locks | POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/return |
| Returned to Draft | Student | Presses Seen | POST /api/plan/seen (else 409 `plan.not_returned`) |
| Under Review to Approved | Advisor | Server revalidation runs all three checks again; permanent lock | POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/approve |
| Draft to Withdrawn | Student | Terminal for the term | POST /api/plan/withdraw |
| Draft or Returned to Discarded | Student | New plan may then be created | POST /api/plan/discard |
| Submitted, Under Review, Returned to Expired | System | registration_closes_at passes | No endpoint; automated, actor system in audit |
| Approved to Closed | System | Window close | No endpoint; automated |

Additional rules the UI must hold (acad-9s3.3, acad-9s3.12, decision 11): the advisor never edits a plan; comments are advisor-posted, the student reads them (GET /api/plan/comments, POST lives only under /api/advisor); visit requests never change plan state; building and editing a draft is never window-gated, only submission is.

## 2. Validation in client-observable terms

The product doc's V1 to V6 rule set is stale. The settled model (acad-9s3.5, decision 17) is three deterministic server-side checks at submission and again at approval; the SIS owns every parameter and the platform stores none. `02-PROJECT-PLAN.md` still describes a PHP port of V1-V6; acad-9s3.5 discarded that. What the UI must show per legacy rule:

| Legacy rule | Settled successor | UI obligation |
|---|---|---|
| V1 credit window 12-18 | Allowance check against the SIS per-student, per-term-kind min and max | 422 key `allowance` with plan.allowance_outside rendering the actual total and min-max, or plan.allowance_missing when the SIS sent no allowance; fail closed, no local defaults |
| V2 probation cap | Gone as a platform rule: the SIS applies probation before sending the allowance | Never compute or label probation; the allowance failure message is the only surface; goal copy keys off SIS state, never a local threshold |
| V3 prerequisites | Prerequisite-chain check; prerequisites resolve in passed history (grade not F) or same-plan lines; same-plan chains allowed | 422 key `prerequisite_chain` with plan.prerequisite_unmet per course or plan.prerequisite_unknown when catalog data is missing |
| V4 repeat policy | Lives inside the SIS course map: a course beyond repeat allowance is not offered | Never count attempts; the builder offers only map courses, so the UI needs no repeat rule |
| V5 summer cap | Same allowance check, keyed by term kind; missing summer allowance blocks summer plans | Show the allowance failure message; no local 6-credit constant |
| V6 shared core | Catalog composition SIS-side | Nothing to surface; no block exists |

Every check failure blocks at both gates. Validation emits no warnings; plan warnings stay advisory. Output names the check and why in the student's language with a stable key and never labels the student (acad-9s3.5). The map-membership check also fires at mutation time on add and update as an input guard: 422 key `course_code` with plan.out_of_map, distinct from the submission check with key `map_membership` (decision 19, acad-9s3.18). The 422 envelope is `{message, errors: {key: [messages]}}` (openapi.json ValidationError); observed keys on submit and approve are `allowance`, `map_membership`, `prerequisite_chain`, and `window` (PlanSubmissionService).

## 3. Permission matrix

From the seed migration (authoritative) plus product doc section 8 as amended by acad-9s3.13 and acad-9s3.15:

| Capability | Student | Advisor | Dean | VP | Admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Create, edit, submit, seen, withdraw, discard own plan | Yes (state-gated) | No, never edits | No | No | No |
| AI chat conversations | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| Own academic record | Yes | No (reads student context via caseload) | No | No | No |
| See advisor availability | Yes, via advisor profile | Publishes it (max 5 day/from/to rows, defaults pre-offered) | No | No | No |
| Raise visit request | Yes (no slots) | Yes (slots from the start) | No | No | No |
| Provide slots, mark visit Done | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| Delete visit request | Initiator only, while Proposed | Initiator only, while Proposed | No | No | No |
| Approve or deny visits | Gone; the model is Proposed to Done with no approval (acad-9s3.13) | No | No | No | No |
| Queue, review caseload plans, comments | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| Governance dashboard and export | No | No | Yes, faculty-scoped | Yes, university-wide | No |
| Student explorer, plans, profiles for dean | No | No | Gone; the dean reads aggregates only, no explorer (acad-9s3.15 corrected the design plan's D3 explorer) | No | No |
| Accounts, staff, assignments, rules text, aging threshold, system log | No | No | No | No | Yes |

Backend enforcement the client can rely on: student holds view-academic-record, view-advisor, manage-plan, create-plan, create-plan-conversation, create-visit-request; advisor holds view-caseload, manage-availability, review-plans, advise-visit-requests; dean and VP share view-governance with server-side faculty scoping; admin holds manage-students, manage-assignments, manage-staff, manage-rules, manage-settings. Gates add ownership: review requires the plan's student to be assigned to the advisor, advise requires the visit's student to be assigned, and conversation view requires ownership (AppServiceProvider gates). AI chat is student-only. Advisor explorer row fields: name, student ID, SIS email, faculty, school, department (empty when unchosen), curriculum year level, plan state, submitted date, aging flag, unmet-meeting flag, CGPA; no risk columns (acad-9s3.15, openapi AdvisorCaseloadStudent).

## 4. Notification slugs

In-app only, deep-linked, rendered in the recipient's language, read via POST read and read-all (decision 8, acad-9s3.14). The contract enum has 9 slugs (openapi.json NotificationSlug; titles and bodies in lang/en/notifications.php):

| Slug | Meaning | Recipient |
|---|---|---|
| plan_returned | Advisor returned the plan; body points at Seen | Student |
| plan_approved | Advisor approved the plan; register in the SIS | Student |
| advisor_changed | Advisor reassignment; part of the student, old advisor, new advisor set (decision 18) | Student |
| caseload_student_added | A student joined the caseload on reassignment | New advisor |
| caseload_student_removed | A student left the caseload on reassignment | Old advisor |
| window_opened | Fires once per term on first observation of the open window; skips students with an approved plan (acad-9s3.4) | Active students |
| window_deadline_nearing | 48-hour config constant before close; once per student per term; skips students with an approved plan (acad-9s3.4) | Affected students |
| visit_requested | A visit request was raised | Receiving party |
| visit_slots_provided | Advisor provided proposed times on a student-initiated request (acad-9s3.13) | Student |

Dead triggers: visit approved, visit denied, and reassignment cancellation died with the Proposed-to-Done model (acad-9s3.13); registration verified or failed died with verification (acad-9s3.3). Queue aging fires no notification: the product doc's dashboard badge line holds, the map baseline sentence listing it as a trigger is the outlier, and the contract exposes it as is_aging flags on queue and caseload rows instead.

## 5. 422 error slugs

The contract envelope is `{message, errors: {key: [messages]}}`. The contract text does not enumerate the keys; the backend catalog is the registry (lang/en/plan.php, auth.php, admin.php, advisor.php, visit.php, governance.php, PlanSubmissionService, PlanService):

Constraint slugs on the submission and approval gates:

- `allowance`: plan.allowance_outside or plan.allowance_missing
- `map_membership`: plan.out_of_map per course
- `prerequisite_chain`: plan.prerequisite_unmet or plan.prerequisite_unknown
- `window`: plan.window_closed (only on submit)

Mutation guards on plan courses (422): `course_code` with plan.out_of_map; `reason` with plan.reason_forbidden when a non-AI actor sends a reason.

State and precondition messages are 409, not 422 (conflict-based idempotency, acad-9s3.17): plan.advisor_missing, plan.already_active, plan.not_draft, plan.not_discardable, plan.not_submittable, plan.not_openable, plan.not_reviewable, plan.not_returned, plan.not_commentable, visit.already_proposed, visit.not_deletable, visit.not_completable, visit.not_slotable. Service errors are 503: plan.sis_unavailable, plan.window_unavailable, plan.term_unavailable, visit.term_unavailable. The chat quota is 429 with key advisor.quota_exhausted.

## 6. SSE frames for AI conversation turns

Transport is synchronous inside the SSE request: no queue, no replay, no Last-Event-ID; a disconnect fails the turn and applied tool effects persist; conversation history is the recovery surface (decision 20, acad-9s3.11). Frames are `event: <type>` plus a JSON data line; every data carries turn_id and seq, with seq incrementing across all frames of a turn.

On POST /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}/turns (openapi.json description):

- `token`: {turn_id, seq, token}. Concatenate token values in seq order to rebuild the assistant message. Alignment Phase questions are ordinary tokens.
- `tool.applied`: {turn_id, seq, tool, payload}. A plan mutation landed; the client refreshes the plan after each batch (acad-9s3.10).
- `submit.suggested`: {turn_id, seq}. The model asked to submit while the conversation is not armed.
- `submit.result`: {turn_id, seq, status: submitted, plan_id} or {status: blocked, errors: {allowance: [message]}}. Only for an armed conversation.
- `turn.completed`: {turn_id, seq, title}. Terminal success; title is null when the conversation keeps its title.
- `error`: {turn_id, seq, code, retryable, key, message}. Terminal failure; code is turn_failed or turn_timeout; keys advisor.turn_failed, advisor.turn_timeout.

The seventh settled event, `submit.armed`, streams on its own endpoint, POST /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}/submit-arm: one frame {conversation_id, submission_confirmed_at}, then the stream ends. Arming is a persisted flag on the conversation (submission_confirmed_at in the PlanConversation schema); the submit tool checks it server-side and the flag clears on use or when plan state changes (acad-9s3.11). Goal Suggestions are static localized strings in the single-conversation response while it has zero user messages (GoalSuggestions schema; acad-9s3.11 amends decision 16: no CGPA interpolation server-side). The quota gate returns JSON 429 instead of streaming.

## 7. SIS staleness and registration window

Staleness (acad-9s3.9): every stored dataset carries a TTL (record 24h, catalog 7d, analytics 7d, offerings 2h in window, window dates 7d). Stale is a display state that never blocks: show the data-as-of banner in the viewer's language. The client reads staleness from GET /api/academic-record, which carries last_synced_at plus a staleness object of three booleans: identity, academic_record, course_catalog (openapi Staleness). A failed pull before validation blocks with 503 as a service error, never a validation failure.

Registration window (acad-9s3.4): university-wide, one window per term, SIS-owned, no platform override. A fresh pull precedes the submit gate, so a same-day SIS-side extension applies immediately. Missing window data blocks submission (503 plan.window_unavailable) but never expires or closes plans; lifecycle transitions happen only when the actual registration_closes_at passes. Deadline notification fires at 48 hours before close; window-open notification fires once per term on first observation. A plan binds to the SIS current term (term_code on the Plan schema). Building is never window-gated; only submission is.

Contract gap: the client API exposes no window dates at all. There is no /terms/current route and no opens_at or closes_at field anywhere in openapi.json, so the product doc's dashboard window countdown and a client-side window-closed banner cannot be rendered from data; the UI can only react to the submit 422 window key, the 503s, and the two window notification slugs.

## 8. Quota limits

One usage limit exists (decision 20, acad-9s3.11): a per-term quota of 100 turns per student, a config constant, not audited, no Admin UI. When exhausted, POST turns returns JSON 429 instead of streaming, with QuotaExceededError {message (localized advisor.quota_exhausted text), key: "advisor.quota_exhausted"}. Retry means the client resends the message as a new turn. The turn timeout is 120 seconds and is retryable; tool-argument failures retry in turn, capped at 2, and are not turn failures. No hourly rate limit exists in v1.

## 9. Contradictions to flag

1. State count: product doc section 7 and the design plan carry a 9-to-11-state machine with Confirmed and Verification Failed; the settled machine is 8 states (acad-9s3.3). The design plan's 9-state chip and teal Confirmed color are stale and the frontend effort must correct them.
2. The contract PlanStatus enum carries a ninth value `discarded` beyond the settled 8, and the governance funnel counts it. Discard is an operation on a draft or returned plan (decision 10), so treat it as a terminal record state, not a lifecycle stage.
3. Validation rules: product doc V1-V6 and the project plan's rules-engine port are superseded by three SIS-parameterized checks (acad-9s3.5). No platform rule numbers exist; the client keys UI off the four 422 keys only.
4. Dean surfaces: the design plan's D3 student explorer and the product doc's dean plan and profile visibility are dead; the dean reads faculty-scoped aggregates only (acad-9s3.15).
5. Visits: the design plan's VisitRequestCard approve and deny flows and the product doc's visit approved and denied notifications are dead; the model is Proposed to Done (acad-9s3.13).
6. Notifications: the map baseline lists queue aging as a notification trigger, but the contract has no slug for it; the product doc's badge line holds. Registration verified or failed notifications are dead with verification.
7. SSE event set: the settled decision lists submit.armed in the turns stream; the contract streams it from the separate submit-arm endpoint instead. The contract also names the error localization field `key` where the decision wrote `message_key`.
8. Window data: the product doc promises a dashboard window countdown and window-closed banner states; the contract exposes no window dates, so those states cannot be data-driven today.
9. Credit totals: decision 19 says total credit hours render as the sum of planned courses' catalog credits, but the contract returns total_credit_hours as "always 0 for now" and exposes no catalog endpoint to the client, so the client cannot compute the sum itself today.
10. Reason rejection status: the contract says a student-sent reason is "rejected with 409", while the implementation throws a 422 with key `reason` (PlanService.assertReasonAllowed).
close_reason: Digest recorded: 8 plan states with role-triggered transitions, 3 validation checks replacing stale V1-V6, role permission matrix from the seed migration, 9 notification slugs, 422 slug registry, 6 SSE turn frames plus submit.armed on its own endpoint, staleness and window semantics, 100-turn quota with QuotaExceededError; 10 contradictions flagged

title: Client API inventory from the OpenAPI contract
description:
## Question

What is the full client-side inventory of the API: one row per operation with hook name, query or mutation, query key, invalidations, unwrapping, and error cases?

## Context

- Contract: `../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json` (58 operations, 9 tags: Auth, Profile, Notifications, Plan, Plan Conversations, Advisor, Visit Requests, Governance, Admin; `data` envelope; pagination meta with 10/20/50/All; bearer Sanctum; SSE for plan-conversation turns).
- Stack: TanStack Query 5, axios, MSW 2 (see `package.json`).

## Record

A table in the resolution notes: method + path, proposed hook name (`use-get-plan` style), query or mutation, query key, which mutations invalidate which keys, envelope/pagination unwrap notes, and error responses per operation (422 slugs, 401, 403, 409, 503).

Flag contract gaps a spec must resolve: no token refresh endpoint, GET `verify-email/{id}/{hash}` semantics inside an SPA, and any missing client need (for example no endpoint listing students for a student-facing view).
notes:
# Client API inventory from the OpenAPI contract (acad-abl.2)

Source of truth: `/home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json` (Academic Advisor API 1.0.0, OpenAPI 3.0.3). Read on 2026-10-01.

Count note: the ticket says 58 operations. The contract defines **61** operations. Count by tag: Auth 7, Profile 2, Notifications 3, Plan 10, Plan Conversations 5, Advisor 13, Visit Requests 2, Governance 2, Admin 17. Total 61. Every operation appears below.

## Conventions (verified against the contract and package.json)

- Stack: TanStack Query 5.103, axios 1.20, MSW 2.15, zod 4, react-hook-form 7, zustand 5 (`/home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-frontend/package.json`). The repo follows bulletproof-react: one file per operation under `src/features/<feature>/api/`, a fetcher function, a `queryOptions` helper, and a hook. Hook names below follow the requested `use-get-plan` style (`useGetPlan`, file `use-get-plan.ts`).
- Auth: Sanctum bearer token from `POST /api/login` (`TokenResponse.token`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Token expires after 30 days. Login, resend, and registration resend are throttled (429).
- Envelope: every resource response is `{ data: <T> }`. Unwrap in the fetcher so hooks see `T` directly (axios: `res.data.data`).
- Paginated lists: `{ data: [...], links, meta }` with Laravel-style `meta.current_page`, `meta.per_page`, `meta.total`, `links.next`. The `per_page` query param accepts `"10" | "20" | "50" | "all"`, default `"10"`. Only three lists paginate: notifications (plus a required `unread_count`), advisor caseload, admin students. Five lists are plain arrays: plan comments, plan conversations, advisor queue, visit requests, university rules.
- Errors: 422 is `{ message, errors: Record<field, string[]> }`; 401/403/404/409/503 are `{ message }`. The only named error keys in the contract: `advisor.quota_exhausted` (429 body on turns) and SSE frame keys `advisor.turn_failed` and `advisor.turn_timeout`. Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header; log it for support.
- SSE: both AI endpoints return `text/event-stream` with `event: <type>\ndata: <json>\n\n` frames. An axios call cannot consume these; use fetch plus a ReadableStream reader (EventSource cannot POST). Check `Content-Type` before streaming: the turns endpoint returns JSON 429 instead of a stream when the per-term quota is gone.
- Global 401 policy: no refresh endpoint exists (see gaps). The axios interceptor clears auth state and routes to login on 401.

## Query key design

Root key per entity, detail keys nested under the list root, request params as the second array element:

- `['me']`
- `['academic-record']`
- `['advisor-profile']`
- `['notifications', { perPage }]`
- `['plan']`, `['plan', 'comments']`
- `['plan-conversations', { ... }]`, `['plan-conversations', conversationId]`
- `['advisor', 'availability']`, `['advisor', 'caseload', { search, perPage }]`, `['advisor', 'queue']`, `['advisor', 'plans', planId]`, `['advisor', 'plans', planId, 'comments']`, `['advisor', 'visit-requests']`
- `['visit-requests']` (student side; no list endpoint, key exists for invalidation)
- `['governance']`
- `['admin', 'students', { search, perPage }]`, `['admin', 'rules']`, `['admin', 'rules', ruleId]`, `['admin', 'settings', 'queue-aging-threshold']`

Mutations invalidate at the root of every entity they touch. Scoped invalidation only where a detail cache exists.

## Auth (7 operations)

| Method + path | Hook | Type | Query key | Invalidates | Unwrap | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST /api/register | `useRegister` | mutation | none | none (bootstraps token flow) | `UserEnvelope` to `User` | 422 name, email (SIS domain), password, language_preference |
| POST /api/login | `useLogin` | mutation | none | `['me']` on success | `TokenResponse` to `token` (store, set bearer) | 422 email, password; 429 throttle `{message}` |
| GET /api/verify-email/{id}/{hash} | `useVerifyEmail({id, hash})` | query (run once from the email-link route, `enabled` on params) | `['verify-email', id, hash]` | `['me']` | `UserEnvelope` to `User` | 403 invalid signature or hash mismatch; 503 SIS down. No 401: the signed link is unauthenticated |
| POST /api/forgot-password | `useForgotPassword` | mutation | none | none | `MessageResponse` to `message` | 422 email |
| POST /api/email/verification-notification | `useResendVerification` | mutation | none | none | `MessageResponse` to `message` | 401; 409 already verified; 429 throttle |
| POST /api/logout | `useLogout` | mutation | none | `queryClient.clear()` | 204, no body | 401 |
| GET /api/me | `useGetMe` | query | `['me']` | none | `UserEnvelope` to `User` | 401 |

## Profile (2 operations)

| Method + path | Hook | Type | Query key | Invalidates | Unwrap | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/academic-record | `useGetAcademicRecord` | query | `['academic-record']` | none | `AcademicRecordEnvelope` to `AcademicRecord` (check `staleness.identity`, `staleness.academic_record`, `staleness.course_catalog`) | 401; 403 (student role) |
| GET /api/advisor/profile | `useGetAdvisorProfile` | query | `['advisor-profile']` | none | `AdvisorProfileEnvelope` to `AdvisorProfile` | 401; 403; 404 no advisor assigned |

## Notifications (3 operations)

| Method + path | Hook | Type | Query key | Invalidates | Unwrap | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/notifications | `useGetNotifications` | query (paginated) | `['notifications', { perPage }]` | none | `NotificationList`: `data[]` plus required `unread_count`, optional `links`/`meta` | 401 |
| POST /api/notifications/read-all | `useReadAllNotifications` | mutation | none | `['notifications']` | 204, no body; patch cache or refetch | 401 |
| POST /api/notifications/{notification}/read | `useReadNotification` | mutation | none | `['notifications']` | 204, no body | 401; 404 not owned by caller. `notification` is a uuid |

Notification `slug` enum for icon and deep-link routing: `plan_returned`, `plan_approved`, `advisor_changed`, `caseload_student_removed`, `caseload_student_added`, `window_opened`, `window_deadline_nearing`, `visit_requested`, `visit_slots_provided`.

## Plan (10 operations)

All plan mutations return the full plan, so a mutation can also `setQueryData(['plan'], ...)` from the response.

| Method + path | Hook | Type | Query key | Invalidates | Unwrap | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/plan | `useGetPlan` | query | `['plan']` | none | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` (`status` enum: draft, submitted, under_review, returned, approved, expired, closed, withdrawn, discarded) | 401; 403 |
| POST /api/plan | `useCreatePlan` | mutation | none | `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` (201) | 401; 403; 409 no advisor assigned or active plan exists; 503 term unavailable |
| POST /api/plan/courses | `useAddPlanCourse` | mutation | none | `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` (201) | 401; 403; 409 plan not draft, course outside map, or `reason` sent by a student; 422 course_code, group, section |
| PATCH /api/plan/courses/{courseCode} | `useUpdatePlanCourse` | mutation | none | `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 409 not draft or course not in plan; 422 group, section |
| DELETE /api/plan/courses/{courseCode} | `useRemovePlanCourse` | mutation | none | `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` (200, updated plan returned, not 204) | 401; 403; 409 not draft |
| POST /api/plan/submit | `useSubmitPlan` | mutation | none | `['plan']`, `['advisor', 'queue']`, `['academic-record']` (SIS recheck may refresh it) | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 422 credit allowance or prerequisite gates (`errors` map); 503 SIS or registration window down. Only inside the registration window |
| POST /api/plan/seen | `useMarkPlanSeen` | mutation | none | `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 409 plan not in returned state |
| GET /api/plan/comments | `useGetPlanComments` | query | `['plan', 'comments']` | none | `PlanCommentList` to `PlanComment[]` (no pagination) | 401; 403; 404 student holds no plan |
| POST /api/plan/withdraw | `useWithdrawPlan` | mutation | none | `['plan']`, `['advisor', 'queue']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 409 state disallows withdrawal |
| POST /api/plan/discard | `useDiscardPlan` | mutation | none | `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 409 only draft or returned plans |

## Plan Conversations (5 operations)

Turns are SSE, not a plain axios mutation. Build `useSendConversationTurn` on fetch plus a ReadableStream reader; reduce frames into local turn state, then invalidate on terminal frames. Frame contract: `seq` increments across the turn, `turn_id` is constant; frames are `token`, `tool.applied`, `submit.suggested`, `submit.result`, `turn.completed` (terminal success), `error` (terminal failure, codes `turn_failed` or `turn_timeout`, key `advisor.turn_failed`).

| Method + path | Hook | Type | Query key | Invalidates | Unwrap | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/plan-conversations | `useGetPlanConversations` | query | `['plan-conversations']` | none | `PlanConversationList` to `PlanConversation[]`, newest first, no messages inside | 401 |
| POST /api/plan-conversations | `useCreatePlanConversation` | mutation | none | `['plan-conversations']` | `PlanConversationEnvelope` to `PlanConversation` (201) | 401; 403; 422 goal |
| GET /api/plan-conversations/{conversation} | `useGetPlanConversation` | query | `['plan-conversations', conversationId]` | none | `PlanConversationEnvelope` to `PlanConversation` (with `messages`; `goal_suggestions` present until the first user message) | 401; 403; 404 |
| POST /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}/submit-arm | `useArmPlanSubmission` | mutation (reads one SSE frame) | none | `['plan-conversations', conversationId]` | stream frame `submit.armed` `{conversation_id, submission_confirmed_at}`; `submission_confirmed_at` is null until the flag lands | 401; 403; 404 |
| POST /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}/turns | `useSendConversationTurn` | mutation over SSE stream (custom hook, not useMutation) | none | `['plan']` on every `tool.applied` frame; `['plan-conversations', conversationId]` and `['plan-conversations']` on `turn.completed` or `error` | frame stream; concatenate `token` by `seq` for the assistant text; `submit.result` carries submitted plan_id or blocked `errors` | 401; 403; 404; 422 message (max 10000); 429 quota, body `QuotaExceededError` with key `advisor.quota_exhausted`, JSON instead of a stream |

## Advisor (13 operations)

| Method + path | Hook | Type | Query key | Invalidates | Unwrap | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/advisor/availability | `useGetAvailabilityWindow` | query | `['advisor', 'availability']` | none | `AvailabilityWindowEnvelope` to `AvailabilityWindow` (`is_default` true when nothing published; five default rows) | 401; 403 |
| PUT /api/advisor/availability | `useUpdateAvailabilityWindow` | mutation | none | `['advisor', 'availability']`, `['advisor-profile']` (profile embeds the window) | `AvailabilityWindowEnvelope` to `AvailabilityWindow` | 401; 403; 422 rows |
| GET /api/advisor/caseload | `useGetAdvisorCaseload` | query (paginated) | `['advisor', 'caseload', { search, perPage }]` | none | `AdvisorCaseloadStudentList`: `data[]` plus `links`/`meta` | 401; 403 |
| GET /api/advisor/queue | `useGetAdvisorQueue` | query | `['advisor', 'queue']` | none | `AdvisorQueueList` to `AdvisorQueueItem[]` (no pagination; `is_aging` per item) | 401; 403 |
| GET /api/advisor/plans/{plan} | `useGetAdvisorPlan` | query | `['advisor', 'plans', planId]` | none (the GET itself moves submitted to under_review; refetch `['advisor', 'queue']` after it resolves) | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 404; 409 only submitted plans can open |
| POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/approve | `useApprovePlan` | mutation | none | `['advisor', 'plans', planId]`, `['advisor', 'queue']`, `['plan']`, `['governance']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` | 401; 403; 404; 409 only submitted or under_review decidable; 422 credit allowance or prerequisite gates; 503 SIS or window down |
| POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/return | `useReturnPlan` | mutation | none | `['advisor', 'plans', planId]`, `['advisor', 'queue']`, `['plan']` | `PlanEnvelope` to `Plan` (reason recorded) | 401; 403; 404; 409 only submitted or under_review; 422 reason (max 2000) |
| GET /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/comments | `useGetAdvisorPlanComments` | query | `['advisor', 'plans', planId, 'comments']` | none | `PlanCommentList` to `PlanComment[]` | 401; 403; 404 |
| POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/comments | `useCreatePlanComment` | mutation | none | `['advisor', 'plans', planId, 'comments']` | `PlanCommentEnvelope` to `PlanComment` (201) | 401; 403; 404; 409 only under_review or returned plans accept comments; 422 body |
| GET /api/advisor/visit-requests | `useGetAdvisorVisitRequests` | query | `['advisor', 'visit-requests']` | none | `VisitRequestList` to `VisitRequest[]`, newest first (no pagination) | 401; 403 |
