## Shared unwrap helpers to build once

- `unwrap<T>()`: `res.data.data` for the 11 envelope types (User, Plan, AcademicRecord, AdvisorProfile, PlanComment, PlanConversation, AvailabilityWindow, VisitRequest, GovernanceNode, UniversityRule, QueueAgingThreshold).
- `unwrapList<T>()`: `res.data.data` for the five plain arrays (PlanComment, PlanConversation, VisitRequest, AdvisorQueue, UniversityRule).
- `unwrapPage<T>()`: `{ items: res.data.data, meta: res.data.meta, links: res.data.links }` for the three paginated lists; notifications also carry `unread_count`.
- SSE reader for the two stream endpoints, with `Content-Type` sniffing to catch the JSON 429 on turns.

## Contract gaps a spec must resolve

1. No token refresh endpoint. The Sanctum token dies after 30 days and 401 has no recovery path except re-login. The spec must either add a refresh or rotation endpoint, or state that long-lived users re-authenticate and the client must never hold partial form state across a 401.
2. `GET /api/verify-email/{id}/{hash}` semantics in an SPA. The endpoint serves a signed email link as JSON. The spec must define where the email link points: an SPA route that extracts `id` and `hash` and calls the API, or the API URL directly (which would render raw JSON in a browser). It must also cover the 403 and 503 screens and the post-verification redirect for an unauthenticated visitor. Note the hash is documented as a SHA-1 of the email.
3. No `page` query parameter. Paginated responses expose `meta.current_page` and `links.next`, and `per_page` accepts 10/20/50/all, but no operation documents a `page` param. A client cannot request page 2 from the contract alone.
4. Students cannot list their own visit requests. `POST /api/visit-requests` and `DELETE /api/visit-requests/{visitRequest}` exist, but no student-facing `GET` list. The UI has no documented way to show an open request or learn the id to delete.
5. No staff list endpoint. Admin can create staff (`POST /api/admin/staff`) and send password resets, but cannot read the staff directory.
6. No profile or preference update. `User.language_preference` is read-only; no `PATCH /api/me` exists. A language switcher surface needs a write endpoint.
7. `Notification.deep_link` is an unformatted string. The spec must fix its shape (SPA route vs API path) or notification routing cannot be built.
8. Governance export filename. The 200 is `text/csv` named after the term per the description, but no `Content-Disposition` header is documented, so the client cannot derive a deterministic filename.
9. Quota visibility. The turns endpoint returns 429 `advisor.quota_exhausted` after the fact, but no endpoint exposes the remaining per-term turn count, so the UI cannot show quota state before failure.

## Sources

- `/home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json` (all paths, responses, schemas, parameters, security schemes; read 2026-10-01)
- `/home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-frontend/package.json` (stack versions)

title: Auth token storage for the SPA
description:
## Question

Where does the client keep the 30-day Sanctum personal access token, and how does it handle 401 and expiry?

## Context

- Contract: `POST /api/login` returns TokenResponse; no refresh endpoint exists.
- DOMPurify is already a dependency; React-query-auth is installed.
- Search the web for current guidance on SPA token storage: OWASP session management cheatsheet, Laravel Sanctum SPA mode vs token mode, localStorage vs httpOnly cookie tradeoffs in 2025/2026.

## Record

A recommendation (localStorage vs httpOnly cookie vs memory) with the tradeoff in one paragraph, the 401/expiry UX consequence, logout behavior, and the XSS posture given DOMPurify and dependency risk. Name the runner-up and the condition under which to switch.
notes:
# acad-abl.3 Resolution: Auth token storage for the SPA

## Decision

Store the 30-day Sanctum personal access token in localStorage on the SPA origin. Attach it as an Authorization: Bearer header on every API call through the axios request interceptor. Handle 401 in one global response interceptor: clear the token, redirect to /auth/login with a redirectTo parameter, and show a session-expired banner on the login screen. Clear the token on logout after a best-effort POST /api/logout.

Tradeoff: localStorage keeps the 30-day session across tabs and restarts with zero backend work. OWASP advises against it because any script on the origin can read and exfiltrate the token, and our contract has no refresh endpoint, so a stolen token stays valid for up to 30 days. An httpOnly cookie would block JavaScript from reading the token, but it needs backend work the current contract does not have: cookie issuance at login, CSRF protection, and SameSite plus CORS credentials for a separate dev origin. Memory-only storage plus a refresh cookie is the strongest pattern in current guidance, and the contract blocks it: POST /api/login returns one 30-day bearer token and there is no refresh endpoint. Given the internal audience, React's default escaping, and DOMPurify on the only raw HTML sink, localStorage is the acceptable risk today, and the switch path is defined below.

## Why not the alternatives

- Memory only. Every tab close or refresh forces a new login. It defeats the 30-day session the contract describes ("The token expires after 30 days").
- httpOnly cookie now. Sanctum's own docs say first-party SPAs should use its cookie session mode, and that mode protects credentials from XSS. But this backend ships token mode only: login returns TokenResponse, and there is no stateful domain list, CSRF cookie route, or session setup for the SPA. Building that is a backend ticket, not a frontend spec.
- sessionStorage. It persists per tab only and fails the same product requirement as memory only.

## Contract shape the spec must encode

The current src/lib/auth.tsx and src/lib/api-client.ts are bulletproof-react boilerplate and do not match the contract.

- POST /api/login returns { token }. Send Authorization: Bearer on every request. auth.tsx currently calls /auth/login and reads an AuthResponse.user; rewire to /api/login and TokenResponse.
- GET /api/me returns the authenticated user. auth.tsx currently calls /auth/me.
- POST /api/logout revokes the current token and returns 204.
- 401 means "Missing, invalid, or expired bearer token" per the contract's Unauthorized response.
- TokenResponse carries no expiry field, so the client cannot know the expiry time. Do not compute a client-side TTL. Treat 401 as the single expiry signal.
- Keep the 401 redirect in api-client.ts and simplify it: redirect to paths.auth.login with redirectTo set to the current pathname plus search. The current code builds an empty URLSearchParams, so redirectTo always falls back to the pathname. The intent is right; the code is not.

## 401 and expiry UX

- One global axios response interceptor owns 401. It clears the stored token, redirects to /auth/login?redirectTo=current-path, and does not toast per request.
- The login screen reads the redirect and shows a calm banner: "Your session ended. Sign in again to continue." design.md DS-W-02 sets the copy pattern: what happened, why, what to do, in one or two sentences. DS-A-09 says nothing important appears only in a toast, so the login banner is the delivery.
- After login, send the user back to the redirectTo target so deep links such as /app/plans/42 survive.
- Separate the failure cases: wrong credentials get inline field errors per design.md section 4.4; an expired session gets the login banner. Never surface a raw 401 or an axios message string.

## Logout

- logoutFn: POST /api/logout, then in a finally block remove the token from localStorage, clear the react-query cache, and navigate to /auth/login.
- If the POST fails (offline, or the token already expired), still clear locally and redirect. Best-effort revocation is acceptable because the token dies at its 30-day expiry anyway.
- Never log the token, and strip the Authorization header from anything sent to error tracking once the Sentry integration lands.

## XSS posture

- React escapes text by default. The only raw HTML sink is src/components/ui/md-preview/md-preview.tsx, and it runs marked output through DOMPurify.sanitize before dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Keep sanitization mandatory for any new sink.
- The residual risk is the dependency supply chain: one compromised npm package with script execution on the origin can read the token. Compensating controls: a strict Content Security Policy, the existing lockfile and lint gates, and server-side revocation on logout.
- The exposure window equals the token lifetime because there is no rotation. That is the main argument to switch when the backend can support it.

## Runner-up and switch condition

Runner-up: Sanctum SPA cookie mode. The backend issues an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax session cookie at login, the SPA and API share one top-level domain (one reverse proxy in dev and prod), and CSRF runs through the /sanctum/csrf-cookie exchange.

Switch when either condition holds: (a) the backend serves the SPA from the same top-level domain and adds cookie issuance with CSRF, or (b) the backend adds a refresh endpoint. Path (a) moves to Sanctum cookie sessions, which the Sanctum docs recommend for first-party SPAs. Path (b) moves to a short-lived access token in memory plus the refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, the prevailing 2025 pattern. Until one lands, localStorage is the decision.

## Sources

- OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html (do not store tokens in web storage; HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies preferred; BFF pattern)
- OWASP HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTML5_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html (XSS reads all of localStorage; prefer sessionStorage when persistence is not needed)
- Laravel Sanctum docs: https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/sanctum (token mode vs SPA cookie mode; "You should not use API tokens to authenticate your own first-party SPA"; revocation; expiration config)
- angular.love, JWT storage overview: https://angular.love/localstorage-vs-cookies-all-you-need-to-know-about-storing-jwt-tokens-securely-in-the-front-end
- Academind, XSS and storage: https://academind.com/articles/localstorage-vs-cookies-xss (HttpOnly stops exfiltration, not authenticated requests made by the injected script)
- OpenReplay, cookies vs localStorage: https://blog.openreplay.com/cookies-vs-localstorage-jwt-auth
- Local contract: /home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json (POST /api/login, GET /api/me, POST /api/logout, 401 description)
close_reason: Recommend localStorage for the 30-day Sanctum bearer token with global 401 redirect to login; switch to Sanctum SPA cookie mode once the backend shares a top-level domain or adds refresh

## What to build

On the admin Assignments page the admin can assign an advisor by typing the student's SIS student ID and picking the advisor from a picker — this works for students who registered (direct assignment) and for students who never registered (scheduled, applied automatically when they register). A pending-assignments section lists everything scheduled, with the chosen advisor and creation date, and each entry can be cancelled. The CSV import summary reports scheduled rows alongside assigned/unchanged.

## Contract (pinned — the mock layer and calls must match exactly)

title: Admin Accounts page: add + edit student dialogs
description:
# Admin Accounts page: add + edit student dialogs

## What to build

From the admin Accounts (students) page the admin can add a student by entering the student's SIS ID, a display name, and a temporary password — the success state surfaces the created account so the admin can hand over the credentials. From the account panel the admin can also edit the account's name and language preference. Server validation errors land on the form fields; a confirmation toast fires on success; the table updates from the query cache without a refetch flicker. SIS-owned fields (email, faculty, binding status) stay read-only in the UI.

## Contract (pinned — the mock layer and calls must match exactly)

- `POST /admin/students` `{student_id, name, password, language_preference?}` → 201 `{data: User}`; 422 field errors (`errors` map); 422 with `admin.sis_unknown_student` key when SIS has no such student; 503 `verification.sis_unavailable` on SIS outage.
- `GET /admin/students/{id}` → `{data: User}`.
- `PATCH /admin/students/{id}` `{name?, language_preference?}` → 200 `{data: User}`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add-student dialog (student_id, name, temp password, optional language preference) creates the account and prepends the row to the cached students list; the success state shows the created account.
- [ ] SIS-unknown (422) and SIS-unavailable (503) responses render distinct, understandable error states in the dialog.
- [ ] Edit-account dialog from the account panel updates name/language preference and patches the cache; SIS-owned fields display read-only.
- [ ] One api module per endpoint following the existing query-key/options pattern, with cache helpers for create/update.
- [ ] MSW handlers + mock db cover the new endpoints, including 422/503 paths.
- [ ] Every new string exists in both en and ar dictionaries (parity test green); RTL-safe markup (logical properties, bidi isolation for IDs).
- [ ] Route/component tests updated or added; `npm run verify` passes.

description: The review-drawer (src/components/domain/review-drawer/review-drawer.tsx) and plan-state-actions (src/features/plan/components/plan-state-actions.tsx) each define a private controlled ConfirmDialog (focus cancel, verb label, destructive variant). Sketch A: controlled-only ConfirmDialog (open, onCancel, onConfirm, title, body, confirmLabel, destructive?, pending?); cancel label resolved from i18n inside the module; trigger sites own one boolean. Trade-off: B leaves trigger call sites untouched, but its ReactElement slots push pending, destructive, and i18n decisions to every call site, which is what produced the two private copies; isDone also forces consumers to track mutation success just to close. Opening a submitted plan moves it under review and refetches the queue. Mock handlers: queue list, plan get, approve, return, comments; 422 approve-gate failures and the 503 SIS banner render next to the actions.

Cites: Advisor surfaces D4 to D18, Error taxonomy conventions 12, 17.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Queue renders oldest first with no sort control; Aging badge appears only from is_aging; waiting days use dayjs diff and tabular-nums.
- [ ] Row activation opens the drawer, sets aria-current, refetches the queue, and the chip reads Under review.
- [ ] Approve confirm focuses cancel, locks on success, closes the drawer, invalidates queue and caseload roots, and toasts nothing.
- [ ] Return demands a non-empty reason (client zod + server 422 merge), survives ESC with a discard confirm when text stands, and closes clean when empty.
- [ ] Approve 422 messages render as a destructive list above the footer; Return stays available; 503 plan.sis_unavailable renders the retry banner.
- [ ] Empty queue, error, and permission states render through the shared state components.

## Blocked by

- Role section scaffolds.

title: Spec: Advaisor React client v1
description:
## Problem Statement

E-JUST students, advisors, deans, the VP, and admins have no client for the Advaisor platform. The backend contract is settled and mocked decisions are recorded, but the repo still runs the bulletproof-react demo (teams, discussions, comments), so nobody can sign in, build a plan, get AI help, review a queue, or read governance aggregates.

## Solution

Build the Advaisor React client v1 in this repo: demolish the demo, keep the scaffold foundations, and implement every surface the wayfinder map settled. Five role sections (student, advisor, dean, VP, admin) behind role-guarded routes, the X1 auth flows, the plan lifecycle surfaces with the AI advisor chat streaming over SSE, advisor review and meeting tools, read-only governance dashboards, and the admin console. All data flows through the contract-typed MSW mock so the app runs end to end before the backend is reachable. Copy is final in EN and AR with RTL mirroring; light and dark themes ride the token flip.

## User Stories

### Auth and account (X1)

1. As a student, I want to sign up with my university email, student ID, password, and language preference, so that my account binds to my SIS record.
2. As a student, I want a check-your-inbox state after signup, so that I know verification is pending and how to get a new link.
3. As a student, I want the email verification link to land on a working app screen, so that I see a clear verified, held, invalid, or retrying state instead of raw JSON.
4. As any user, I want to sign in with email and password, so that I reach my role's home screen.
5. As any user, I want wrong-credential and throttled attempts to show inline field errors, so that I know exactly what to fix.
6. As any user who was signed out, I want a calm session-ended banner on the login screen and a return to the page I came from, so that deep links survive expiry.
7. As any user, I want a forgot-password flow that ends at an honest sent-confirmation, so that I know where the reset link goes.
8. As a staff member, I want no signup path, so that I understand staff accounts come from the admin.
9. As any user, I want to sign out from the account menu, so that my session ends on this device.

### Shell and cross-cutting

10. As any user, I want a role-scoped navigation rail and topbar, so that I only see what my role can do.
11. As any user, I want direct URL hits on another role's section to show a calm permission panel with a way back, so that I am never lost.
12. As any user, I want light and dark themes that persist per device, so that the app renders comfortably in my environment.
13. As any user, I want an EN/AR language toggle that flips direction immediately and persists, so that I can work in my language.
14. As any user, I want every list and page to show skeleton loading, empty, and error states with retry, so that the app never looks broken while it works.
15. As any user, I want destructive actions to confirm with a dialog that states the consequence, so that I never lose data by accident.
16. As any user, I want servers' request ids surfaced on destructive errors, so that support can trace my failed request.

### Notifications (S6, A5, D4)

17. As any user, I want a notification center fed by in-app notifications only, so that plan, window, and visit updates reach me.
18. As any user, I want an unread badge on the topbar bell that polls while the tab is visible, so that I notice new items without reloading.
19. As any user, I want opening a notification to mark it read and route me to the relevant screen for my role, so that I act in one click.
20. As any user, I want a mark-all-as-read action, so that I can clear the list at once.

### Student plan surfaces (S1-S4)

21. As a student, I want a dashboard whose plan card shows my term, plan state, course count, and the one action my state calls for, so that I always know the next step.
22. As a student with no plan, I want a dashboard empty state that starts the builder flow, so that creating a plan is obvious.
23. As a student with no assigned advisor, I want a calm blocking banner instead of a broken builder, so that I know the administration assigns advisors.
24. As a student, I want My Plan to show the plan document, its state chip, and advisor comments, so that I can read where my plan stands.
25. As a student whose plan was returned, I want the return reason as a top banner, comments visible immediately, and Seen as the primary action, so that feedback is never hidden behind a click.
26. As a student, I want to submit, withdraw, or discard my plan from My Plan with the right confirmations, so that state changes are deliberate.
27. As a student, I want submit failures to list the server's constraint messages per course line with a summary panel, so that I can fix exactly what failed.
28. As a student, I want the Plan Builder as a single scrolling document with a course combobox, inline group and section edits, and instant server-backed persistence, so that building feels like editing a document, not a form wizard.
29. As a student, I want the course picker to offer only my course map entries with their map state, so that I pick real options.
30. As a student, I want an honest validation panel that says the checks run at submit, so that I am never misled by fake live validation.
31. As a student, I want a read-only profile with my identity, CGPA, remaining requirements, prerequisite map, enrollments, and history, so that my academic record is one glance away.
32. As a student, I want stale SIS data to show a non-blocking data-as-of banner with retry, so that I always know how fresh my data is.

### AI advisor chat (S5)

33. As a student, I want AI chat in my rail with a conversation list and transcripts, so that I can plan with the AI advisor.
34. As a student, I want to start a conversation by picking one of three goals, so that the advisor knows my intent.
35. As a student, I want to see the reply stream in token by token with typing feedback, so that the conversation feels alive.
36. As a student, I want every AI plan edit to appear as a system row in the transcript with a link to the builder, so that I can see and check each change.
37. As a student, I want a submit suggestion card after the AI proposes submission, so that I decide in two confirmed steps.
38. As a student, I want the submission result streamed back as a success or constraint row, so that I see the outcome where I chatted.
39. As a student, I want failed turns to keep partial text and offer retry when retryable, so that a network drop never loses my context.
40. As a student who hits the term quota, I want the composer disabled with the fixed quota message and a link to the builder, so that I know what still works.
41. As a student, I want a stop button while the advisor replies, so that I can cut a long stream.
42. As a student, I want the constitution line "The AI advisor explains and drafts. Your advisor approves. Only you can submit.", so that authority is always clear.

### Advisor surfaces (A1-A5)

43. As an advisor, I want a queue of submitted and under-review plans ordered oldest first with aging badges, so that I work the oldest waits first.
44. As an advisor, I want client-side queue filter tabs with counts, so that I can focus on one state.
45. As an advisor, I want a review drawer with the student context, plan lines, and comment thread, so that review is one panel.
46. As an advisor, I want opening a submitted plan to move it under review, so that the queue reflects reality.
47. As an advisor, I want approve behind a confirm that says approval locks the plan, so that the permanent step is deliberate.
48. As an advisor, I want return to demand a written reason inline with a discard guard on close, so that students always get actionable feedback.
49. As an advisor, I want approval gate failures (validation, SIS down) rendered next to the actions with retry, so that I can still choose to return.
50. As an advisor, I want a student explorer over my caseload with server search and honest client filters, so that I can find and open any student's plan.
51. As an advisor, I want meetings as Proposed-to-Done visit requests with slot proposals, so that availability exchange stays simple.
52. As an advisor, I want an office-hours editor of at most five day-and-time rows labeled Africa/Cairo, so that students see my availability.
53. As an advisor, I want an empty queue, empty caseload, and empty meetings state written for the moment they happen, so that quiet terms read as calm.

### Governance (D1, D4, V1, V2)

54. As a dean, I want a faculty overview with five KPI cards, the plan funnel, and a quartile-colored child grid, so that pipeline health is one screen.
55. As a dean or VP, I want to export the governance CSV from the header, so that I can take aggregates offline.
56. As a dean without an assigned faculty, I want a no-faculty empty state, so that the misconfiguration is named calmly.
57. As a VP, I want a university scorecard table over faculties, so that I compare at a glance.
58. As a VP, I want a drill-down that walks faculty, school, department from one cached payload, so that exploration never refetches.
59. As a dean or VP, I want the funnel and heatmap to carry text alternatives, so that screen readers get the same data.

### Admin (M1-M4)

60. As an admin, I want a searchable student accounts table with status, binding, and assignment badges, so that account health is scannable.
61. As an admin, I want an account panel with suspend, reactivate, retry SIS check, correct student ID, delete, and reassign, each with the settled confirmation policy, so that one-way doors confirm and reversible ones do not.
62. As an admin, I want a caseloads surface with CSV import that reports an honest summary or a row-numbered error table, so that bulk assignments are trustworthy.
63. As an admin, I want university rules CRUD with EN and AR fields, so that the AI advisor quotes current rules.
64. As an admin, I want staff creation with an admin-set initial password and a reset-link action, so that staff can sign in.
65. As an admin, I want the queue-aging threshold editable with a statement of what it affects, so that the aging flag matches policy.

### Quality (every story)

66. As any user, I want every screen to work with keyboard alone and visible focus, so that assistive tech and power users both thrive.
67. As any user, I want all copy in my language with Latin numerals and mirrored layout, so that EN and AR are first-class.

## Implementation Decisions

All decisions cite the closed wayfinder tickets on the frontend map "Wayfinder map: Advaisor React client v1 decisions". The map is the decision record; this section carries the decisions the build must obey.

### Demolition and skeleton

- Delete the demo features (teams, discussions, comments, demo users), their routes, the landing page, demo MSW handlers and fixtures, the ADMIN/USER roles, and the team fields on signup. Keep the api client, query setup, auth wiring shape, ui primitives, errors, seo, hooks, utils, mock server, storybook, plop, and all gates (App skeleton and demo demolition).
- Twelve feature folders: auth, plan, plan-builder, ai-chat, advisor-queue, advisor-students, advisor-meetings, advisor-hours, governance, admin, notifications, profile; cross-feature domain components in the approved src/components/domain/ folder (App skeleton, Decision 2).
- Route tree: role redirect at /, X1 at /login, /signup, /forgot-password, /verify-email/:id/:hash; student /app section (index, plan, builder, profile, chat, chat/:conversationId, notifications); advisor /advisor section (index, students, meetings, hours, notifications); dean /dean (index, notifications); VP /vp (index, drilldown); admin /admin (index redirect to students, assignments, rules, settings); not-found fallback (App skeleton Decision 3, Admin D1).
- Five lazy role sections, each with its own shell module and RoleRoute guard rendering the permission-denied state on foreign-role hits (App skeleton Decisions 4-6).
- One app-shell: role rail from a config map, spacious density for students, compact for staff; topbar carries language toggle, theme toggle, notification bell with unread badge, account menu (App skeleton Decision 5, Cross-cutting UX D6).
- Exactly four env variables: API_URL (default http://localhost:8000/api), ENABLE_API_MOCKING, APP_URL, APP_MOCK_API_PORT (App skeleton Decision 7).
- Generators: component generator emits a test file; a feature generator scaffolds uniform feature folders (App skeleton Decision 8).

### Tokens and styling

- Apply the design.md Appendix B token block to index.css: crimson ramp, seven state pairs (draft, submitted, under-review, returned, approved, failed, closed), status channels, data quartiles, motion tokens; dark mode flips via the .dark block; discarded renders on state-closed with a slate dot (design.md 3, Appendix B; contract gaps item 10).

### API conventions

- One axios instance; bearer token from localStorage; response interceptor normalizes every failure into one ApiError with status, key, fields, message, requestId; 401 clears the token and redirects to /login with redirectTo and reason=expired; the interceptor never toasts (API and state conventions 1-8).
- Shared unwrap helpers for single envelopes, plain arrays, and paginated lists; the SSE reader serves the two stream endpoints (Client API inventory).
- Query keys follow the inventory scheme; plan mutations apply the returned plan with setQueryData; optimism only on notification reads; the settled per-family staleTime and polling table (conventions 20-30).
- Every form is react-hook-form plus zod with dictionary messages, onBlur mode, focus on first error, server errors merged over client errors (conventions 31-36).
- Error taxonomy: 422 inline by key with fixed surfaces for the four plan-gate keys, 403 permission panel, 404 not-found/empty, 409 invalidate-plus-one-calm-toast, 429 quota inline in chat and throttle inline on auth forms, 503 service slugs as the destructive banner with retry (conventions 9-19).

### Auth

- Token in localStorage behind the interceptor; no client TTL; 401 is the expiry signal; logout is best-effort with local cleanup guaranteed; sanitized redirectTo (Auth token storage).
- X1 flows per the auth UX resolution: signup fields email, student ID, password, confirmation, language preference; university-domain client rule; four verify-email states (ready, held, invalid, SIS-retry); forgot-password ends at the sent confirmation; login redirects per role with sanitized redirectTo (Auth and account UX).

### i18n and RTL

- react-i18next with typed EN/AR JSON namespaces (common, auth, plan, chat, advisor, governance, admin, notifications), key-parity test, zustand-persisted language store seeded from the profile preference, dir on html, logical properties with rtl: reserved for icon flips, Fontsource Inter and Cairo self-hosted, Latin numerals through one formatting module with a dayjs ar locale clone (i18n and RTL approach).

### Mock server

- openapi-typescript generates the contract types; openapi-msw types hand-written handlers over the data store; nine scenario seeds (happy, empty, error, permission-denied, stale-sis, registration-closed, quota-exhausted, import-errors, binding-incomplete); browser switching by ?scenario= persisted in sessionStorage, tests via handler overrides, e2e via POST /__mocks/scenario; SSE mocked with ReadableStream bodies carrying the seven frame types (Mock server research; conventions 37-41).

### Shared UX system

- State components: skeleton family, EmptyState, ErrorState with retry and requestId, PermissionDenied, StaleSisBanner, WindowClosed; toast policy where 401/403/429-quota/5xx never toast and success toasts only for off-screen effects; confirm only for irreversible actions per the settled table; notification center with the slug icons, optimistic reads, and the screen-to-route deep-link map resolved by role; two-density table system; class-flip dark mode; axe over the mock scenarios in e2e (Cross-cutting UX system).

### Primitives

- Add in order: card, badge, chip, banner, skeleton family, empty-state, avatar, confirm-dialog, kpi-card, tabs, tooltip, popover, combobox, progress; upgrade table in place (dense, tabular-nums, sticky header, aria-sort, page sizes 10/20/50/All); each with story and test (Component primitive gap list).

### Surfaces

- Student S1-S4, chat S5, advisor A1-A5, governance D1/D4/V1/V2, admin M1-M4, and the notification pages follow the per-surface resolutions on the map: the student builder is a single-scroll document with live server mutations and an honest validation panel; the review drawer is shared by queue and explorer; the funnel is the one chart (recharts, route-split); admin has no structure or system-log surface.
- Domain components live in features or src/components/domain/ per the settled homes: PlanStateChip, plan cards and lines, validation panel, comment thread, Seen button, submit suggestion card, prereq map, slot editor and viewer, visit request card, queue table, review drawer, governance set, notification center.

### Contract-gap stances honored in the build

- No window dates: WindowClosed renders date-free on the three settled triggers. No credits: course counts render, credit totals omitted. No student visit-request list: the creating session caches the request. No quota read: quota surfaces at 429 only. No staff list: password reset only for accounts created in-session. deep_link routes by screen object resolved by role (Contract gaps and contradictions; backend handoffs recorded in docs/backend-contract-handoffs.md).

## Testing Decisions

- Seams: the primary seam is the MSW-backed HTTP API. Feature tests render the real app provider with the router against scenario-seeded MSW handlers and assert on user-visible behavior, never on hook internals or store shapes; this extends the repo's existing renderApp integration pattern. The secondary seam is the component seam: ui primitives and domain components get Testing Library tests beside stories, asserting semantics (roles, names, states), not pixels. The third seam is the i18n key-parity test over the namespace JSON.
- What makes a good test here: it drives the component or app as a user does (type, click, wait for the observable outcome), routes every network call through MSW, and fails on the behavior regression rather than the implementation. No fetch or axios stubbing.
- Prior art: the scaffold's form and route integration tests, the authorization and head component tests, and the discussions route tests (the pattern, not the domain, survives demolition).
- Every ui primitive ships a story with a11y checks; domain components get stories with state coverage via scenario fixtures; e2e covers the J1 happy loop, the J2 return loop, one advisor review, and axe scans over the six core scenarios.

## Out of Scope

- Backend contract changes: the four handoffs and doc riders live in docs/backend-contract-handoffs.md for the backend effort.
- Real backend integration: the client runs on the mock layer until the API is reachable; no env beyond the settled four.
- Dean advisor-detail and student-explorer surfaces, the governance scoreboard and trends charts, admin structure and system log: contract-blocked, recorded designs exist on the map.
- Quota meter, plan history, term countdown, dated window banner: accepted contract gaps, v2.
- Memory visualization and trust-stage controls for the AI beyond the constitution line.
- New design tokens or visual directions beyond design.md v1.1; deviations amend design.md through governance.

title: Contract gaps and contradictions
description:
## Question

For each contract gap and contradiction the research surfaced, what is the client's stance: work around it in the client, raise it to the backend effort, or accept and document it?

## Context

Inputs: the resolutions of "Client API inventory from the OpenAPI contract" (9 gaps: no refresh endpoint, GET verify-email semantics inside an SPA, no page query param despite pagination meta, no student-facing visit-request list, no staff list endpoint, no profile or language-preference update, notification deep_link format undefined, governance export Content-Disposition undocumented, no endpoint exposing remaining AI turn quota) and "Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions" (10 contradictions, including the contract's ninth PlanStatus value `discarded` against the settled 8 states, and the design plan's stale 9-state chip). Decide per item. Anything raised to the backend is a handoff: contract changes stay out of scope on this map, so record the ask and move on.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling.

## Record

A numbered stance per item: workaround, handoff (with the exact ask), or accept.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; backend authority cited per item)

Resolution for acad-abl.20 (wayfinder:grilling). Nineteen items: the 9 contract gaps from acad-abl.2 and the 10 contradictions from acad-abl.1. Each item carries one stance: workaround (the client-side stance), handoff (the exact ask to the backend effort), or accept (what we document and where). Backend authority: the acad-9s3 settled decisions and children acad-9s3.3, acad-9s3.14, acad-9s3.15. Implementation facts were verified in /home/shehab/Projects/academic-advisor-backend on 2026-10-01 (openapi.json, routes/api.php, app/Notifications, app/Http/Controllers). Client-side design calls follow design.md and the settled frontend tickets (acad-abl.8, acad-abl.9, acad-abl.13).

## A. Contract gaps (acad-abl.2)

1. No token refresh endpoint. Accept. The spec's auth chapter states: the Sanctum token lives 30 days, 401 is the only expiry signal, the interceptor clears the token and redirects to /login with redirectTo (acad-abl.13 conventions 6 and 8), and no form state survives a 401 (convention 36). Re-authentication is the only recovery in v1; a refresh endpoint stays a v2 ask. (acad-9s3 decision 1.)

2. GET /api/verify-email/{id}/{hash} semantics inside the SPA. Handoff. Verified: routes/api.php names the API route verification.verify, so Laravel mails the API URL and a browser click renders raw JSON. Exact ask: "Point the verification email link at the SPA, {app origin}/verify-email/{id}/{hash}, keeping the expires and signature query params the signed middleware requires, and document that the client route calls GET /api/verify-email/{id}/{hash} on the user's behalf." Client meanwhile (my design call): the client serves /verify-email/:id/:hash, calls the endpoint, renders success per design.md 4.3, then redirects an authenticated user to /app and a guest to /login; 403 invalid-link renders the calm error panel, 503 renders the SIS panel with Retry. (acad-9s3 decision 2.)

3. No page query parameter. Workaround. No surface paginates past the first page in v1: tables offer the settled 10/20/50/All sizes (backend API conventions; design.md 5.2), and moving deeper follows links.next, which the server already emits for the three paginated lists (notifications, caseload, admin students). No numeric jump control is built. Rider handoff (doc only): "Document the page parameter name (Laravel page) in openapi.json." (acad-9s3 cross-cutting pagination convention.)

4. No student visit-request list. Handoff. Verified: the student visit-requests group has POST and DELETE only (routes/api.php lines 180 to 186), so a reloaded client has no id for Delete and no open-request status surface. Exact ask: "Add GET /api/visit-requests returning the signed-in student's own requests with the VisitRequest schema, under the create-visit-request permission." Client meanwhile: after POST the client writes the returned VisitRequest into the ['visit-requests'] cache so the current session shows the open request and Delete works; a reload loses it until the endpoint lands. (acad-9s3 Meetings baseline: at most one Proposed request per student per term.)

5. No staff list endpoint. Accept. Settled decision 18 caps the admin console at six capabilities and grants staff account creation only; no staff directory was settled. The admin accounts surface (M1) lists students through GET /api/admin/students with search; staff creation is an action that confirms inline with the created account, role, and reset-email state. The spec's admin chapter states that staff management beyond creation does not exist in v1. A staff list is a v2 feature request, not a v1 handoff. (acad-9s3 decision 18.)

6. No profile or language-preference write. Workaround. Language: the client owns a device-local toggle (Zustand persist, acad-abl.6) seeded from user.language_preference at login; the server keeps the registration-time preference. Profile: S4 is read-only (CGPA, remaining credits, prerequisite map, history) because identity and academic data are SIS-owned (acad-9s3 decision 21) and no surface settles a profile edit. The spec's profile chapter states both rules; no PATCH /api/me is asked in v1.

7. Notification deep_link format. Workaround, on the implemented shape. Verified: app/Notifications/Notification.php emits deep_link as an object {screen, ...subjectIdentifiers} with screen in {plan, student, advisor, visit} and ids plan_id, visit_request_id, student_id, or term_code, and NotificationResource passes it through; openapi.json types it as a nullable string, which is stale. Client convention (my design call): one screen-to-route map keyed by screen and resolved by the recipient's role: plan to /app/plan with plan_id; student to /advisor/students with student_id; advisor to /app (the advisor card on the student dashboard); visit to /advisor/meetings for advisor recipients and /app for students until item 4 lands; unknown screens fall back to the role landing. Rider handoff (doc only): "Update openapi.json Notification.deep_link to the object schema the implementation sends."

8. Governance export filename. Workaround. Verified: ExportGovernanceController streams through response()->streamDownload with the name governance-{term_code}.csv, so Content-Disposition is sent but undocumented and unreadable cross-origin without Access-Control-Expose-Headers. The client names the file itself: governance-{term_code}.csv built from the governance payload's term_code, with governance.csv as fallback. The spec's governance chapter fixes that pattern. Rider handoff (doc only): "Document Content-Disposition in openapi.json." (acad-9s3 decision 9, acad-9s3.15 decision 10.)

9. No quota read endpoint. Accept. The chat UI shows no quota meter in v1; quota surfaces only at the turns 429 with the fixed copy from acad-abl.13 convention 15, and the composer stays disabled for the term because retry means a new turn that cannot succeed (acad-9s3 decision 20: 100 turns per term, config constant, no Admin UI). The spec's chat chapter states that the remaining count is invisible until exhaustion and that a counter needs an endpoint (v2).

## B. Contradictions (acad-abl.1 section 9)

10. The ninth PlanStatus value, discarded, against the settled 8 states. Workaround: render it, do not filter it. PlanStateChip accepts the ninth value as a terminal record state and maps it to the state-closed token pair with its own label and a slate dot (acad-abl.9 D3). Lifecycle copy and funnel labels still count 8 states, because discard is an operation on a draft or returned plan, not a lifecycle stage (acad-9s3 decision 10). The S2 discard action is a confirm-dialog, never a chip state the student waits in.

11. The stale 9-state design-plan chip. Accept, corrected by the frontend effort. The spec and design.md use 8 chip states; design.md 3.4 and 5.4 drop Registration Confirmed and Verification Failed as plan states and delete the state-confirmed token pair entry; state-failed remains only as expired's pair (acad-abl.9 D3). acad-9s3.3 resolution point 4 assigns this correction to the frontend effort; the same pass corrects the chip sizing note in docs/03-DESIGN-PLAN.md. (acad-9s3.3: approval is the final stage, 8 states.)

12. V1-V6 versus the three settled checks. Accept. The client computes no rule and keys all validation UI off the four 422 keys: allowance, map_membership, prerequisite_chain, window (acad-9s3 decision 17). The design.md 4.4 line "validates live against V1-V6" is corrected in the frontend spec pass to mean: render server results per DS-ST-09 to DS-ST-11; the hard block sits at the submit gate (DS-ST-10), and mutation-time map guards surface under the course line (decision 19).

13. The dean student explorer is dead. Accept. acad-abl.8 Decision 3 already omits /dean/students: the dean reads faculty-scoped aggregates only, with no individual students, plans, or profiles (acad-9s3.15 decision 4; acad-9s3 decision 22). The doc pass corrects design.md 6.1, 6.2, and foundation 14 (acad-abl.8 flag 1).

14. Visit approve and deny flows are dead. Accept. The settled model is Proposed to Done with no approval, denial, slot picking, or booking (acad-9s3 Meetings baseline, amended by the office hours ticket). VisitRequestCard's Accept/Decline design is reworked by the advisor-meetings surface work per acad-abl.8 flag 4; the client builds no approve or deny affordance anywhere. (acad-9s3 decision 23 area, acad-9s3.13.)

15. Missing notification slugs (registration_confirmed, verification_failed) and the queue-aging trigger. Accept. The client renders only the contract's 9 slugs (openapi NotificationSlug; lang/en/notifications.php). registration_confirmed and verification_failed never existed: verification died with acad-9s3.3, and no icon or route map entries are built for them. Queue aging fires no notification; the UI reads the is_aging flags on queue and caseload rows (acad-abl.1 section 4). The spec's notification chapter lists the 9 slugs and a fallback rule: unknown slugs render a generic row that routes to the role landing. (acad-9s3 decision 8, acad-9s3.14.)

16. submit.armed placement and the key field name. Accept. The contract is the source of truth: submit.armed streams one frame on POST /plan-conversations/{conversation}/submit-arm, not inside the turns stream, and the error frame's localization field is key, not message_key (acad-abl.1 contradiction 7; acad-9s3 decision 20). acad-abl.13 conventions 18 and 40 already quote the contract shape; the spec repeats it.

17. Registration window dates are not client-visible. Handoff. Exact ask: "Expose the current term's registration window to the client, for example GET /api/terms/current returning opens_at and closes_at, or a window object on an existing envelope, so the dashboard countdown and a dated WindowClosedBanner can be data-driven." Client meanwhile (my design call): the banner renders without dates with honest copy, "Registration is closed. Your approved plan waits for the next window." (design.md 4.3), and triggers only on the submit 422 window key, the 503 plan.window_unavailable, and window notification deep links (acad-abl.13 flag); the dashboard countdown is cut in v1. (acad-9s3.4: SIS owns the window; acad-abl.1 section 7.)

18. Credit totals and the missing catalog endpoint. Handoff. Verified: Plan.total_credit_hours is "Always 0 for now; the SIS computes credit totals" and PlannedCourse carries only course_code, group, section, reason, so no client-side sum or per-course credit is possible. Exact ask: "Populate Plan.total_credit_hours, or add a credits field to PlannedCourse rows, so the client can render the plan total and per-course credits." Client meanwhile: course titles join from the prerequisite_map entries (course_code, title, state, prerequisites) of GET /api/academic-record; the credit total is omitted rather than rendered as a fake zero; prerequisite chain visuals render from the map's prerequisites and state fields and block on nothing else. (acad-9s3 decision 19; acad-abl.1 contradiction 9; acad-abl.9 flag 5.)

19. Reason rejection status: contract 409 versus implementation 422. Accept. The client never sends a reason (acad-abl.13 convention 33; acad-9s3 decision 19), so neither status has a UI branch; the interceptor normalizes both into ApiError and the standard surfaces apply. The spec's builder chapter states reasons are AI-only and notes the divergence: openapi.json says rejected with 409, PlanService.assertReasonAllowed throws 422 with key reason. Rider handoff (doc only): "Align the openapi.json reason wording with the 422 implementation."

## Summary

Five workarounds (3, 6, 7, 8, 10), four handoffs (2, 4, 17, 18), ten accepts (1, 5, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 19). Rider doc-only asks ride on items 3, 7, 8, and 19.
Owner follow-up (2026-10-02): the four handoffs, the four riders, and the secondary asks are written up for the backend effort at docs/backend-contract-handoffs.md in this repo.
close_reason: 19 stances recorded: 5 workarounds, 4 handoffs (SPA verification link, student visit-request list, window dates endpoint, credit totals source), 10 accepts

title: Dean and VP surfaces
description:
## Question

What do the dean dashboard, advisor detail, student explorer, and VP scorecard and drill-down show, and which charts render where?

## Context

Governance contract: `GET /api/governance/dashboard` (metrics, funnel, nodes) and `GET /api/governance/export`. Chart choice follows the "Charting library for governance dashboards" resolution. design.md tokens define heatmap quartiles and the crimson ramp. Decide: scoreboard composition, drill-down paths, advisor detail scope, export button behavior, read-only guardrails (dean and VP never mutate), and empty and denied states.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling.

## Record

Per-surface numbered decisions, including the chart-to-surface mapping.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.17 (wayfinder:grilling), Dean and VP surfaces. Sources: design.md sections 3, 5, 6.2, 8, 9; docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md sections 5, 13, 14, 15, 18; zoomed resolutions acad-abl.5 (charting), acad-abl.1 (digest), acad-abl.19 (shared states, tables), acad-abl.9 (primitives), acad-abl.13 (conventions), acad-abl.20 (export filename, explorer stance); backend map acad-9s3 settled decisions 9, 15, 22 and child acad-9s3.15 (governance, 13 decisions); openapi.json Governance endpoints and schemas; the backend controllers and lang catalog verified 2026-10-01. Routes follow the settled tree in acad-abl.8 Decision 3, which maps this ticket's scope lines as: dean /department overview = /dean, advisor detail = /dean/advisors/:id, student explorer = /dean/students; VP /university scorecard = /vp, drilldown = /vp/drilldown. Impeccable (Operate mode) informed craft judgment; scanability and consistency outrank expression.

## 0. Contract truth: one tree, one export

The contract serves the whole feature with two endpoints (openapi.json, verified against routes/api.php):

- GET /api/governance/dashboard returns GovernanceNodeEnvelope: one root GovernanceNode with recursive children. Node: level (university, faculty, school, department), code, name_en, name_ar, term_code, metrics, children. Metrics: students, caseload (students with an assigned advisor), approved, completion_rate (fraction 0 to 1, null when caseload is 0, verified in GovernanceService line 122), completion_is_final (boolean), median_decision_hours (number, null when no decided plans), aging_count (Submitted plus Under Review past the Admin threshold), funnel (nine integer counts: draft, submitted, under_review, returned, approved, expired, closed, withdrawn, discarded).
- GET /api/governance/export streams the flattened tree as CSV with no parameters. The server names it governance-{term_code}.csv but sends no readable Content-Disposition cross-origin, so the client names the file itself (acad-abl.20 stance 8).

What the contract does not contain shapes the honest scope: no advisor rows anywhere in the tree, no per-advisor endpoint, no time series, no student rows, no term selector (acad-9s3.15 decision 8: current term only, no history). Dean scoping is server-side: the root is the dean's faculty; VP and other governance roles get the university root (endpoint description; acad-9s3.15 decision 4). A dean whose account has no faculty gets 403 with the message governance.faculty_unassigned, "Your dean account has no faculty assigned." (GovernanceService line 24, lang/en/governance.php).

Client conventions: query root ['governance'], staleTime 5 minutes, no polling, no optimistic updates (acad-abl.13 rules 22, 25, 28). The whole tree arrives in one payload, so all navigation inside the feature is client-side over the cached tree; the feature owns one useGovernance hook over the root key and a node-lookup util that walks children by code (acad-abl.13 rule 21). Feature folder: src/features/governance/ (acad-abl.8 Decision 2). Primitives come from acad-abl.9: kpi-card (item 9), banner, empty-state, skeleton, badge, card, the upgraded table.

## D1. Dean overview (/dean)

Read-only, faculty-scoped, current term (foundation 5: "read-only, own department only" as amended by acad-9s3.15 decision 4: the dean is a faculty-scoped VP with aggregates only).

D1.1 Header. Page title = the faculty node name (name_en or name_ar by locale, code fallback when both are null). Context line = "{Level label} . {term_code} . {students} students" with the localized level label from the dictionary (the backend carries governance.levels; the client duplicates the four words in its dictionary, DS-W-01). Primary action: Export CSV (D6.2).

D1.2 KPI row. Five kpi-cards in the dense variant, grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-5 (design.md 5.3), tabular-nums (DS-C-11). Which metrics earn cards, chosen from the contract's governance metrics against foundation 18 success metrics:

1. Completion rate: value = completion_rate as a percentage, one decimal; context line from completion_is_final: "Live during the window" when false, "Final" when true (acad-9s3.15 decision 7: live during the window, final at close). Null renders an em dash with context "No assigned caseload yet".
2. Median decision time: median_decision_hours rendered in hours, one decimal when fractional, unit suffix "h"; context "Current term decided plans" (decision 7). Null renders an em dash with context "No decisions yet this term".
3. Aging: aging_count; context "Past the {n}-day threshold". The threshold value is Admin-configured and not in the governance payload, so the context line omits the number unless a later contract addition carries it; default context: "Undecided past the aging threshold" (acad-9s3.15 decision 5).
4. Caseload: caseload count; context "Students with an assigned advisor" (schema description).
5. Approved: approved count; context "Approved and closed plans this term" (the backend counts Approved plus Closed, GovernanceService APPROVED_STATES).

The node's raw students total lives in the header context line, not a card, to keep the row at five. No delta arrows and no sparklines: the contract carries no series and no prior-period value (decision 8); inventing a trend would lie (DP-09).

D1.3 Funnel chart. FunnelChart per design.md 5.4 and acad-abl.5: one recharts BarChart with layout="vertical" (horizontal bars), one category per GovernanceFunnel key, count on the value axis, labels always visible (color is redundant, DS-C-10). Stage order: the pipeline group draft, submitted, under_review, returned, approved, then a visual divider and the terminal group expired, closed, withdrawn, discarded. Labels count 8 lifecycle states; discarded renders as its own terminal row with its own label because discard is an operation, not a stage (acad-abl.1 section 1; acad-abl.20 item 10). Bar fills use the design.md 3.5 categorical series mapped to fixed per-stage token constants, dark mode through var() tokens (acad-abl.5). Tooltip: stage label plus count, dictionary copy. Text alternative: the chart ships with a visually-hidden or adjacent table carrying the same nine rows (DS-C-10, DS-A-03); the accessibilityLayer prop plus an aria-label on the chart region. RTL: explicit props per direction, XAxis reversed plus YAxis orientation="right" under dir=rtl, margins mirrored through logical properties (acad-abl.5 RTL plan). Empty funnel: all nine counts zero renders EmptyState, title "No plans yet this term", body "Counts appear as students build and submit plans for {term_code}." (DS-W-07), never an empty axis frame.

D1.4 Child drill grid with heatmap coloring. One component, GovernanceChildGrid, over the root node's children (schools, then their departments; acad-9s3.15 decision 2 nesting). Cell anatomy: node name, completion rate as a percentage in tabular-nums, background = the design.md 3.5 quartile token data-1 to data-4 with the matching foreground pair. Banding is by absolute rate: 0 to .25 data-1, .25 to .5 data-2, .5 to .75 data-3, .75 to 1 data-4; null renders a muted "No data" cell. Absolute bands keep the color stable and comparable across pages; rank-based quartiles would re-color on every sibling set change. This is my design call within design.md 3.5's "aggregate intensity" intent. Color never carries the value alone: the number sits in the cell (DS-C-08), and the grid doubles as the DS-C-10 text alternative (acad-abl.5 heatmap stance: plain HTML, token classes, no chart library). Cell press scopes the page to that node through the ?node={code} search param: the KPI row, funnel, and grid re-render from the cached subtree (the drill-down of acad-9s3.15 decision 22, hosted inline because the settled dean route tree has no drill route and the payload is already client-side). A node with no children renders EmptyState, "No sub-units under {name}. Metrics for this unit appear above."

D1.5 Advisor scoreboard: designed, blocked on the contract. acad-9s3.15 decision 6 defines the table (one row per advisor with assigned students in scope: caseload size, completion, median decision time, aging count) and design.md 5.4 ScoreboardTable specs it, but openapi.json exposes no advisor-level governance data (see Flag 1). The v1 build renders no scoreboard and no /dean/advisors/:id. The recorded design for the moment the contract adds it: columns advisor name, caseload size, completion %, median decision hours, aging count; default sort aging count descending (the escalation ask, PR-13), sortable headers with aria-sort; compact density, sticky header, tabular-nums, right-aligned numerics (acad-abl.19 D5); row click opens the advisor detail; aging cells above threshold carry the amber aging badge treatment from design.md 5.4; CSV export already mirrors it once it exists (decision 10). Placed on /dean below the funnel.

## D2. Advisor detail (/dean/advisors/:id): cut

The route dies for v1. Evidence: the governance tree carries level, code, names, term_code, metrics, and children only; no advisor identity or advisor-keyed node exists anywhere in openapi.json. The caseload and plan endpoints are advisor-gated (/api/advisor/*): the permission seed gives the dean exactly view-governance (seed migration line 16; acad-abl.1 section 3), so a dean calling them gets 403. No per-advisor history endpoint exists, and inventing one from node aggregates would fake decision-time or aging values that the tree does not carry (DP-09). Actions: omit the route; the dean rail drops the Advisors item (rail becomes Overview, Notifications); design.md 6.1 and 6.2 D2 and foundation 14's advisor-detail row join the pending doc pass (acad-abl.8 flag 1, acad-abl.20 item 13). Flag 1 carries the contract ask.

## D3. Dean student explorer (/dean/students): cut, verified dead

Verified against the backend decisions: acad-9s3.15 decision 4 states "the dean sees no individual students, no student plans, no student profiles, and no student explorer", amending the former baseline; acad-9s3 decision 15 and 22 carry the same amendment; the acad-abl.1 digest flagged the dean explorer row dead (contradiction 4); acad-abl.20 item 13 accepted it; acad-abl.8 Decision 3 already omits the route. The explorer field set quoted in the digest (name, student ID, SIS email, faculty, school, department, level, plan state, submitted date, aging flag, CGPA) belongs to the advisor explorer (acad-9s3.15 decision 5), not the dean. Outcome: no route, no rail item, no component, no filter model. Nothing to scope; the doc pass stands.

## D4. VP scorecard (/vp)

Read-only, university-wide, aggregates only, never individual students (foundation 5, Q63; acad-9s3 decision 22).

D4.1 Header and tiles. Title "University scorecard" or the university node name; context line = "{term_code} . {students} students". The five KPI cards from D1.2 render at university grain through the same GovernanceKpiRow component; exact numbers at every group size, no suppression (acad-9s3.15 decision 1).

D4.2 Faculty scorecard table. FacultyScorecard per design.md 5.4: plain HTML on the existing table component (acad-abl.5: no chart library on tables), one row per faculty child of the university root. Columns: faculty (bilingual name, code fallback), students, caseload, approved, completion %, median decision hours, aging count. Compact density, sticky header, tabular-nums, numerics right-aligned at the inline end (acad-abl.19 D5, DS-C-11, DS-R-03). Default sort completion % descending with nulls last because the VP's job is comparison at a glance (foundation 14); sortable headers override with aria-sort. Page size defaults to All; the tree is one payload and the VP compares all faculties at once. No checkbox multi-select (acad-abl.19 D5.4). Row click navigates to /vp/drilldown?node={code}.

D4.3 Trends chart: cut. The task asked for a Recharts line with series and range. The contract serves one current-term snapshot per node and decision 8 (acad-9s3.15) allows no term selector and no history; no field in GovernanceMetrics is a series. There is no line to draw, and a fabricated range would violate the no-invented-data scope rule. The recharts AreaChart trend wrapper from acad-abl.5 is deferred until a series endpoint exists. Consequence: recharts lands in v1 for the FunnelChart only, still route-split to the /dean and /vp sections (acad-abl.9 D2), and its DS-G-07 approval still gates the build (Flag 5).

D4.4 Heatmap on V1: none. The university root's children are faculties and the scorecard table already shows their rates with sort; a second colored grid over the same values duplicates the comparison (DP-02, DP-05). Heatmap coloring appears where the contract supplies per-node values and no table already carries them: the drill grid (D1.4, D5.2).

## D5. VP drill-down (/vp/drilldown?node={code})

D5.1 Navigation model. One payload renders every path; the route carries the selected node code in the search param. Absent or unknown code falls back to the university root. Drill order follows the nesting: university, faculty, school, department (acad-9s3.15 decision 3). The VP never reaches advisors or students at any depth (decision 3).

D5.2 Node view. Breadcrumb from the walked path with localized level labels (DS-L-02 header pattern; breadcrumb items navigate, current node is aria-current). Body = GovernanceKpiRow + FunnelChart + GovernanceChildGrid scoped to the selected node, the exact components from D1. A department (leaf) renders KPIs and funnel with no child grid; EmptyState covers the childless case. DrilldownTable from design.md 5.4 is the child grid's table aspect; no separate component exists (DP-05). Scope label "{Level} . {node name}" repeats in the header so a screenshot stays interpretable (design.md 5.4 "same table anatomy with scope labels").

D5.3 Relationship to dean views. The dean's /dean is the same component set rooted at the faculty (acad-9s3.15 decision 4: the dean is a faculty-scoped VP); the VP's drill view reaches the same faculty, school, and department nodes but stops there. One feature folder, shared components, different roots; no route or data path leads a VP into dean-only advisor content, and none exists to show (D2).

## D6. Shared governance components and the export button

D6.1 Component list, all in src/features/governance/ (acad-abl.8 Decision 2): useGovernance (['governance'] root, 5-minute staleTime, no polling), GovernanceHeader (title, context line, Export CSV action), GovernanceKpiRow, FunnelChart (recharts wrapper: token fills, RTL props, accessibilityLayer, tooltip, text-alternative table, EmptyState), GovernanceChildGrid (heatmap-table hybrid with quartile tokens), useGovernanceNode (tree walk by code). No new ui/ primitives; kpi-card, empty-state, skeleton, banner, badge, table all come from acad-abl.9.

D6.2 Export. Placement: the header action on /dean and /vp (one verb label "Export CSV", DS-L-02, DS-W-04). V2 omits the button: the endpoint takes no parameters and always streams the requester's whole scoped tree, so a second button would download the identical file (DP-02). Behavior: GET as a blob through the shared api client; the button keeps its label, shows the Spinner, and sets aria-busy during the download (design.md 4.1); no progress percentage exists because the endpoint is a single streamed response, and none is promised. Filename: the client names the file governance-{term_code}.csv from the cached root node's term_code, fallback governance.csv (acad-abl.20 stance 8). Success: toast "CSV export generated." (acad-abl.19 D2.2 names this exact case). Failure: a destructive toast with the server message when one exists, else the dictionary load-failed line; recovery is pressing the button again (acad-abl.13 rules 19, 2.1 taxonomy). A 403 during export renders the same denied handling as the dashboard (D7). Headers inside the CSV come localized from the backend in the requester's language (acad-9s3.15 decision 10); the client adds nothing to the file.

## D7. Read-only guardrails, denied states, and the six screen states

D7.1 Guardrails. The governance feature renders no mutation affordance anywhere: no approve, return, comment, visit, or assignment control, and no link into any plan, profile, or student surface. This is structural: the payload contains no student or advisor rows, and the build rule bans imports from the advisor and plan features (cross-feature import ban, acad-abl.8 Decision 2). Rows navigate only between governance nodes.

D7.2 The six states (acad-abl.19 D1, DS-ST-08), per surface:

- Loading: skeleton matching the KPI grid, funnel block, and grid or table shape (SkeletonCard, SkeletonTableRows); aria-busy on the region (acad-abl.19 D1.1).
- Empty: empty funnel (D1.3), childless node (D1.4), and the dean without a faculty: a page EmptyState titled "No faculty assigned", body "Your dean account has no faculty assigned. Ask an administrator to finish setup.", no action. This is a missing-config state, decided client-side from dean role plus user.faculty null on ['me'], not from string-matching the 403 (Flag 4).
- Error: ErrorState with Retry refetching ['governance'] (acad-abl.19 D1.3; acad-abl.13 rule 24).
- Permission denied: RoleRoute guards the /dean and /vp sections on direct URL hits (acad-abl.8 Decision 4); an API 403 renders the PermissionDenied panel naming the governance audience with a way back (acad-abl.13 rule 12). The no-faculty dean renders the EmptyState above instead, because the panel's role reminder would be false: the dean is in the right place and the data is missing.
- Stale SIS: N/A. Governance nodes carry no staleness payload; the metrics are platform-computed for the current term. Freshness is the 5-minute staleTime convention (acad-abl.13 rule 25); no banner.
- Window closed: N/A. No submission affordance exists on these surfaces.

D7.3 Craft constraints that bind every decision above: dictionary-only copy in EN and AR (DS-W-01), Latin tabular numerals (DS-T-03, DS-C-11), logical properties with icon flips only under rtl: (DS-L-03, acad-abl.19 D7), no color-only meaning (DS-C-08), plan-state colors stay off these surfaces except inside the funnel's fixed stage mapping which is chart data coloring, not plan-state chrome (DS-C-09 is respected because the funnel uses the 3.5 categorical series, not the 3.4 state token pairs), compact staff density from the shell (acad-abl.19 D6.2), 44px touch targets on touch viewports (DS-S-01). New components ship stories and tests (DS-CP-03); both render directions verified (acad-abl.19 D7.4); npm run verify before any commit.

## Flags for the owner

1. Advisor performance has no contract source. Backend decisions 6 and 22 (acad-9s3.15) name it a dean surface (university-wide for the VP table per decision 6) with fixed columns, but openapi.json serves only the org tree; GovernanceNode carries no advisor rows. Exact ask: "Add an advisor performance read to the governance contract, for example GET /api/governance/advisors returning one row per advisor in scope with caseload size, completion, median decision hours, and aging count, scoped server-side like the dashboard." Until it lands, D2 stays cut and the D1 scoreboard stays unbuildable; the recorded design in D1.5 unblocks it in one ticket.
2. Trends have no data source. The contract serves one current-term snapshot and decision 8 allows no history, so the acad-abl.5 trend wrapper is deferred and the funnel is the only v1 chart. A series endpoint would revive it; none is asked here.
3. Doc pass items for design.md and foundation 14 (extends acad-abl.8 flag 1 and acad-abl.20 item 13): drop D2 /dean/advisors/:id and the dean Advisors rail item, mark the D1 scoreboard as contract-blocked, and mark the V1 trends chart as cut.
4. The 403 for an unassigned dean carries only the message governance.faculty_unassigned, no machine-readable key. The client branches on role plus user.faculty from ['me'] instead of message matching. A stable error key on that response would be cleaner; doc-only ask.
5. recharts still needs DS-G-07 human approval before install (acad-abl.5, acad-abl.9 flag 4); it now gates the FunnelChart alone.
6. MSW needs a governance handler serving the faculty tree for a dean and the university tree for a VP, plus the no-faculty dean case, added to the acad-abl.13 rule 39 scenario set at build time.
close_reason: Dean and VP surfaces resolved on the governance contract: D1 dean overview (5 KPI cards, recharts funnel, quartile drill grid, inline drill), D2 advisor detail and D3 student explorer cut (no contract data), V1 scorecard, V2 drilldown, export spec; 6 owner flags

title: Admin surfaces M1-M5
description:
## Question

What do the admin surfaces (M1–M5) show and do?

## Context

M1 accounts (students: suspend, reactivate, retry-sis, correct student id), M2 caseloads (assignments import, reassign), M3 structure (org units), M4 rules (university rules CRUD for V1–V6 parameters), M5 settings and staff (queue-aging-threshold, staff creation, password reset). Input: the "Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions" resolution. Decide: destructive-action confirmations, import file UX and ImportSummary display, the rules editor form shape, and staff flows.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling.

## Record

Per-surface numbered decisions.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.18 (wayfinder:grilling), Admin surfaces. Sources: backend map acad-9s3 settled decisions 2, 8, 15, 17, 18, 21, 22 and child acad-9s3.16 (admin console, both amendments); the contract openapi.json (admin paths and schemas, verified 2026-10-01); backend implementation files for error keys and account states (paths cited inline); design.md sections 4, 5, 6, 8; foundation sections 3, 5, 8, 17; zoomed resolutions acad-abl.1 (digest), acad-abl.13 (conventions), acad-abl.19 (shared states, confirms, tables), acad-abl.9 (primitives), acad-abl.8 (admin shell and routes), acad-abl.20 (gap stances). Design calls follow design.md; feature answers cite backend decision numbers.

## D1. Routes, guard, and navigation

1. The admin section keeps the compact staff shell (acad-abl.8 Decision 5, acad-abl.19 D6.2). RoleRoute gates it on role ADMIN; direct URL hits render PermissionDenied (acad-abl.19 D1.4, acad-abl.13 rule 12).
2. Routes: `/admin/students` renders M1 accounts, `/admin/assignments` renders M2 caseloads, `/admin/rules` renders M3 rules, `/admin/settings` renders M4 staff and settings. The section index `/admin` redirects to `/admin/students` (design.md 6.1: admin landing is Accounts).
3. The rail items are Accounts, Caseloads, Rules, Settings. No Structure item: no org tree is stored and admin maintains none (decisions 15, 18; acad-abl.8 flag 2). No System Log item in v1: the contract exposes no endpoint (D6 below). The topbar bell stays as shared shell chrome; no notification slug names an admin recipient (decision 8).
4. Route names supersede acad-abl.8 Decision 3 in two places: `/admin/assignments` replaces `/admin/caseloads`, and the queue-aging threshold moves from `/admin/rules` to `/admin/settings` (flag 4). Paths live in src/config/paths.ts with getHref builders per that decision.

## D2. M1 accounts (/admin/students)

5. Data source: GET /api/admin/students with `search` and `per_page` (10, 20, 50, all; the param is documented here, so the settled page sizes map to it directly). The response is a UserList of User rows. No page jump control; the client follows links.next (acad-abl.19 D5.6).
6. Search model: one search input above the table. The server matches name, email, and student ID (verified StudentAccountService::search; the openapi description says name or student ID and the implementation adds email, flag 7 rider). The debounced term (300 ms) sits in the query key. No role, faculty, or status filter exists in the contract; the client builds none.
7. List columns: name, email, student ID (bidi-isolated, tabular-nums), status badge, actions menu. Status derives from the row: suspended_at set means Suspended (destructive badge), otherwise Active (neutral). Binding state renders beside the ID column value (decision 9). Headers do not sort: the contract takes no sort param and the server orders by name ascending; no aria-sort is set.
8. Account states from User fields, three orthogonal dimensions the row and panel both render:
   - Status: Active or Suspended (suspended_at).
   - Binding: bound (student_id set), pending (student_id null and pending_admin_at null), or ID check failed (pending_admin_at set, decision 2: the ID derives from the verified SIS email and admin correction overrides it; decision 21: identity comes from the SIS pull).
   - Assignment: advisor_id set or null. The contract carries no advisor name, so the UI shows an Assigned or Unassigned badge, never a name (flag 5).
9. Row click opens the account panel (acad-abl.19 D5.4). The panel is a feature component in src/features/admin/ with four blocks: identity (name, email, faculty as read-only context, decision 15), binding state with its actions, assignment with the reassign form (decision 19 in acad-9s3.16: single reassign lives on the student account page), and the danger zone.
10. Row and panel actions, each with its confirmation per the settled policy (acad-abl.19 D3):
    - Suspend: ConfirmDialog destructive. Body: "Suspension blocks login immediately and signs the student out. The account and its data stay." Confirm label "Suspend". Backend fact: suspend revokes tokens at once (StudentAccountService::suspend).
    - Reactivate: no dialog; the state change is visible and reversible.
    - Retry SIS check: no dialog; the button shows its own loading. Success applies the returned User with setQueryData. If the account stays held, the panel keeps the failed state and points at "Correct student ID". A 409 admin.binding_complete refreshes the row and toasts the one calm line (acad-abl.13 rule 14). A 503 verification.sis_unavailable renders the destructive Banner anatomy scoped to the panel, non-dismissible, with Retry (acad-abl.13 rule 17 pattern, panel scope because the list data itself is not stale).
    - Correct student ID: form in the panel, digits only, 1 to 20 (CorrectStudentIdInput pattern), RHF plus zod (acad-abl.13 rules 31 to 35). Submit runs through a ConfirmDialog primary: "This sets the student ID for this account. The ID cannot be edited again." Confirm label "Save student ID". The dialog exists because the guard is a one-way door: correctStudentId throws admin.binding_complete once the binding completes (verified StudentAccountService::assertBindingIncomplete), and no unbind endpoint exists.
    - Delete: ConfirmDialog destructive: "This deletes the student account and removes the student from their advisor's caseload. This cannot be undone." Confirm label "Delete account". No reason input: the endpoint takes no body.
    - Reassign: email input plus submit inside the panel, no dialog (single reassign is reversible, acad-abl.19 D3). The client lowercases and trims on submit (the server normalizes; ReassignStudentRequest). A 422 keyed advisor_email renders inline with the server text admin.reassign.unknown_advisor (acad-abl.13 rule 9). Success applies the returned user; the server notifies the student and both advisors (decision 18).
11. SIS-failure display: the binding block speaks about the check, never the student (PR-01, DS-ST-11). Held copy: "The student information system has no record for this account's derived ID. Correct the student ID or retry the check." Pending copy: "The student ID binding has not completed yet. Retry the check." The admin cannot distinguish the SIS failure variants beyond these two field states, and the UI invents no third.
12. Six states: loading renders SkeletonTableRows matching the columns (acad-abl.19 D5.3); empty renders EmptyState with search-aware copy: "No students match this search. Clear it or try another name or ID." and, with no rows at all, "No student accounts yet. Accounts appear when students sign up."; error renders ErrorState with Retry and the requestId line (acad-abl.19 D1.3); permission denied per rule 1; stale SIS N/A (platform data, not SIS datasets; the binding 503 uses the panel banner); window closed N/A.

## D3. M2 caseloads (/admin/assignments)

13. The contract has no assignments list endpoint; the surface reads GET /api/admin/students and renders the assignment dimension of the same rows. M1 and M2 share one query root, ['admin', 'students', { search, per_page }], so both surfaces show one truth (acad-abl.13 rules 20 to 22).
14. Columns: name, student ID, advisor assignment badge (Assigned or Unassigned), faculty. Row action "Reassign" opens the same account panel assignment block as M1; there is one reassign implementation in the feature (DP-05). No unassigned-only filter exists because the server takes no filter param and a client-side filter over one page would lie about the population; cut (DP-02).
15. Import flow. Primary action "Import CSV" opens a dialog with: a file picker accepting .csv and .txt up to 2048 KB (ImportAssignmentsInput description), client-side extension and size pre-checks with inline errors, and helper text: "CSV with student_id and advisor_email columns. One row per student."
16. Import confirmation: ConfirmDialog primary inside the flow: "Applied rows move students to the named advisors immediately. Rows that already carry the advisor stay unchanged." Confirm label "Import assignments" (acad-abl.19 D3: bulk movement confirms; decision 18: all-or-nothing).
17. Success renders ImportSummary honestly: "Import applied. {assigned} students moved. {unchanged} already carried their advisor." plus the settled success toast for the finished import (acad-abl.19 D2.2), then invalidates ['admin', 'students'].
18. Failure renders the 422 error report and applies nothing (decision 18; the rejected run leaves no audit event, the report is the record). Key mapping, verified in AssignmentService::import and the admin message catalog:
    - Key `file`: upload or header problems. Renders as a destructive banner at the top of the dialog with the server text.
