    - Keys `rows.{n}`: one failure per CSV row. Renders as a row-numbered table inside the dialog, sorted by row number, showing the first 20 rows plus "and {n} more rows". Each row shows the row number and the server message (missing student, missing advisor, unknown student with the value, unknown advisor with the value).
    The dialog stays open with the report; nothing applied, so there is no partial state to reconcile.
19. Six states: as M1 (rule 12) for the list, plus the dialog's own loading (button spinner, acad-abl.13 rule for button loading) and the error-report state of rule 18. Stale SIS and window closed N/A.

## D4. M3 rules (/admin/rules)

20. Scope: the surface edits University Rule texts only. The rules engine is backend-owned and the SIS owns every validation number (decision 17; acad-9s3.16 second amendment: the rules screen, if one remains, edits only the University Rule texts the AI prompt consumes). No parameter fields beyond UniversityRuleInput exist. The queue-aging threshold is not here; it lives in M4 (rule 25).
21. List: GET /api/admin/rules returns a plain array under data (UniversityRuleList), so no pagination. Columns: title_en, title_ar, updated_at. Row click opens the editor dialog. Primary action "New rule" opens the same dialog empty.
22. Editor dialog: four fields, title_en and title_ar (max 255), body_en and body_ar (required textareas), grouped under EN and AR labels because both pairs are required (UniversityRuleInput). Create POSTs and returns 201 with the envelope; update PUTs. The 422 keys title_en, title_ar, body_en, body_ar map inline under their fields (acad-abl.13 rules 9, 35). On success the client applies the returned rule into ['admin', 'rules'].
23. Delete: ConfirmDialog destructive: "This deletes the rule. The AI advisor stops quoting it immediately. This cannot be undone." Confirm label "Delete rule" (acad-abl.19 D3). No enable or disable toggle exists: UniversityRule carries no enabled field, so the client builds none (flag 3).
24. Source badges from foundation section 14 M4 and Q56 are dead here: the platform stores no validation parameters, the list has exactly one source, and a column with one value is noise (DP-02, decision 17). The M3 list renders no source column. The foundation doc correction rides the doc pass (flag 4).
25. Six states: loading renders skeleton rows; empty renders "No university rules yet. Add the first rule the AI advisor quotes."; error renders ErrorState with Retry; permission denied per rule 1; stale SIS and window closed N/A.

## D5. M4 staff and settings (/admin/settings)

26. Layout: two cards on one page, Staff accounts and Queue aging. One primary action per card (DS-L-02).
27. Staff creation form: name, email, password, role, faculty. Contract facts (CreateStaffInput, CreateStaffRequest): role enum is advisor, dean, vp, admin; password minimum 8; email unique and lowercased; faculty is required when the role is dean and prohibited for every other role (422 key faculty). The 422 keys name, email, password, role, faculty render inline (acad-abl.13 rules 9, 35).
28. Password semantics per decision 18: the admin enters the initial password; there is no generated password and no invite email. The admin never sets or sees a user password anywhere else; an admin password reset only triggers a reset email (acad-9s3.16 resolution, guards). The success confirmation (201) renders inline: "Staff account created. Share the initial password with {name} through a safe channel." The panel never echoes the password. The effect is visible in place, so no toast (acad-abl.19 D2.2).
29. Password reset action: available on the creation confirmation panel for the account just created, and anywhere else the client holds a staff id (which is nowhere else today, flag 2). ConfirmDialog primary: "This emails a password reset link to {email}." Confirm label "Send reset link". Success toasts the settled line for the sent reset (acad-abl.19 D2.2); the endpoint returns passwords.reset_link_sent.
30. Queue-aging threshold editor: GET /api/admin/settings/queue-aging-threshold seeds the form; PUT saves { days }, integer, minimum 1 (422 key days, inline). The control is a number input with the unit rendered as a suffix label "days". No confirmation dialog: it is the editor's own submit and the saved value renders in place.
31. Who sees the effect, stated under the editor: "Advisor queue rows and caseload rows flag aging past this threshold. Dean and VP aging metrics use the same value." Citations: decision 18 sets the threshold capability; decision 22 wires the advisor explorer aging flag and the governance aging metric to the admin-configured threshold; acad-abl.1 section 4 records that aging fires no notification, the UI reads the is_aging flags. design.md PR-13 and the QueueTable spec fix aging at 3+ days; decisions 18 and 22 amend that, and the doc pass corrects design.md (flag 6).
32. Org units stay read-only context: faculty renders as text on the staff form (dean role), in the M1 account panel, and as the M2 column. No tree, no editor, no unit records (decisions 15, 18; /admin/structure stays removed, verified: no org endpoint exists in openapi.json).
33. Six states: forms render with no fetch. The threshold card loads its value: skeleton input, ErrorState compact with Retry on failure. List-level states beyond that are N/A; permission denied per rule 1; stale SIS and window closed N/A.

## D6. M5 system log stance

34. The contract exposes no log or audit endpoint (verified: a path scan of openapi.json names no log or audit route). The audit catalog exists only server side (decision 18; acad-9s3.16 resolution: one append-only catalog, admin-only reader, CSV export with current filters). Client stance, following the acad-abl.20 pattern: accept and defer. No /admin/log route ships in v1 and the rail omits it (rule 3). The ask rides to the backend effort: a read endpoint with filters plus CSV export, for example GET /api/admin/audit-events. When it lands, M5 becomes a filtered table with an Export action reusing the D5 table system.

## D7. Cross-cutting decisions

35. Query keys and caching: ['admin', 'students', { search, per_page }] shared by M1 and M2, ['admin', 'rules'], ['admin', 'settings'] for the threshold. staleTime 5 minutes, no polling (acad-abl.13 rule 25). Every mutation invalidates the root of each entity it touches; account mutations apply the returned UserResource through setQueryData before invalidating, because the response is the server truth (acad-abl.13 rules 20, 23).
36. Forms: every admin form runs react-hook-form with a zod resolver beside its fetcher in src/features/admin/, mode onBlur, first errored field focused on failed submit, server errors merged with setError and winning (acad-abl.13 rules 31 to 35).
37. Copy: dictionary keys only, final in EN and AR before merge (DS-W-01). Errors follow DS-W-02: what happened, why, what to do. Confirm labels are verbs of three words or fewer (DS-W-04). Student IDs and advisor emails sit in the bidi isolate inside Arabic sentences (DS-L-05). Numerals stay Latin (DS-W-06). No em dashes anywhere (DS-W-05).
38. Tables: compact density from the shell, sticky header, tabular-nums, states replace the body (acad-abl.19 D5). Icon-only actions in the menu carry tooltips plus accessible names (acad-abl.9 D1 item 11).
39. Mock scenarios: the MSW set gains two named seeds beside the settled seven (acad-abl.13 rule 39): import-errors (422 with file and rows keys) and binding-incomplete (held and pending accounts in the students list). Tests route through MSW (rule 41).
40. Confirmation policy summary for this feature, one line each: confirm suspend, delete student, delete rule, import, correct student ID, send reset link; skip reactivate, retry SIS, reassign, threshold save, rule create and update.

## Flags for the owner

1. No system log endpoint exists (openapi.json path scan, 2026-10-01), so M5 cannot ship. The ask: an admin audit-event read endpoint with filters plus CSV export (D6). Until it lands, the rail carries four items.
2. The staff password-reset endpoint takes a staff id, but no staff list or lookup endpoint exists (acad-abl.20 item 5 accepted creation-only). The reset affordance therefore works only for accounts created in the same session. The ask: a staff list endpoint, or an email-addressed reset route. The same endpoint would let M1 and M2 show advisor names instead of an Assigned badge, and could power an advisor picker for reassign and import (rule 8, flag 5 in the body).
3. University Rule enable and disable has no contract field on UniversityRule, so the client builds no toggle. If the semantics are wanted, it needs a schema field and an openapi pass.
4. Doc maintenance pass: acad-abl.8 Decision 3 names /admin/caseloads and places the threshold on /admin/rules; this resolution sets /admin/assignments and moves the threshold to /admin/settings. Foundation section 14 M4 (source badges, SIS-synced values) and design.md PR-13 plus the QueueTable 3-day aging copy need the same corrections the backend decisions already settled.
5. Contract doc riders: openapi.json says the students search matches name or student ID while the implementation also matches email (StudentAccountService::search); the import 422 row keys rows.{n} are implementation keys the contract describes only as "keyed by row" (AssignmentService::import). Both descriptions should align with the implementation.
close_reason: Resolved: 40 numbered decisions for the four surviving admin surfaces (accounts, caseloads, rules, settings), routes and rail aligned to backend decision 18, M5 deferred for a missing endpoint, 5 owner flags

title: Cross-cutting UX system
description:
## Question

What shared UX system do all surfaces reuse?

## Context

The six mandatory screen states (loading, empty, error, permission denied, stale SIS, window closed) need shared components. Plus: toasts, confirm dialogs, the notification center, table conventions under the two densities (student spacious, staff compact), dark mode and density switching, i18n and RTL application per the "i18n and RTL approach" resolution, and accessibility conformance testing (DS-A rules; the Storybook a11y addon is installed). Input: the constraint digest resolution.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling; consult ui-ux-pro-max and impeccable per design.md section 10.

## Record

The shared-component list with their props and states, plus the conventions as numbered rules.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.19 (wayfinder:grilling), Cross-cutting UX system. Sources: design.md sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and Appendix B; zoomed resolutions acad-abl.1 (constraint digest), acad-abl.6 (i18n/RTL), acad-abl.8 (skeleton), acad-abl.9 (primitives), acad-abl.13 (conventions); backend map acad-9s3 (decision 8 notifications via acad-9s3.14, decisions 10, 14, 19, 23 for destructive actions); openapi.json endpoints and Notification schema; ui-ux-pro-max and impeccable (craft floor) for craft judgment. Component locations follow acad-abl.8 Decision 2: shared domain components live in src/components/domain/ (owner approval pending there), primitives in src/components/ui/.

## D1. Shared state components and their APIs

Every screen implements all six states (DS-ST-08). The state layer is six components; the first three are ui/ primitives or compositions on them, the last three are domain components in src/components/domain/.

D1.1 Loading. Skeletons only for area loads (design.md 4.3); no full-screen spinner. Build Skeleton, SkeletonText, SkeletonTableRows, SkeletonCard in src/components/ui/skeleton/ per acad-abl.9 item 5 (animate-pulse on bg-muted rounded-md). API: Skeleton takes className only; SkeletonTableRows takes rows: number and columnSkeletons: ReactNode so the skeleton matches the real column shape. Page-level: route skeletons render topbar plus shell-shaped skeleton (4.3). Panel-level: drawers and cards render line-shaped skeletons. Timing per DS-M-05 and DS-ST-03: feedback within 100ms (button spinner), skeletons for waits over 300ms. Button-level loading stays Spinner plus preserved label with aria-busy (4.1). Loading regions set aria-busy (DS-A-09).

D1.2 EmptyState. ui/ primitive per acad-abl.9 item 6 and design.md 5.3. API: { icon?: LucideIcon (default 24px), title: string, description?: string (max 2 lines), action?: { label: string; onClick: () => void } }. One action maximum (5.3). Copy per DS-W-07: names the missing thing and the first step; copy strings come from the feature that renders it, from the dictionary (DS-W-01). Page-level: the route body renders it when the list or entity is absent. Panel-level: drawers and lists render the same component with the compact variant prop (smaller icon 20px). The dedicated edge states (no advisor assigned, empty queue, empty caseload, empty chat) are EmptyState instances with feature copy, not new components.

D1.3 ErrorState (with retry). A shared composition on the Banner anatomy, not a new primitive. API: { title?: string (default from dictionary key errors.loadFailed), message: string (server text when one exists, per acad-abl.13 rule 19), onRetry?: () => void, requestId?: string (printed as a muted reference line, acad-abl.13 rule 5), compact?: boolean }. Renders icon + title + body + Retry button; Retry is the only recovery affordance; global defaults set retry false (acad-abl.13 rule 24), so Retry calls queryClient refetch for the failed root key. Page-level: renders as the page body when the primary fetch fails. Panel-level: compact variant inside drawers, cards, and table bodies. Copy pattern DS-W-02: what happened, why, what to do. Never alert(), never raw status codes.

D1.4 PermissionDenied. Domain component in src/components/domain/permission-denied/. Calm panel, not an error aesthetic (4.3). API: { audience: string (dictionary key naming the intended role, e.g. roles.advisor), message?: string, backTo: { label: string; href: string } }. Renders: one-line role reminder plus one way back ("This area is for advisors. Go to your dashboard."). Renders in exactly two places: the RoleRoute guard on direct URL hits (acad-abl.8 Decision 4) and the 403 mapping (acad-abl.13 rule 12). Never a toast, never destructive styling.

D1.5 StaleSisBanner. Banner variant stale (5.3), non-dismissible, never blocking (acad-abl.1 section 7). API: { stale: { identity?: boolean; academic_record?: boolean; course_catalog?: boolean }, asOf: string | Date (last_synced_at), onRetry?: () => void }. Body renders "Data as of {asOf}." via src/lib/i18n/format.ts (dayjs, Africa/Cairo, 24h, Latin numerals per acad-abl.6 and acad-abl.9 D4); when named datasets are stale the body lists them; always offers Retry, which refetches ['academic-record'] (acad-abl.13 rule 27). Placement: page-level above the affected content (S4 profile, prereq map, plan surfaces reading SIS data). One banner per page even when several datasets are stale. Content below stays visible and interactive. Never triggers refetch loops; the user pulls (acad-abl.13 rule 27).

D1.6 WindowClosed. Banner variant window-closed (5.3), non-dismissible, replaces the submit CTA area (4.3). Honest copy, no countdown, no dates the contract cannot supply: "Registration is closed. Your approved plan waits for the next window." (4.3 copy pattern; acad-abl.1 contradiction 8: no window dates exist in the contract). API: { reason?: 'window_closed' | 'window_unavailable' } mapping to two dictionary lines: closed (422 plan.window_closed) and unavailable (503 plan.window_unavailable: "Registration status is unavailable right now. Retry in a moment."). Placement: at the submit gate next to the CTA in the Plan Builder and on My Plan's submit affordance (acad-abl.13 rule 10). The builder stays readable and editable; only submission blocks (acad-abl.1: building is never window-gated). Also renders when the user follows a window notification deep link and submission is blocked.

## D2. Toast system

The toast layer is the existing src/components/ui/notifications store (acad-abl.9: no separate toast primitive). It gets one in-place upgrade: retokenize its raw colors to the 3.3 status pairs (DS-C-01; the current text-blue-500 and friends are violations to fix when the component is touched), render from the inline-end in RTL, cap the stack at three, and auto-dismiss after 5 seconds (ui-ux-pro-max feedback rule; successful confirmations never linger). role="alert" on error and warning toasts, polite announce for success.

D2.1 Which statuses toast (fixed by acad-abl.13): 401 never toasts (rule 6), 403 never toasts (rule 12), 429 quota renders inline in chat (rule 15), 422 toasts only as fallback when the key matches no visible field (rule 9), 409 toasts the one calm line "That action is no longer available. Your view is up to date." (rule 14). Any undocumented 5xx renders the global destructive Banner, not a toast (rule 17).

D2.2 Success toasts are the exception, not the rule (DP-02): when the result is visible in place (plan edits applied through setQueryData, queue row state change after approve or return), no toast. Toast success only when the effect lands off-screen: password reset link sent, staff password reset sent, SIS binding retry queued, assignments import finished, CSV export generated. One dictionary line each, verb-anchored to the action.

D2.3 Copy: DS-W-01 dictionary only, DS-W-02 order, verb buttons, no emoji (DS-W-05). Toasts never carry the only copy of something important (DS-A-09); anything that matters also renders inline or as a Banner.

D2.4 RTL: the toast stack anchors to the logical inline-end (start-* / end-* utilities, no left/right), text-start alignment, dismiss icon needs no flip, directional icons in toasts flip per D7. z-toast z-[60] (DS-Z-01).

## D3. Confirm dialogs

ConfirmDialog is ui/ primitive acad-abl.9 item 8, built on the existing dialog. Spec per design.md 5.3: title, body stating the consequence, cancel plus confirm; confirm label is verb-specific ("Discard plan", never "OK"); destructive confirms use the destructive variant; focus starts on cancel; ESC closes; focus returns to the trigger (DS-A-02). API: { title: string, body: string, confirmLabel: string, cancelLabel?: string, variant?: 'destructive' | 'primary', onConfirm: () => Promise<void> (button shows its own loading, closes on success) }.

The destructive and consequential actions, from the contract (openapi.json) with backend map citations:

| Action | Endpoint | Dialog or not | Body states the consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discard plan (student, draft or returned) | POST /api/plan/discard (decision 10) | Confirm, destructive | "This plan is discarded for good. Start a new plan when you are ready." |
| Withdraw plan (student, terminal for the term) | POST /api/plan/withdraw (decision 3 area) | Confirm, destructive | Names that the plan cannot come back this term |
| Seen (student, on Returned) | POST /api/plan/seen | Confirm, primary | "This marks the feedback as read and unlocks editing." (5.4 SeenButton) |
| Delete visit request (initiator, while Proposed) | DELETE /api/visit-requests/{id} (decision 23) | Confirm, destructive | "This removes the request. You can raise a new one." |
| Remove plan course line (student, draft) | DELETE /api/plan/courses/{code} | No dialog | Reversible in one click from the same picker; a confirm would tax the builder loop (DP-02) |
| Approve plan (advisor, locks permanently) | POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/approve (decision 3) | Confirm, primary | "Approval locks the plan for this term." |
| Return plan (advisor, mandatory reason) | POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/return (decision 11) | Confirm inside the drawer after the reason textarea passes validation; body restates "The plan returns to the student and editing reopens." |
| Mark visit done (advisor) | POST /api/advisor/visit-requests/{id}/done (decision 23) | No dialog | Visible state change on the row; reversible importance is low, copy states it inline |
| Republish availability (advisor) | PUT /api/advisor/availability | No dialog | It is the editor's normal save; the editor shows the full resulting set |
| Delete student account (admin) | DELETE /api/admin/students/{student} | Confirm, destructive, restates the student's name | Account and caseload assignment are removed |
| Suspend student account (admin) | POST .../suspend | Confirm, destructive | Login is blocked until reactivation |
| Reactivate (admin) | POST .../reactivate | No dialog | Non-destructive restore |
| Delete university rule (admin) | DELETE /api/admin/rules/{rule} | Confirm, destructive | The rule disappears from the rules list |
| Import assignments CSV (admin) | POST /api/admin/assignments/import | Confirm inside the import dialog, restating file name and advisor column mapping | Bulk reassignment fires advisor_changed and caseload notifications (decision 8) |
| Reassign one student (admin) | POST /api/admin/assignments/{student}/reassign | No dialog | Reversible single-row edit; result visible in the table |

Pattern: confirm whenever the action is irreversible or terminal; skip when the effect is visible, reversible, and part of a normal edit loop. Every dialog body passes DS-W-02 order and the no-label test (PR-01, DS-W-03).

## D4. Notification center

Domain component in src/features/notifications/ (acad-abl.8 Decision 2); the topbar bell is part of app-shell. The 9 slugs and recipients come from acad-abl.1 section 4 (contract NotificationSlug; backend map decision 8, acad-9s3.14). The center renders server-localized title and body and never invents channels.

D4.1 Item anatomy (5.4 NotificationCenter/NotificationItem plus contract fields): unread dot (aria-hidden, state-submitted blue dot is banned there; use --primary) + icon by slug family (plan returned/approved: file-check and lock; advisor_changed and caseload pair: user arrows, flips per D7; window pair: calendar-clock; visit pair: calendar-plus/calendar-check) + title + body + absolute time (created_at through format.ts, 24h, Latin numerals, DS-W-06). The whole item is one button when it navigates. Read items drop the dot and dim the title weight.

D4.2 Read semantics: opening an item fires POST read with the optimistic pattern (acad-abl.13 rule 28: snapshot in onMutate, restore in onError, refetch in onSettled). Read-all button at the list top fires POST read-all, same pattern. Navigation happens after the read call is dispatched, not awaited.

D4.3 Unread count: unread_count from the poll response drives the topbar badge; the badge carries an aria-label "{n} unread notifications" and updates in a polite live region (DS-A-09, DS-ST-06).

D4.4 Polling: 30 second refetchInterval in the foreground, paused when the tab hides (acad-abl.13 rule 26). No SSE for notifications (decision 8).

D4.5 deep_link route convention. The contract carries deep_link as an unformatted nullable string (acad-abl.13 flag). Client convention until the format lands: the center routes by slug through one fixed table, the only deep_link consumer, in src/features/notifications/routes.ts. Table: plan_returned and plan_approved to /app/plan; advisor_changed to /app/plan; caseload_student_added and caseload_student_removed to /advisor/students; window_opened and window_deadline_nearing to /app/builder; visit_requested to /app/profile for students and /advisor/meetings for advisors (the receiving party per acad-abl.1); visit_slots_provided to /app/profile. A null or unknown deep_link falls back to the role's notifications page. When the backend later fixes the format, only this table changes.

D4.6 List states: loading renders skeleton rows matching the item shape; empty renders EmptyState ("No notifications yet. Plan and visit updates will appear here."); error renders ErrorState compact. Newest first; no tabs, no channels (DP-02, PR-05 in-app only).

## D5. Table system

The existing table plus pagination gets the in-place upgrade from acad-abl.9 (dense mode, tabular-nums, sticky header, aria-sort, page sizes 10/20/50/All).

D5.1 Two densities on one component. Table reads a density from a shell-provided React context (TableDensityProvider mounted by app-shell): spacious for the student shell (py-3 cells, text-sm), compact for the four staff shells (px-3 py-2, text-sm with text-2xs meta per 3.7). A density prop overrides the context for tests and stories. No third density (DP-05).

D5.2 Sticky header: thead th sticky top-0 z-sticky bg-card; the only allowed shadow-xs (DS-R-02); a single rule under the header row, no vertical cell borders (DS-R-03).

D5.3 States replace the body, never overlay it: loading renders SkeletonTableRows matching the real columns; empty renders EmptyState in a full-width tbody row; error renders ErrorState compact. Overlays that float over stale rows are banned: they lie about what the user is looking at (DP-09).

D5.4 Row selection: no checkbox multi-select exists in v1 (acad-abl.9: no surface names one). Rows navigate: the queue row opens ReviewDrawer (5.4), admin account rows open the account panel. The row is clickable with a real focusable control carrying an accessible name; the open row gets aria-selected or aria-current plus the 4.1 selected treatment. Sortable headers set aria-sort (5.2). Numeric cells right-align at the inline end with tabular-nums (DS-C-11, DS-R-03).

D5.5 RTL: cells, sort icons, and pagination chevrons mirror through logical properties and icon flips (D7); numeric columns keep Latin numerals at the inline end (DS-T-03). Wide tables sit in an overflow-x-auto wrapper; never break the page layout (ui-ux-pro-max responsive rule).

D5.6 Pagination: page sizes 10/20/50/All; the client follows links.next when present because no page query parameter is documented (acad-abl.13 flag, stands until the contract answers).

## D6. Theme and density switching

D6.1 Dark mode is class-strategy on documentElement (Appendix B .dark block; DS-C-03: a token flip, never per-class improvisation). prefers-color-scheme seeds the initial theme when nothing is stored (DS-A-07). An inline boot script in index.html applies the stored or seeded class before React mounts so first paint never flashes. The Zustand-persisted theme store (5.2: theme via Zustand store + documentElement class; key advaisor.theme) holds 'light' | 'dark' | 'system'; ThemeToggle in the topbar cycles it (5.3) and shows the current state in its accessible name.

D6.2 Density is not a user preference. The role shell decides it (acad-abl.8 Decision 5): spacious for students, compact for the four staff roles, 44px touch targets on touch viewports regardless (DS-S-01, 36px staff controls only behind pointer: fine and lg). Nothing persists.

D6.3 Persistence is per device for both theme and language; the server language_preference seeds language only and never receives toggles back until a PATCH endpoint exists (acad-abl.6; backend gap).

## D7. RTL application rules

D7.1 dir on <html> drives everything (DS-L-03, acad-abl.6). Logical properties everywhere (ps/pe, ms/me, start/end, text-start/text-end); physical pl/pr/ml/mr/left/right are banned in src/components/** and the ESLint guard from acad-abl.6 enforces it. rtl:/ltr: variants are the exception path, for directional icon flips only.

D7.2 Icon flip list. Flip under RTL: ChevronRight, ChevronLeft, ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, ArrowUpRight, ArrowDownRight, ChevronsRight, ChevronsLeft, LogOut, ExternalLink, and lucide's other marked flip-ables; when unclear, flip (DS-L-04). Never flip: bell, calendar, lock, plus, trash, x, check, search, settings, user icons. Vertical chevrons (ChevronDown, ChevronUp) never flip. Flip with rtl:-scale-x-100.

D7.3 Numerals and embedded Latin. src/lib/i18n/format.ts is the single formatting entry point: Intl.NumberFormat('ar-EG-u-nu-latn'), the dayjs ar locale clone without digit postformat, 24h times (acad-abl.6). i18next interpolation receives pre-formatted strings. Course codes and other Latin tokens inside Arabic sentences sit in the BidiCode isolate wrapper (DS-L-05). Numeric table cells keep tabular-nums (DS-C-11).

D7.4 The key-parity vitest test (en and ar namespaces) and the design review gate (both directions, section 0) are the enforcement points; a component that renders without passing both directions is not done.

## D8. Accessibility conformance testing

What runs in CI, under the DS-A rules:

D8.1 eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y on every file: existing gate, zero new warnings (section 9 item 18). This is the DS-A-03/DS-A-04 static floor.

D8.2 Vitest plus Testing Library on every ui/ and domain state component (DS-CP-03): assert semantics, not pixels. The shared suite asserts: skeletons set aria-busy on the region, EmptyState and ErrorState expose role and text association, PermissionDenied names the audience and carries a working way back, banners are non-dismissible and announce politely, ConfirmDialog focus order (cancel first, trap, return to trigger), notification items expose read state, tables set aria-sort and aria-selected. No new dependency needed.

D8.3 Storybook a11y addon: pending install (needs DS-G-07 approval). Once installed, every story runs the addon check and a CI test-runner pass; a violation fails the gate (DS-CP-03 names the addon check as part of done).

D8.4 Playwright axe on the six states: the MSW scenario set already covers them (acad-abl.13 rule 39: happy, empty, error, permission-denied, stale-sis, registration-closed, plus quota-exhausted). Each e2e spec navigates to one representative route per scenario and runs an axe scan against WCAG 2.1 AA (DS-A-01). The keyboard flows for the two hardest surfaces, Builder and queue, run as Playwright keyboard specs per DS-A-02. axe in Playwright uses axe-playwright or the playwright axe package and needs the same DS-G-07 approval at e2e setup.

D8.5 jest-axe inside vitest is an option, not a decision: it would duplicate D8.1 and D8.3 for a per-test cost. Skip it unless D8.3 slips.

## Flags for the owner

1. deep_link format is undefined in the contract (acad-abl.13 flag 2; acad-abl.20 in progress): the slug-to-route table in D4.5 is the client convention and the single point of change. The backend should either document deep_link's shape or drop the field in favor of slug-based client routing.
2. No window dates exist in the contract (acad-abl.1 contradiction 8): WindowClosed cannot show dates or a countdown, and the D1.6 copy stays date-free. A current-term read endpoint would unlock both.
3. Storybook a11y addon install (D8.3) and the Playwright axe package (D8.4) need DS-G-07 approval before they land.
4. src/components/domain/ still needs the owner's standing approval recorded on acad-abl.8 (its flag 6); D1.4 through D1.6 and D4 assume it.
5. The toast layer retokenization (D2) touches an existing ui/ component's raw colors; it is a DS-C-01 fix, but schedule it with the first feature that toasts.
close_reason: Shared UX system decided: six state components (Skeleton set, EmptyState, ErrorState, PermissionDenied, StaleSisBanner, WindowClosed) with fixed APIs and placements, toast policy on the existing notifications layer, 15-action confirm-dialog table, notification center with slug-to-route table and 30s polling, two-density table system, class-strategy dark mode, RTL flip list, and the four CI a11y gates

title: Student surfaces S1-S6
description:
## Question

What exactly does each student surface show and do across all plan states, including the plan builder's look and behavior?

## Context

S1 dashboard, S2 my plan, S3 builder, S4 profile, S5 chat (decided separately in "AI chat surface"), S6 notifications. Input: the "Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions" resolution. Decide per surface: content, actions, the six screen states (loading, empty, error, denied, stale SIS, window closed), submit/withdraw/discard confirmations, comments and seen UX, and the builder interaction: course list per semester, add/edit/remove flows, the validation panel for V1–V6, the prerequisite map, and the plan state chip (8 states). design.md 6.2 fixes routes and key components. Raise fidelity with the prototype skill if the owner prefers reacting to an artifact.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling; consult ui-ux-pro-max and impeccable per design.md section 10.

## Record

Per-surface numbered decisions, including the builder interaction model.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.14 (wayfinder:grilling), student surfaces S1 dashboard, S2 my plan, S3 builder, S4 profile, S6 notifications. S5 chat is decided separately in acad-abl.15 and stays out of scope here. Sources: design.md 3, 4, 5, 6.2, 8; docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md 2, 7, 12, 14, 15, 16; zoomed resolutions acad-abl.1 (digest), acad-abl.8 (routes and shells), acad-abl.9 (primitives), acad-abl.13 (conventions), acad-abl.19 (cross-cutting UX), acad-abl.20 (contract gaps); backend map acad-9s3 and children acad-9s3.3, acad-9s3.4, acad-9s3.5, acad-9s3.6, acad-9s3.8, acad-9s3.9, acad-9s3.12; openapi.json. Craft judgment comes from ui-ux-pro-max and the impeccable craft floor; structure follows design.md. Every surface implements the six screen states through the shared components of acad-abl.19 D1.

## Cross-surface decisions

C1. Plan state renders only through PlanStateChip (DS-ST-04) with the acad-abl.9 D3 token map for the 8 settled states (acad-9s3.3). The contract's ninth value, discarded, renders as a terminal record state on state-closed tokens with its own label and slate dot (acad-abl.20 item 10; map decision 10).

C2. One primary action per screen (DS-L-02, DP-03). Secondary destructive actions (withdraw, discard) collapse into a header "More actions" dropdown on S2; the builder header carries Discard as its one destructive control.

C3. Every plan mutation applies the server response with setQueryData(['plan'], serverPlan) and never runs optimistic (acad-abl.13 rules 23 and 29; map decision 19 mutation surface).

C4. Credit numbers are omitted wherever the contract cannot supply them: total_credit_hours is always 0 and PlannedCourse carries no credits (acad-abl.20 item 18). Surfaces render course counts instead of a fake zero.

C5. The client computes no validation rule (acad-abl.20 item 12; map decision 17, acad-9s3.5). Check results render only from the four 422 keys after the server reports them: allowance, map_membership, prerequisite_chain, window.

C6. Window state is never data-driven because no window dates exist in the contract (acad-abl.20 item 17). WindowClosed renders only on the submit 422 window key, the 503 plan.window_unavailable, or a window notification deep link with submission blocked (acad-abl.19 D1.6).

C7. Copy follows DS-W: errors state what happened, why, what to do; buttons are verbs; every string sits in the dictionary in EN and AR (DS-W-01, DS-W-02, DS-W-04). Messages never label the student (PR-01, DS-ST-11).

## S1 dashboard (/app)

1. Composition: page header with the term context line, then the current plan card (PlanCard), then at most one banner region. No KPI row, no vanity metrics, and no notification digest section: the dashboard exists to move the plan forward (foundation 2, principle 3), and the topbar bell plus S6 carry notifications (DP-02).
2. PlanCard content: term and program identity, PlanStateChip, one course count line ("4 courses planned"), and exactly one primary CTA picked by state. The design.md 5.4 credit progress line is cut under C4.
3. No DraftPlanCard and no chat card. The AI edits the one plan through tools and produces no draft artifact (map decision 13; acad-abl.8 flag 3; foundation 12 as amended). AI chat lives in the student rail only (PR-08).
4. CTA per state, from foundation 15's student column adapted to the 8 settled states (acad-9s3.3):

   | Plan state | Primary CTA | Context line |
   |---|---|---|
   | Draft | Resume in builder, to /app/builder | "Not submitted yet." |
   | Submitted | View plan, to /app/plan | "Waiting for {advisor}." |
   | Under Review | View plan, to /app/plan | "Your advisor is reviewing." Plus a visit badge when the session cache holds an open request. |
   | Returned (locked) | Review feedback, to /app/plan | "Your advisor returned your plan with comments." |
   | Approved (locked) | none | "Approved. Register your courses in the SIS." |
   | Expired | none | "The registration window closed before your plan was approved." |
   | Closed | none | "This term's plan cycle is closed." |
   | Withdrawn | none | "Your plan was withdrawn for this term." Terminal for the semester (foundation 7.2, transition 12). |
   | Discarded | Start a new plan, to /app/builder | "Your previous plan was discarded." A new plan may follow (map decision 10). |

5. No plan cached: EmptyState "No plan for {term} yet. Start in the Plan Builder." with one action, "Start your plan", routing to /app/builder. Creation happens there (S3 decision 29).
6. No advisor assigned (me.advisor_id null): a calm blocking banner, "You have no assigned advisor yet. The administration office assigns advisors." The builder entry renders disabled with that reason beside it (foundation 15 edge states; POST /api/plan answers 409 plan.advisor_missing).
7. Window: no countdown and no window section (acad-abl.20 item 17 cuts the foundation 14 countdown). WindowClosed renders only under C6 triggers.
8. The advisor name in "Waiting for {advisor}" comes from GET /api/advisor/profile (the ['advisor-profile'] root, acad-abl.13 rule 22). While that query has no data the line falls back to "Waiting for your advisor."
9. Six states: loading is the route skeleton, topbar plus shell shape (D1.1). Empty is decision 5. Error is ErrorState with Retry as the page body (D1.3). Denied is PermissionDenied with backTo the dashboard (D1.4). Stale-SIS is N/A because the dashboard renders no SIS-backed data (documented per DS-ST-08). Window-closed is only under C6 triggers, else N/A.

## S2 my plan (/app/plan)

10. Composition: page header "My Plan" with the term context and the banner-size PlanStateChip, then the return-reason banner when returned, then the plan document, then the comment thread.
11. No semester grouping inside the plan. One plan binds to one term and Plan.courses is a flat list keyed by course_code (acad-9s3.6 baseline; openapi Plan). The term renders in the header. The contract serves no plan history endpoint, so S2 shows the current term only (flag 5).
12. Course lines render through PlanLine: course code in a bidi isolate (DS-L-05), title joined from the academic-record prerequisite_map (acad-abl.20 item 18), group, section. No credits and no client-computed validity icon; validity marks appear only from server 422 results (C4, C5).
13. Return reason prominence: when status is returned, Plan.return_reason renders verbatim in a plan-state banner on state-returned tokens (DS-C-09) at the top of the body, above the lines. Product truth shows the returned student sees the comment and the Seen CTA together (foundation 15, Returned row). Nothing hides behind Seen: design.md 4.2's "comments become visible after Seen" phrasing yields to the product doc and the settled transition (acad-9s3.12: Seen is the student's acknowledgment that returns the plan to Draft).
14. Comment thread: GET /api/plan/comments renders below the lines, oldest first, each with author and created_at through format.ts (DS-W-06). The student has no reply affordance (PR-06; foundation 16, J2 resubmits with no note). Comments unread since the last return carry the crimson-100 tint background plus a "New" text badge until Seen is pressed (color paired with text per DS-C-08; design.md 5.4 unread treatment rendered as a tint, not a thick border).
15. Seen: SeenButton per design.md 5.4, visible only on returned plans. ConfirmDialog, primary variant: "This marks the feedback as read and unlocks editing for this plan." (acad-abl.19 D3). On success the server plan replaces the cache (C3), the chip animates to draft (DS-ST-06), and editing reopens in the builder.
16. Actions per state, from the digest transition table:
    - Draft: Submit is the primary header action with no confirm dialog (acad-abl.19 D3 lists no dialog for submit; the visible state change is the confirmation). The "More actions" dropdown holds Withdraw plan and Discard plan, both destructive confirms. Withdraw body: "This plan is withdrawn for {term}. You cannot submit another plan this term." Discard body: "This plan is discarded. You can start a new plan for {term}."
    - Returned: Seen primary (decision 15); Discard secondary in the dropdown, because POST /api/plan/discard accepts a draft or returned plan (digest section 1).
    - Submitted and Under Review: no actions; the context line only.
    - Approved: no actions; guidance "Register your courses in the SIS." The platform never registers anyone (acad-9s3.3 rationale).
    - Expired, Closed, Withdrawn, Discarded: terminal notice, no actions.
17. Submit failure surfaces (acad-abl.13 rule 10): the 422 window key renders WindowClosed at the CTA. allowance, map_membership, and prerequisite_chain render per line under PlanLine plus a summary ValidationPanel above the lines, each entry carrying the server text. A closing line links to the builder: "Edit in the Plan Builder to fix these." The 503 service slugs render the destructive banner with Retry at the CTA (rule 17).
18. Staleness: StaleSisBanner above the document when ['academic-record'] reports stale, because line titles come from it. Retry refetches that root (D1.5, acad-abl.13 rule 27).
19. Six states: loading is the header plus line skeletons. Empty: a null plan renders EmptyState "No plan for {term} yet." with one action to /app/builder. Error is ErrorState with Retry as the page body. Denied is PermissionDenied. Stale-SIS is decision 18. Window-closed sits at the submit affordance under C6 triggers only.

## S3 builder (/app/builder)

20. Interaction model: a single scrolling document, not semester tabs. The plan is one term with a flat course list, so tabs would add structure the data does not have (DP-02). Page order: add bar on top, the line list under it, the validation summary panel next, and the submit area at the end.
21. Course add: the combobox primitive (acad-abl.9 item 13) in a persistent "Add a course" bar. The search corpus is the student's prerequisite_map from GET /api/academic-record, filtered client-side (acad-abl.9 flag 5; no catalog endpoint exists). Rows show code, title, and the map state (completed, planned, eligible, locked) as a badge (acad-9s3.8). The client filters nothing by eligibility and invents no rule: the server stays the authority, and 422 plan.out_of_map surfaces under the line (map decision 19; acad-abl.13 rule 10). Entries already on the plan drop out of the list. Empty result copy: "No courses in your course map match "{query}"."
22. Line edit is inline, not a drawer. A line's only editable fields are group and section (UpdatePlanCourseInput), so each line renders two small selects wired to PATCH /api/plan/courses/{courseCode}. The course code is the row key and never edits; changing courses means remove and re-add. Remove carries no confirm because it is reversible in one action (acad-abl.19 D3). No drawer and no modal: the craft floor refuses panels for tasks that need neither interruption nor protected focus.
23. No reason field exists for students: the builder never renders or sends one (map decision 19; 422 plan.reason_forbidden; acad-abl.13 rule 33).
24. Draft persistence is server-backed. Every add, update, and remove is a live mutation and the response replaces the plan cache (C3, acad-abl.13 rule 29). There is no save button, no client-only staging area, and the draft survives a reload. In-flight rows show feedback within 100ms (DS-M-05).
25. Validation panel behavior is honest about the contract: the three checks run at submission and again at approval only (map decision 17), so nothing validates live pre-submit. The panel renders advisory plan.warnings, labeled advisory and never blocking (digest section 2), plus per-line mutation errors as they occur. Pre-submit it shows one helper line: "Your plan is checked when you submit." After a failed submit the panel lists the returned errors grouped by line (DS-ST-09) with jump-to-line links, the header shows the count, and Submit stays disabled with "Resolve {n} issues to submit." until a course mutation clears the stale results.
26. Submit is never client-disabled for unknown violations. It is disabled only while the plan is empty, while a mutation is in flight, or while decision 25's post-submit errors stand. This corrects design.md 4.4's live-validation premise per acad-abl.20 item 12; the hard block sits at the submit gate.
27. Prerequisite display without a catalog endpoint: each line can expand to list its prerequisite codes from the map entry, bidi-isolated, plain text. No resolved or unresolved color: the chain check resolves on passed attempts with attempted-final semantics the client cannot reproduce (acad-9s3.5), so the caption reads "The check result shows after submit." The S4 PrereqMap stays the visual place for SIS-assigned states (acad-9s3.8).
28. Submit and discard: Submit posts once and the state change is the confirmation, no dialog (acad-abl.19 D3). Discard sits in the header as the single destructive control with its confirm dialog (draft scope inside the builder).
29. Entry states: with no plan, the builder renders EmptyState "No plan for {term} yet." with the primary action "Start your plan", which POSTs /api/plan. A 409 plan.advisor_missing renders the calm no-advisor banner from S1 decision 6 and no editor. With a plan in a non-draft state, the lines render read-only (DS-ST-05) with a state context line; mutation affordances render only in Draft. A returned plan shows "Review your feedback first." linking to /app/plan.
30. Six states: loading is the add bar plus three line skeletons. Empty has two designs: no plan (decision 29) and a plan with zero courses, "Your plan is empty. Add your first course." Error is ErrorState with Retry as the page body. Denied is PermissionDenied. Stale-SIS is StaleSisBanner above the list, because titles and the search corpus come from the academic record; content stays interactive (D1.5). Window-closed is WindowClosed at the submit CTA under C6 triggers; the builder stays readable and editable because building is never window-gated (map decision 11, acad-9s3.4).

## S4 profile (/app/profile)

31. The page is read-only (acad-abl.20 item 6): identity and academic data are SIS-owned (map decision 21) and no profile-write endpoint exists. No edit affordance anywhere. Language preference is the device-local topbar toggle (acad-abl.6), never a profile field.
32. Composition top to bottom: identity card (avatar initials, name, student ID, email, faculty from GET /api/me, curriculum year level from the academic record); two kpi-cards, CGPA as served on the 4.0 scale (acad-9s3.7) and remaining credit hours from remaining_requirements rendered verbatim in the student's language (acad-9s3.8: no local model); then the prerequisite map, current enrollments, and course history.
33. Prerequisite map: the PrereqMap domain component (design.md 5.4) renders prerequisite_map with the four SIS-assigned states mapped to node styles: completed emerald, planned blue, eligible amber, locked slate (acad-9s3.8). The SVG carries a visually-hidden list alternative (DS-A-03); at 390px it scrolls horizontally with snap.
34. Current enrollments render as their own section without grades (acad-9s3.8). Course history renders every finished attempt, passed or failed, with code, title, term, and grade in the spacious student table (acad-9s3.8; no repeat features, PR-14). Empty sections render EmptyState compact; an empty map renders "Your course map is not available yet." with a Retry action.
35. Advisor line: a small card naming the assigned advisor from GET /api/advisor/profile with published availability. When no advisor is assigned it renders the calm no-advisor line from S1 decision 6.
36. Six states: loading is section skeletons matching the final layout. Empty is decision 34. Error is ErrorState with Retry as the page body. Denied is PermissionDenied. Stale-SIS is StaleSisBanner above all content, since the whole page is SIS data (D1.5). Window-closed is N/A: the page has no submit affordance (documented per DS-ST-08).

## S6 notifications (/app/notifications)

37. Page-level composition only; item behavior is acad-abl.19 D4. The page is the header "Notifications", the "Mark all as read" action at the list top when unread_count is above zero, and the list, newest first. No tabs and no channels (DP-02, PR-05).
38. Routing follows the acad-abl.20 item 7 screen map, the later resolution keyed on the implemented deep_link object {screen, ...}; it supersedes the D4.5 slug table where the two differ. For students: plan to /app/plan, advisor to /app, visit to /app until GET /api/visit-requests lands. A null or unknown deep_link falls back to /app.
39. Six states: loading is skeleton rows matching the item shape (D4.6). Empty is "No notifications yet. Plan and visit updates will appear here." Error is ErrorState compact. Denied is PermissionDenied. Stale-SIS is N/A: no SIS data. Window-closed is N/A. Polling stays on the D4.4 30-second foreground interval.

## Flags for the owner

1. Credits (acad-abl.20 item 18 handoff): until the backend populates Plan.total_credit_hours or adds credits to PlannedCourse, S1 and S2 render course counts and omit every credit number.
2. Window dates (acad-abl.20 item 17 handoff): the dashboard countdown stays cut and WindowClosed copy stays date-free. A GET /api/terms/current endpoint would unlock both.
3. Student visit-request list (acad-abl.20 item 4 handoff): the S1 under-review visit badge and any visit status surface render only from the session cache until GET /api/visit-requests exists.
4. deep_link format (acad-abl.20 item 7 rider): openapi.json still types deep_link as a nullable string while the implementation sends an object. S6 routes by the screen map until the doc fix lands.
5. No plan history endpoint: S2 shows the current term only. Past-term plans have no data source; if history belongs on S4, the ask is a student plan-list endpoint.
6. GET /api/me exposes faculty but not school or department, while the SIS identity payload carries both (acad-9s3.15). S4 renders faculty and curriculum year only. Confirm whether students should see school and department.
close_reason: Student surfaces decided: S1 landing shows one plan card with per-state CTA and no metrics; S2 plan document with returned-reason banner, comment thread, Seen confirm, per-state actions; S3 single-scroll server-backed builder with map combobox, inline group and section edits, honest submit-gate validation; S4 read-only SIS profile; S6 composition on the D4 center; 39 decisions and 6 owner flags

title: AI chat surface
description:
## Question

What is the full UX of the AI chat surface (S5), including how streaming looks in the transcript?

## Context

Conversation list and history, starting a conversation, transcript conventions while frames arrive, the submit-arm moment end to end (what the student confirms when an AI draft becomes a plan draft), quota handling and copy (QuotaExceededError), error and degraded states, and i18n of AI content. Input: the "SSE streaming pattern for AI chat" resolution. The agentic-ux-design-relationship-centric-interfaces skill applies per design.md section 10. Raise fidelity with the prototype skill if the owner prefers reacting to an artifact.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling.

## Record

Numbered decisions; call out anything explicitly deferred to the spec.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.15 (wayfinder:grilling), AI chat surface S5 at /app/chat.
Sources: acad-abl.4 (SSE pattern and frames), acad-abl.1 (digest, sections 6 and 8), acad-abl.13 (conventions 15, 18, 24, 40), acad-abl.19 (shared states, toasts, confirm dialogs), acad-abl.9 (primitives, dayjs, icons), acad-abl.8 (routes, ai-chat feature folder, flag 3), acad-abl.20 item 9 (quota stance); design.md 3, 4.3, 5, 6.2, 8 (DS-W-08), 10.4 (agentic row); docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md 12 and 16; backend map acad-9s3 (decisions 4, 7, 13, 14, 20) with acad-9s3.10 (AI advisor flow) and acad-9s3.11 (AI chat technical contract); openapi.json (listPlanConversations, createPlanConversation, showPlanConversation, createPlanConversationTurn max 10000, armPlanConversationSubmission, PlanConversation, GoalSuggestions). Skills applied: agentic-ux-design-relationship-centric-interfaces (transparency-first trust stage, correction paths, no fake autonomy) and impeccable (Operate mode, DP-01 to DP-09, craft floor).

## 1. Frame and routing

1. S5 is a two-pane layout from md up: conversation list rail at the inline start plus transcript pane. Below md it collapses to the list, and selecting a conversation navigates to the transcript pane. Both panes live inside the student app-shell; the AI chat rail item exists only in the student rail (PR-08, acad-abl.8 Decision 5).
2. Selection lives in the URL: /app/chat renders the list, /app/chat/:conversationId renders the transcript with the list beside it on wide screens. This child route extends the acad-abl.8 tree; the spec pass records it in design.md 6.2.
3. Header: title, one context line naming the assistant, one primary action "New conversation" (DS-L-02). Crimson identity is allowed here (6.2) and is spent only on the assistant identity marks; all status color stays semantic (DS-C-02, DS-C-09).

## 2. Conversation list

4. Data is GET /api/plan-conversations. An item shows the AI-generated title, a goal chip (maintain, improve, excel), and updated_at as an absolute 24h time through src/lib/i18n/format.ts (acad-abl.9 D4). Order is updated_at desc: the backend settles a recency-ordered list (acad-9s3.10 point 1, decision 13).
5. No preview line exists and the client fakes none: the list response carries no message content (PlanConversation holds messages only in the single-conversation response). Before the first completed turn the title is null, so the item shows the dictionary label of the goal as the fallback title (acad-9s3.11: the AI generates the title after the first turn; no student renaming in v1).
6. New conversation opens a dialog with the three Goal Suggestions as three equal cards, equal styling, nothing recommends one (acad-9s3.11 amendment). Start enables only after the student picks one, because CreatePlanConversationInput requires goal. POST then navigates to the new transcript. The localized starter strings render later in the transcript (decision 12); the dialog uses the dictionary goal labels.
7. Empty list: EmptyState (acad-abl.19 D1.2) with copy that names the missing thing and the first step: "No conversations yet. Start one and your AI advisor will help you plan." Action: New conversation.
8. No archive, delete, or rename in v1: the contract holds only create, list, and get. The client builds no client-only hide that would lie about server state. Recorded as an honest limit.
9. List states: skeleton rows matching the item shape on load; ErrorState compact with Retry on failure. No unread dots: the contract tracks no conversation read state.

## 3. Transcript

10. History loads from GET /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}. Message anatomy: identity mark (assistant: small "AI" avatar on the crimson tint; user: slate initials avatar), body, absolute 24h timestamp at text-2xs. Assistant bodies render through the existing md-preview with DOMPurify (acad-abl.8 keep list) capped at max-w-prose (DS-T-06). User bodies render as plain text, never markdown, so a student cannot fake UI chrome inside their own message.
11. Bubbles: assistant on bg-card with a 2px crimson-950 inline-start accent (3.2 assigns crimson-950 to chat bubbles; 6.2 allows the crimson identity), user on bg-muted. Borders over shadows (DP-04), rounded-lg (DS-R-01), dark theme uses the Appendix B crimson dark pair.
12. A conversation with zero user messages renders its three goal_suggestions strings from the conversation response as three equal selectable prompt cards above the composer; pressing one fills the composer. They disappear after the first turn (acad-9s3.10 point 2; acad-9s3.11 serves them only at zero user messages). This is the Alignment Phase entry; the AI's clarifying questions arrive as ordinary tokens (acad-9s3.11).
13. Streaming renders as the last transcript row from the ephemeral zustand store (acad-abl.4) with a block caret at the append point (opacity only; reduced motion shows a static caret). Between send and first token, a three-dot typing row announces "Your AI advisor is replying." in a polite live region (DS-A-09; linear loop allowed by 3.10; dots degrade to a static ellipsis). The sent user message appends optimistically and reconciles at the turn.completed invalidation; on a pre-stream failure the client removes the optimistic row and restores the composer text.
14. Scroll: auto-follow the stream only while the user sits at the bottom within a threshold; scrolling up unpins and shows a "Jump to latest" pill; sending always scrolls down; smooth scrolling respects prefers-reduced-motion.
15. Frames render per type (frame facts from acad-abl.4 and acad-abl.1 section 6):
   - token: append in seq order; validate turn_id and seq stability, drop and log violations instead of rendering garbled text (acad-abl.4).
   - tool.applied: a system event row at its position in the stream: icon, localized line naming the applied change ("Added {course code} to your plan." when the payload carries a course code, bidi-isolated per DS-L-05; a generic per-tool line otherwise), and an inline "Open Plan Builder" link so the student can inspect the change. The client invalidates ['plan'] per acad-abl.4. Transparency first: every plan write is visible where it happened (agentic skill, trust stage 1).
   - submit.suggested: after turn.completed, the SubmitSuggestionCard renders below the assistant message (section 4).
   - submit.result: a system result row. submitted: success row with check icon, "Your plan was submitted for review.", link to /app/plan, invalidate ['plan'] and ['plan-conversations']. blocked: destructive tint, each server constraint message listed under its key with the constraint, reason, path forward order (DS-ST-11); the same turn's prose explains the failure (acad-9s3.10 point 6).
   - turn.completed: finalize the row, replace ephemeral state with canonical cache data (acad-abl.4), and update the list title when frame.title is non-null.
   - error: terminal failed-turn row (acad-abl.13 rule 18): destructive tint, server message, Retry when retryable. Partial tokens stay visible above the row; applied tool effects stay (decision 20, acad-9s3.11 transport).

## 4. The submit-arm moment

16. The SubmitSuggestionCard: banner anatomy, info tint. Title "Ready to submit?". Body in DS-W-02 order: what the AI found (the plan looks complete), what submitting does (it runs the real gates, registration window and validation, then sends the plan to the advisor for review), and what it never does (the AI cannot submit on its own; the student can always submit from the Plan Builder). Actions: primary "Confirm submission" and a link "Review in Plan Builder". No discard action exists: the plan is the only draft and the AI edits it in place; there is no draft artifact (decision 13, acad-9s3.10 point 3). design.md 5.4 DraftPlanCard is dead for S5 (acad-abl.8 flag 3).
17. The confirmation: the primary opens ConfirmDialog, primary variant, focus starts on cancel (acad-abl.19 D3). Body states the consequence plainly: "This confirms you want to submit. Your next message lets your AI advisor submit the plan through the normal checks. Your advisor then reviews it." Confirm label "Confirm submission". Free text never authorizes; only this control arms the flag (decision 14).
18. Arming: on confirm, the client POSTs /api/plan-conversations/{conversation}/submit-arm with button loading; the submit.armed frame resolves the mutation (acad-abl.4). Success swaps the card to the armed state: "Submission confirmed. Send a message and your AI advisor will submit your plan." with one composer suggestion that inserts "Please submit my plan now." for the student to edit and send. The student stays the author; the armed flag is the authorization; the audit records the confirmation with the submission (acad-9s3.10 point 6). No auto-send: the client never posts a turn the student did not send.
19. Result and clear: the next turn streams submit.result and renders per decision 15. The flag clears on use or when plan state changes (acad-9s3.11), and the armed card state clears on the next conversation refetch when submission_confirmed_at is null. Arm failure renders ErrorState compact inside the card with Retry; 404 invalidates the list and returns to /app/chat.
20. Ephemerality: submit.suggested exists only in the stream, so the card does not survive a reload; the assistant's prose suggestion persists in history, and asking again yields a fresh card. The armed flag persists and renders from the conversation resource whenever submission_confirmed_at is set. Accepted contract asymmetry, also flagged below.
21. The Plan Builder keeps the direct submit control (decision 14). S5 adds no window banner; a blocked submit.result shows the gate messages inline.

## 5. Quota

22. The 429 arrives as JSON before the stream (acad-abl.4). It renders as a non-dismissible warning banner above the composer with the fixed copy of acad-abl.13 rule 15: "You have used your conversation limit for this term. You can still edit and submit your plan in the Plan Builder." with a link to /app/builder. The composer disables for the session and offers no retry, because retry means a new turn that cannot succeed this term (decision 20). The unsent text returns to the composer.
23. No quota meter anywhere in v1: no endpoint exposes the remaining count, an accepted gap (acad-abl.20 item 9). If the handoff lands, the counter renders as one quiet text-2xs line under the composer ("{n} of 100 replies left this term") and nothing bolder. Nothing is built now.

## 6. Errors and degraded states

24. Six states per DS-ST-08: loading uses skeletons matching list rows and transcript bubble shapes; empty conversation is decision 12; empty list is decision 7; error uses ErrorState compact in the list and at page level in the transcript, with Retry refetching the failed root; permission denied: RoleRoute renders PermissionDenied for any non-student before chat data loads (acad-abl.8 Decision 4); stale SIS is N/A for this route; window closed surfaces through submit.result blocked and the builder, not as a chat banner.
25. Mid-stream failure: an error frame or a network break is terminal (acad-abl.4). Partial tokens stay with a one-line muted note, the failed-turn row offers Retry when retryable is true, and Retry resends the same message as a new POST. Never a stream resume: no Last-Event-ID exists (acad-9s3.11 transport). Mutation retries stay off (acad-abl.13 rule 24). Applied tool effects persist (decision 20).
26. 404 on the conversation get: invalidate the list, render EmptyState naming the missing conversation, navigate back to /app/chat. 403 is unreachable for students in-app and renders PermissionDenied on direct hits.

## 7. Composer

27. Anatomy: auto-growing textarea (16px text per 5.2, one row at rest, capped height then scroll), a 44px send icon button (SendHorizontal, flips under RTL per DS-L-04), and a helper slot for state lines.
28. Limits: hard maxLength 10000 per CreatePlanConversationTurnInput, mirrored in the feature zod schema; a text-2xs counter appears only within 200 characters of the limit (DP-02). Empty input disables send.
29. Streaming lock: while a turn is in flight the composer disables with the visible reason "Your AI advisor is replying." and Send swaps to a 44px Stop button that calls the abort path of acad-abl.4. On abort the partial reply stays, a muted "Stopped." line closes it, and the composer re-enables. No resume exists; a stopped turn stays partial (acad-abl.4 cancellation).
30. Quota lock follows decision 22. After reload the composer re-enables because no endpoint reports exhaustion; the next send re-learns 429. Honest consequence of acad-abl.20 item 9.

## 8. Relationship stance

31. Name and address: the assistant presents as "your AI advisor" (dictionary term). It never claims to be a person and never claims to be the assigned human advisor; the advisor appears by name only on plan and profile surfaces. The AI addresses the student in the second person, calm and concrete (DS-W-08).
32. It never claims approval authority (copy says the advisor approves), registration authority (copy says the student registers in the SIS), waiver power (it explains validation, never waives it, acad-9s3.11 validation amendment), submission power without the armed confirmation (decision 14), or the power to label or predict (PR-01, PR-10, DS-W-08).
33. Constitution line: one persistent quiet footer under the transcript, text-xs text-muted-foreground, dictionary copy: "The AI advisor explains and drafts. Your advisor approves. Only you can submit." It renders once per conversation view, never per message, never as a modal, and never blocks input. This is the v1 AI constitution framing (design.md 10.4 agentic row); memory visualization and trust-stage controls stay out of scope in v1.
34. Trust comes from transparency, not charm: no confidence meters, no expressive avatar behavior, no proactive nudge banners (proactive triggers surface only as chat entry points, foundation 12). Every plan edit shows its system row and an inspect link (decision 15). Correction is one click away in the builder, and the audit names the actor per change (acad-9s3.10 point 5).

## 9. i18n of AI content

35. The server localizes prompts, plan content, and error messages en/ar (decision 7). The client renders the streamed language as-is, takes all chrome from the dictionary (DS-W-01), and never translates or rewrites AI content. Course codes inside Arabic text sit in the bidi isolate (DS-L-05); numerals stay Latin (DS-T-03).

## 10. Deferred to the spec

- The exact dark-theme crimson pair for the assistant accent, verified against Appendix B.
- The /app/chat/:conversationId route line in design.md 6.2 and the S5 component list correction (DraftPlanCard out, SubmitSuggestionCard and the tool event row in).
- Component files as domain components inside src/features/ai-chat/components/ (folder already fixed by acad-abl.8 Decision 2; no new base folders), each with story and test per DS-CP-03.

## Flags for the owner

1. design.md 5.4 DraftPlanCard and the 6.2 S5 row still name draft-plan-card; backend decision 13 removed the draft artifact and handoff card (acad-abl.8 flag 3). This resolution confirms the replacement for S5: tool.applied system rows plus the SubmitSuggestionCard. S1 needs the same correction.
2. submit.suggested is stream-only while the armed flag persists, so the suggestion card does not survive a reload and the student must ask again. Stance: accept. Alternative ask for the backend: persist a pending-suggestion state on PlanConversation so the card renders from data.
3. The settled flow needs two steps: the student arms, then sends a message that triggers the submit tool (decision 14, acad-9s3.11). If the owner prefers submission on the arm press itself, the arm endpoint would need to stream submit.result; that is a backend change. Current stance follows the settled contract.
4. Quota visibility stays an accepted gap (acad-abl.20 item 9). A remaining-quota read endpoint remains the v2 ask; the client has a reserved slot for it (decision 23).
close_reason: S5 resolved: recency-ordered list without previews (honest limits), per-frame transcript rendering, arm-then-submit confirmation with no auto-send, quota silent until 429 with fixed copy, student-only route, transparency-first AI stance

title: Advisor surfaces A1-A5
description:
## Question

What exactly does each advisor surface show and do, including the review flow?

## Context

A1 queue, A2 student explorer (caseload), A3 meetings, A4 office hours, A5 notifications. Inputs: the "Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions" resolution. Decide: queue ordering and aging display (a queue-aging-threshold setting exists), the review drawer scope: plan summary, validation state, comments, approve, return with mandatory written reason, seen semantics; explorer filters; visit request and slot flows; the office-hours editor including timezone handling for availability windows (the contract carries AvailabilityWindow rows); and stale-SIS display on student plans. Raise fidelity with the prototype skill if the owner prefers reacting to an artifact.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling; consult ui-ux-pro-max and impeccable per design.md section 10.

## Record

Per-surface numbered decisions, including the review flow.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.16 (wayfinder:grilling), Advisor surfaces A1-A5. Sources: design.md 3, 5, 6.2, 8; foundation 5, 8, 10, 15, 16 as amended by the settled backend decisions; zoomed resolutions acad-abl.1, .8, .9, .13, .19, .20; backend map acad-9s3 (decisions 11, 17, 18, 22, 23) and children acad-9s3.12 (return, Seen, comments), acad-9s3.13 (office hours and visits), acad-9s3.16 (aging threshold); openapi.json and the backend controllers and services verified on 2026-10-01; ui-ux-pro-max and impeccable (craft floor) for craft judgment. Copy lines below are the EN dictionary lines; AR ships with them per DS-W-01. Every surface implements the six screen states through the acad-abl.19 D1 components.

## Shared decisions (all five surfaces)

D1. Feature homes and the shared drawer. A1 lives in src/features/advisor-queue/, A2 advisor-students/, A3 advisor-meetings/, A4 advisor-hours/, A5 composes the shared notifications feature (acad-abl.8 Decision 2). The review drawer is shared by A1 and A2, so cross-feature imports stay banned: it lands in src/components/domain/review-drawer/ under the pending approval flagged on acad-abl.8 flag 6.

D2. Query keys and freshness. Under the ['advisor'] subtree (acad-abl.13 convention 22): ['advisor', 'queue'], ['advisor', 'caseload', { search, perPage }], ['advisor', 'plans', planId], ['advisor', 'plan-comments', planId], ['advisor', 'visit-requests'], ['advisor', 'availability']. Queue, caseload, and visit requests get staleTime 30 seconds with refetchOnWindowFocus true, the focus-refetch rule from acad-abl.13 convention 25 extended to visit requests as the third operational advisor list. Availability keeps 5 minutes with no polling (convention 25). Comments on an open plan use staleTime 0 like plan data because the student and server mutate them.

D3. Density and tables. All advisor tables render compact through the shell-provided TableDensityContext (acad-abl.19 D5): px-3 py-2 cells, text-2xs meta, tabular-nums numeric columns at the inline end, sticky header, aria-sort where sortable, overflow-x-auto wrapper. No checkbox multi-select anywhere (acad-abl.19 D5.4).

## A1 Queue (/advisor)

D4. Data and ordering. GET /api/advisor/queue returns only Submitted and Under Review plans of the advisor's caseload, ordered by submitted_at then id, oldest first (backend AdvisorReviewService::queue). The client keeps that order as the only sort and builds no sort control: oldest first is the aging semantics. The queue item carries plan id, student summary, status, term_code, submitted_at, is_aging. No query params exist, so filters and pagination are client-side; the list is one page.

D5. Columns. Student (avatar, name, student_id), State (PlanStateChip, dot-only variant), Term (term_code), Waiting (days since submitted_at, dayjs core diff, tabular-nums, with the amber Aging badge from is_aging beside it). Two design.md 5.4 columns are cut for honesty: "plan summary" is impossible without GET /api/advisor/plans/{plan}, and that GET moves a Submitted plan to Under Review (contract description, transition 3), so the row cannot prefetch a summary; the "visit-request flag" has no field on AdvisorQueueItem. Visit work lives on A3.

D6. Aging display. The row renders the server's is_aging flag as the Aging badge and nothing else. The client never shows the threshold value, never computes aging, and never hardcodes 3 days (the threshold is Admin-configured, backend decision 18; design.md PR-13's fixed 3-day note is stale and the doc pass corrects it). The Waiting days figure is display only and is not the criterion.

D7. Filters. Tabs (acad-abl.9 item 10): All, Submitted, Under review, with counts, filtered client-side. The server already restricts the set to those two states. No search: the endpoint takes none and the queue is small by nature.

D8. Row anatomy and open. The whole row is one focusable control; activation opens the review drawer, sets aria-current on the row, and applies the 4.1 selected treatment (acad-abl.19 D5.4). Open always calls GET /api/advisor/plans/{plan}; a Submitted plan lands Under Review server-side and the queue refetches so the chip tells the truth. Opening is review intent; no confirm (visible, settled transition).

D9. States. Loading: SkeletonTableRows matching D5 columns. Empty: EmptyState, "No plans are waiting for review. New submissions appear here." Error: ErrorState with Retry and the requestId line. Permission denied: RoleRoute panel and the 403 mapping (acad-abl.13 convention 12). Stale SIS: N/A, no advisor endpoint carries last_synced_at or staleness (see flag 3). Window closed: N/A, no advisor action is window-gated.

## Review drawer (shared by A1 and A2)

D10. Shell. The existing drawer primitive, side panel at the inline end: full width below md, max-w-xl (576px) at lg and up, overlay bg at z-overlay, content at z-modal, shadow-lg. It is visually a side panel and behaviorally modal: Radix focus trap, ESC to close, focus returns to the triggering row (DS-A-02). "Not modal" in design.md 5.4 is honored as visual placement; the focus contract is a MUST and wins.

D11. Sections, single scroll, sticky action footer. Header: student name, student_id, term_code, PlanStateChip, close. Context line: CGPA from the ['advisor', 'caseload'] cache ("CGPA 3.20" tabular-nums, an em dash when null). Remaining credits are cut: no advisor endpoint carries them (flag 7). Plan area: the server summary when present; then course lines under one heading built from term_code, because the plan binds one term and the contract has no semester grouping to render. Course line: course_code (bidi isolate), title joined from the academic-record prerequisite_map cache, group and section, and the AI reason as a muted "AI note" line when set (backend decision 12). Credit total is omitted, never rendered as a zero (acad-abl.20 stance 18). Advisory plan warnings render as info lines below the courses.

D12. Validation display. The drawer has no live validation panel: a plan here already passed the submit gate. Server verdicts render at the moment they happen. An approve 422 renders each server message (allowance, prerequisite_chain) in a destructive result list above the footer; the plan stays Under Review and both actions stay live, because Return remains a path after a failed approval (backend decision 17). A 503 plan.sis_unavailable renders the destructive banner with Retry next to the actions (acad-abl.13 convention 17). A 409 invalidates the plan and queue roots and toasts the one calm line (convention 14).

D13. Comment thread. GET and POST /api/advisor/plans/{plan}/comments, ordered oldest first, author and absolute timestamp through format.ts. The composer is the advisor's one free-text surface: textarea, maxLength 2000, dictionary zod message, "Add comment" button. This thread is separate from the return reason: the reason is a distinct field on the return action and the client never mirrors it into the thread (backend decision 11). A plan.not_commentable 409 follows convention 14.

D14. Seen marker. Cut for honesty: no advisor-readable payload carries a seen receipt or timestamp. The advisor infers it only from the plan leaving Returned. Flag 2 asks for seen_at.

D15. Approve. Primary footer button. ConfirmDialog (acad-abl.19 D3): title "Approve plan?", body "Approval locks this plan. {name} registers the courses in the SIS.", confirm "Approve plan", focus starts on cancel. Success closes the drawer and invalidates the queue and caseload roots; the row leaves the queue, so no toast (acad-abl.19 D2.2).

D16. Return. Footer button opens an inline return form in the drawer: required textarea (maxLength 2000), helper "The reason goes to {name}. They press Seen before they can edit and resubmit.", submit button "Return plan". Empty input fails client-side with the inline field error "Write the reason so {name} knows what to change."; a server 422 on reason merges through setError and wins (acad-abl.13 convention 35). Success closes the drawer and invalidates the queue and caseload roots, no toast. ESC or close with text in the field asks ConfirmDialog "Discard the return reason?" before closing; an empty field closes straight away.

D17. Staleness banner. N/A on the drawer for the same reason as D9: no staleness payload reaches advisor surfaces. The honest SIS signal is the 503 banner in D12.

D18. Keyboard path. Open from row focuses the drawer heading; tab order runs close, header, plan lines, comments, composer, return form when open, footer actions; ESC closes under the D16 guard; focus returns to the triggering row. The queue-and-drawer keyboard flow is a Playwright keyboard spec (acad-abl.19 D8.4).

## A2 Student explorer (/advisor/students)

D19. Data. GET /api/advisor/caseload?search&per_page, server-sorted by name ascending (backend decision 22). Row fields are exactly AdvisorCaseloadStudent: name, student_id, sis_email, faculty, school, department (nullable), curriculum_year_level, plan_state, submitted_at, is_aging, has_unmet_meeting, cgpa. No risk columns (backend decision 22).

D20. Search and filter model. Search is the server param, debounced 300ms, matching name and student ID (backend decision 22). Two client-side filter tabs join it: All, Unmet meeting, Aging. Activating Unmet meeting or Aging refetches with per_page=all and filters the loaded set client-side, so the filter is honest over the whole caseload (advisor caseloads are small; the endpoint allows all). The level filter promised by backend decision 22 has no query param (flag 4): level renders as a column now, and the same fetch-all client filter pattern covers it when a select is added.

D21. Row anatomy. Student (avatar, name, student_id), Email, Faculty and school and department stacked as text-2xs lines (em dash when unchosen), Level, Plan state (dot-only chip, em dash when null), Submitted (absolute date, format.ts), Waiting with the Aging badge, Meeting badge "Meeting not met" when has_unmet_meeting (backend decision 23: only the advisor caseload view flags it), CGPA (tabular-nums, em dash when null).
