D22. Detail destination: the drawer, not a page. The contract offers no student-detail endpoint beyond caseload rows and single-plan access, so a page would be an empty shell. Row activation opens the same review drawer (D10 to D18): identity, context line, and the current plan with its actions. Opening a Submitted plan moves it Under Review, the settled semantics of an advisor opening a plan; the drawer is the one review surface and no drawer nests inside a drawer. A student with plan_state null renders the plan-area EmptyState, "{name} has not created a plan this term." The drawer also carries "Request meeting", the advisor-initiated visit entry point (D26).

D23. States. Loading: SkeletonTableRows. Empty caseload: EmptyState, "No students are assigned to you yet. The Admin assigns caseloads.", no action. Empty search: EmptyState, "No students match '{search}'. Check the spelling or clear the search." with the Clear search action. Error, permission, stale, window per D9.

## A3 Meetings (/advisor/meetings)

D24. Data and model. GET /api/advisor/visit-requests returns every request for the advisor's current caseload students, newest first, Proposed and Done together (backend VisitService::forAdvisor). The settled model rules everything here (backend decision 23, acad-9s3.13): Proposed to Done, no approval, no denial, no slot picking, no booking; slots are information; the advisor marks Done; only the initiator deletes while Proposed; at most one Proposed request per student per term. Tabs: Open (proposed, with count) and Done. The initiator is derived by comparing initiator_id with student.id: "Requested by {name}" or "Requested by you".

D25. Row anatomy and actions. Student (name, student_id), direction line, created date (absolute), status badge (Proposed: info tint, Done: success tint), term, and the slot list: each VisitRequestSlot renders "DD MMM YYYY, HH:mm-HH:mm" converted to Africa/Cairo through format.ts (these are full date-times, unlike availability rows). On Proposed: "Mark done" button, no dialog, visible state change (acad-abl.19 D3); and "Propose slots" when the request is student-initiated. The advisor's own deletions are out of the v1 UI: the advisor deletes only advisor-initiated requests, a rare correction; no affordance ships in v1 (DP-02) and DELETE stays a contract capability.

D26. Propose slots and raise request. "Propose slots" opens a dialog with slot rows (date, start, end), max 10 (ProvideVisitSlotsInput maxItems), each row validated end after start, times labeled "Times are Africa/Cairo time." Save sends the ISO instants built in Africa/Cairo with the dayjs timezone plugin; the row re-renders from the server response, so any DST shift is visible in the rendered times (honesty rule, D29). Success copy in the dialog: "Slots sent. {name} is notified in the app.", the only visibility claim, backed by the visit_slots_provided notification (backend decision 23). Raising a request lives on the A2 drawer as "Request meeting" with optional slot rows, because after an informal meeting the advisor raises one and marks it Done immediately (acad-9s3.13), and that flow starts from a student. A3 carries no compose action (DS-L-02). The implementation returns 201 with the VisitRequest; the client writes it into the cache (flag 5).

D27. Copy honesty and states. Advisor copy never promises student-side list visibility: the student has no visit-request list (acad-abl.20 stance 4), so copy claims only the two notifications. Empty Open tab: "No open meeting requests. Requests from your students appear here." Empty Done tab: "No meetings marked done this term." Loading, error, permission, stale, window per D9. A 409 visit.not_slotable or visit.not_completable invalidates ['advisor', 'visit-requests'] and toasts the calm line (convention 14).

## A4 Office hours (/advisor/hours)

D28. Editor form, not a grid. The deferred time grid stays dead (acad-abl.9 D2): the editor is form rows on the existing form primitives, per design.md 5.4 SlotEditor. Each row: day select, from time, to time, remove button. The Add button dies at five rows with the helper "Up to 5 rows." (contract maxItems 5). The day select sends the seven canonical lowercase English tokens (sunday through saturday, the backend's own storage form, max 20 chars) and renders localized labels from the dictionary; unknown stored strings render as-is, bidi-isolated. GET /api/advisor/availability returns the defaults with is_default=true before first publish; the editor pre-fills them with the info line "These are the default hours. Publish to make them yours."

D29. Timezone and DST. Availability rows are naive day plus H:i wall times (openapi pattern, backend stores them verbatim). Africa/Cairo is the platform's single timezone (acad-9s3.13). The client enters and renders them as written and never converts (acad-abl.9 D4), and the editor carries the standing label "Times are Africa/Cairo time." DST is handled by honesty, not math: the rows carry no offset, so a DST switch changes what a wall time means, and the label plus the shared Cairo clock is the contract the student side reads too. No per-row offsets, no UTC storage, no warnings in v1. Visit-request slots (D26) are the contrast case: real instants, converted for display.

D30. Validation and save. Zod on every row: end after start with "End time must be after the start time."; same-day overlap is a hard inline error, "Two rows overlap on {day}. Adjust the times so each row stands alone.", client-side only, because the server accepts overlaps and design.md 5.4 mandates overlap validation in the editor. Save is PUT with the full rows array (contract is a full replace), button "Publish hours". Success reflects the saved state in place, no toast, no dialog (acad-abl.19 D3). Clear-all asks ConfirmDialog (destructive): "This removes your published hours. Students will no longer see your office hours.", confirm "Clear hours", because saving an empty array unpublishes the window and students then see nothing (backend AvailabilityWindowService). 422 field errors land inline under their rows (convention 35).

D31. States. Loading: skeleton rows in the editor's shape. Error: ErrorState with Retry. Empty: N/A as a screen state, the editor always shows rows (defaults or saved); the cleared state renders as the is_default info line. Permission, stale, window per D9.

## A5 Notifications (/advisor/notifications)

D32. Composition only, per scope: the shared notification center (acad-abl.19 D4) mounted under the advisor shell. The slug-to-route table resolves by role: caseload_student_added and caseload_student_removed route to /advisor/students, visit_requested routes to /advisor/meetings for the advisor recipient; the student-recipient slugs never arrive for an advisor and unknown slugs fall back to /advisor (acad-abl.20 stance 15). Read-all, 30-second foreground poll, optimistic reads, item anatomy, and states all follow acad-abl.19 D4 unchanged. Empty: "No notifications yet. Plan and visit updates will appear here."

## Flags for the owner

1. AdvisorQueueItem carries no visit-request flag, so design.md 5.4's queue "visit-request flag" column is unbuildable; it is cut and visit work lives on A3. A backend flag field would restore it.
2. No advisor-readable payload carries a Seen receipt (no seen_at, no read flag on comments). The advisor cannot know whether a returned student has seen the reason, only that the plan later left Returned. Add seen_at to the plan payload or accept the gap.
3. No advisor endpoint carries last_synced_at or the staleness object, so StaleSisBanner is unrenderable on A1 through A4; the 503 plan.sis_unavailable banner at approve is the only SIS surface. Staleness on the caseload payload would fix it.
4. GET /api/advisor/caseload has no level query param, though backend decision 22 settles level as a filter. The client filters the loaded set (fetch-all pattern); a level param is the clean fix.
5. openapi.json documents POST /api/advisor/visit-requests as 200 with an empty body; the implementation returns 201 with a VisitRequestResource. Doc-only rider: align the contract.
6. design.md needs the standing corrections pass: PR-13's fixed 3-day aging becomes the is_aging flag, VisitRequestCard's Accept/Decline becomes the Proposed-to-Done model (already acad-abl.8 flag 4), and the ReviewDrawer's "remaining credits from SIS" line is cut (no advisor endpoint carries it, flag 7's pair).
7. The advisor drawer cannot show remaining credits or any student academic record: permission rows deny advisor access to the academic record, and no advisor endpoint carries it. CGPA from the caseload row is the whole context line. A student-context payload for advisors is a v2 ask.
close_reason: Advisor surfaces resolved: 32 decisions across queue, review drawer, explorer, meetings, and office hours; form-rows editor in Africa/Cairo wall time; 7 owner flags recorded

title: Design workflow bindings
description:
## Question

How do the design skills bind to this effort's artifacts without competing sources of truth?

## Context

design.md is the design source of truth. ui-ux-pro-max can persist a `design-system/` tree (MASTER.md plus page overrides). impeccable expects PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md; neither exists yet. superdesign keeps mockups on a canvas. Storybook 10 is installed. Decide: whether ui-ux-pro-max output persists or stays advisory against design.md; when impeccable init and document run (now versus at first implementation); whether DESIGN.md references or mirrors design.md; story expectations per component; and where prototype artifacts live when a grilling session raises fidelity.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling.

## Record

Numbered bindings: artifact, owning skill, location, and update rule.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01)

## Basis

design.md 0.1 precedence (docs/product > design.md > skills), DS-AI-01/02 (skills never outrank the repo), DS-G-01..07 (governance), DS-0-01 (no skill output overrides design truth). Feature grounding comes from the backend map: page inventory (§14), six-state matrix (§15), cross-cutting EN/AR + RTL + dark/light + accessibility (§17). The frontend 03-DESIGN-PLAN supplies the D-phase ladder and the ~30-component library (PlanStateChip per §7, SeenButton per Q32, ValidationPanel per Q57). Repo state verified: no design-system/, no PRODUCT.md, no DESIGN.md, no .superdesign/; Storybook 10.6.0 installed; the a11y addon is not installed.

## Bindings

**B1. design.md stays the only design source of truth.** Owning skill: none; governed by section 11. Location: /design.md. Update rule: DS-G-05 semantic versioning only. No skill, brief, or generated file may mirror it as a competing truth (DS-0-01).

**B2. ui-ux-pro-max output is advisory and never persists.** Owning skill: ui-ux-pro-max (routing table, section 10.2). Location: none in the repo. Update rule: run its searches per DS-AI-14 for any UI task; never run `--persist`; never create design-system/MASTER.md here. Any token, palette, or pattern it surfaces enters design.md only through DS-G-02 or DS-G-03 (issue, before/after, human approval). A second persisted truth would drift against the Appendix B token block and the DS-G rules that own contradictions.

**B3. PRODUCT.md is generated once at first implementation kickoff.** Owning skill: impeccable `init`. Location: /PRODUCT.md (repo root, committed). Timing: when the first UI implementation ticket starts (shell + auth, D1/P1), not now; DS-AI-07 keeps the map phase producing decisions, not deliverables. Update rule: init sources docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md; the file carries a header naming docs/product as product truth; regenerate only when product scope changes.

**B4. DESIGN.md is generated from shipped code, after the first real screens exist.** Owning skill: impeccable `document`. Location: /DESIGN.md (repo root, committed). Timing: not at kickoff; only after the first screens render, so it documents shipped truth, not intent. Update rule: mandatory header "design.md is the source of truth; on conflict design.md wins"; regenerate after every DS-G-02 or DS-G-03 change lands; never hand-edit it into a third variation (DS-G-04).

**B5. Surface briefs: one per surface group, written when that group's implementation starts.** Owning skill: impeccable `shape` / new-work. Location: .impeccable/surfaces/ (the skill's own convention), committed. Surfaces, from backend map §14: shell + auth, student S1-S6, advisor A1-A5, dean + VP, admin M1-M5. Timing: each brief is written at the first ticket of its group and pinned to mode Operate (task UI, not Persuade). Density pins follow 03-DESIGN-PLAN section 3: students phone-first with breathing room, staff desktop-first data-dense. Update rule: a brief cites design.md rules and never overrides them (DS-AI-02); refresh when the surface's D-phase acceptance (DS-G-06) fails on a brief-level assumption.

**B6. Prototype and mockup artifacts live on the canvas, not in git.** Owning skill: superdesign (and the prototype skill for cheap grilling probes, per the map note). Location: the superdesign canvas by default; canvas and preview links are recorded in the raising ticket's notes. Local exports go to /design (git-ignored) only when the owner asks for a reviewable file; superdesign's .superdesign/ init cache stays git-ignored too. Update rule: mockups are probes, never reference; a decision approved from a mockup is promoted into design.md through DS-G-02/03 or into code, then the artifact dies. No design/mockups/ committed tree: a browsable mockup folder would read as a third design truth.

**B7. Storybook: a story per ui/ primitive is mandatory; domain components get stories with state coverage.** Owning skill: none (plop generator plus DS-CP-03). Location: src/components/ui/<name>/<name>.stories.tsx; domain component stories beside the component in src/features/<domain>/components/. Rules: every ui/ primitive ships story + Testing Library test through `npm run generate` (DoD item 6, DS-CP-03); the a11y addon check is mandatory because section 7 and backend §17 make accessibility non-negotiable. Domain components from design.md 5.4 (PlanStateChip's 9 states, SeenButton per Q32, ValidationPanel per Q57, QueueTable + ReviewDrawer, ScoreboardTable, FunnelChart) get stories decorated with MSW fixtures covering their §15 states. Install @storybook/addon-a11y under the owner's trusted-install grant of 2026-10-01, reason: DS-CP-03 requires an a11y check and the addon is missing. Add theme and direction decorators (light/dark, LTR/RTL) so stories can prove DoD item 3.

**B8. design-audit runs before any UI ticket closes and at each D-phase acceptance.** Owning skill: design-audit, with impeccable for bounded verification (DS-0-03). Timing: one batched audit pass (build fully, inspect once, fix in one batch, at most one confirm round) before an agent marks any UI ticket done, and again per D-phase against DS-G-06. Output rule: findings use the audit format from section 10.4 (what is wrong, what it should be, why it matters, token-level instructions) in priority order DS-Q-01; findings that need new tokens or components route through DS-G-02/03; audit results land in ticket notes, never in new repo doc files.

## Flags for the owner

1. @storybook/addon-a11y is absent while DS-CP-03 requires its check. B7 installs it under the 2026-10-01 trusted-install grant. Veto now if you want a different a11y harness.
2. The Storybook theme and RTL decorator (B7) is small tooling work with no owning ticket. It fits the app skeleton or component gap ticket; say which.
3. 03-DESIGN-PLAN is Figma-centric (D0-D7, variable modes, dev-mode handoff). These bindings replace the Figma mechanics with agent artifacts on the same D-phase ladder. No ticket reopens that plan, but a one-line reconciliation in that doc would remove the ambiguity.
close_reason: Resolved: design.md stays the only design truth; ui-ux-pro-max advisory only, no persisted design-system/; impeccable init at first kickoff, document after first screens; briefs per surface group in .impeccable/surfaces/; mockups on canvas, exports git-ignored; story+a11y per component; design-audit before UI ticket close and per D-phase

title: Auth and account UX
description:
## Question

What is the UX for register, login, email verification, forgot password, and session expiry?

## Context

Contract: register, login, logout, me, forgot-password, email/verification-notification, and GET `verify-email/{id}/{hash}`. Signup binds a student ID and gates on `@ejust.edu.eg`. React-query-auth is installed; token storage follows the "Auth token storage for the SPA" resolution. Decide: form validation UX, the verification-pending state, how the GET verification link lands in an SPA, per-role redirect after login, expiry and 401 recovery, and error copy per design.md section 8.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with the grilling and domain-modeling skills.

## Record

Numbered UX decisions per flow, with the exact states each screen shows.
notes:
# acad-abl.12 Resolution: Auth and account UX

RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Inputs: acad-abl.2, acad-abl.3, acad-abl.8, acad-abl.13 (all closed); design.md 3, 4, 6.2, 7, 8; docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md 4, 5, 9, 14 (X1), 16; backend map acad-9s3 decisions 1, 2, 3, 7, 18 and child acad-9s3.2 (registration, verification, binding, tokens, throttles); the contract at ../academic-advisor-backend/openapi.json (Auth tag, read 2026-10-01). ui-ux-pro-max grounded the form and a11y rules; impeccable (Operate mode, craft-floor.md) set the craft bar. Decisions are numbered so the spec can quote them. All copy below is EN; AR lands with the dictionary per DS-W-01.

## 1. Surface set, routes, and guards

1.1 X1 holds four surfaces, all rendered in the centered auth-layout: /login, /signup, /forgot-password, /verify-email/:id/:hash. design.md 6.2 names only /login and /signup; the two extra routes extend X1 (flag 5).
1.2 Auth surfaces carry the theme and language toggles in the auth-layout header, since the app shell does not wrap them. Language choice applies immediately and persists client side (acad-abl.13 flag: no language write endpoint).
1.3 A visitor with a valid token is redirected away from all four surfaces to the role landing. A visitor without one who hits a protected route lands on /login with redirectTo (acad-abl.3).
1.4 Staff never see a signup path. Staff accounts are Admin-created (acad-9s3.2; foundation 14). The login page links to sign-up for students and to forgot-password for everyone.

## 2. Login flow

2.1 Fields: email and password, exactly the contract's LoginInput. Visible labels with htmlFor wiring (DS-A-04). autocomplete="email" and autocomplete="current-password"; paste is never blocked (WCAG 2.2 accessible authentication, ui-ux-pro-max). A password reveal toggle ships as an aria-labeled icon button.
2.2 Validation: zod + RHF, mode onBlur, revalidate on change after first submit, focus the first errored field on failed submit (acad-abl.13 convention 31). Client messages: "Enter your university email." / "Enter your password."
2.3 Submit button: "Sign in" (verb, DS-W-04). Pending: spinner replaces the icon, label preserved, button disabled, aria-busy="true" (design.md 4.1). The single primary action on the page (DP-03).
2.4 Errors: 422 field errors map under their fields with the server message verbatim; the server localizes en/ar (map decision 7; acad-abl.13 conventions 9 and 35). Invalid credentials are a 422 keyed to email and render inline under email; the message stays generic per acad-9s3.2 ("These credentials do not match an account." as dictionary fallback). 429 renders the convention-16 inline error: "Too many attempts. Try again in a minute." (limits: login 5/min per email plus IP, acad-9s3.2).
2.5 Unverified, pending-Admin, and suspended accounts: the server message renders inline and the client invents nothing. No student-side retry exists for pending-Admin (acad-9s3.2); recovery is Admin retry or ID correction (map decision 18). Login never calls the SIS (acad-9s3.2).
2.6 Success: store the token (acad-abl.3), fetch and cache ['me'], then redirect. redirectTo wins when present; the role landing is the default: student /app, advisor /advisor, dean /dean, vp /vp, admin /admin (acad-abl.8 decision 4). redirectTo is sanitized: it must start with a single slash and must not start with //, otherwise the role landing. Students land on /app even before an advisor is assigned; the no-advisor state is S1's job (map decision 3).
2.7 Secondary links: "Forgot password?" and "Create an account", text links under the form, 44px touch targets (DS-S-01).

## 3. Signup flow

3.1 Fields per acad-9s3.2 (the only self-supplied data): email, student ID, password, password confirmation, language preference. No name field: the SIS supplies identity at verification (acad-9s3.2; contract drift flagged in flag 1).
3.2 Student ID: label "Student ID", helper "The ID on your university record." Client validation: required only; the server owns format and uniqueness (422 inline). Binding is by student ID (foundation 9 row 11, foundation 14); the SIS lookup later derives from the verified email (map decision 2 amendment), which the form never needs to explain beyond the helper.
3.3 Email: zod rule enforces the @ejust.edu.eg domain client side with "Use your university email ending in @ejust.edu.eg." The server 422 wins over client copy when present (convention 35). Duplicate email with matching student ID returns 422 and renders the server message plus a "Send a new verification email" action that resubmits the registration; acad-9s3.2: re-registering a used email with its matching student ID offers a verification resend (mechanism flagged in flag 2). A taken student ID blocks registration with the server inline message, no displacement (acad-9s3.2).
3.4 Password: minimum 8 characters, confirmation field with "Passwords do not match." client side; no composition rules, no breached check (acad-9s3.2). autocomplete="new-password".
3.5 Language preference: required segmented control "English / العربية", default en. Selecting العربية flips the UI locale and dir immediately and sends language_preference: "ar" (map decision 7: preference chosen at registration).
3.6 Submit: "Create account". Registration performs no SIS call (acad-9s3.2), so the pending state is short; same spinner contract as login. Throttle 429 (register 5/min per IP) renders the convention-16 inline error.
3.7 Success state (pending email verification), rendered in place of the form: title "Check your inbox", body "We sent a verification link to {email}. The link expires after 60 minutes." Actions: "Back to sign in". The honest resend guidance: "Nothing arrived? Submit the sign-up form again with the same email and student ID to get a new link." (acad-9s3.2 resend path; flag 2). No login is possible until verification completes (acad-9s3.2: no login until complete).

## 4. Email verification landing

4.1 The email link targets the SPA route /verify-email/:id/:hash and preserves the full query string. On mount the page calls GET /api/verify-email/{id}/{hash} with the preserved query (flag 4). This resolves acad-abl.2 gap 2 for the frontend side: never render the raw API URL in the email.
4.2 Processing state: brief spinner with "Verifying your email..." and aria-busy (DS-M-05 feedback within 100ms).
4.3 Ready (200, pending_admin_at null): success panel, one h1 "Your email is verified", body "Your account is ready. Sign in to continue.", primary action "Sign in" routing to /login. The visitor is always unauthenticated here because login was blocked before verification.
4.4 Held (200 with pending_admin_at set): the generic parked message per acad-9s3.2, pointing at administration: "We could not finish setting up your account. Contact the administration office to continue." Action "Back to sign in". The copy never states a cause; public messages never distinguish SIS-unreachable from ID-not-found (acad-9s3.2).
4.5 Invalid or expired link (403): "This link is invalid or has expired. Verification links last 60 minutes." Recovery follows the one real path: "Submit the sign-up form again with the same email to get a new link." Action "Back to sign up" to /signup.
4.6 SIS unavailable (503): the destructive-banner pattern of convention 17 with a Retry action that re-issues the GET, plus "The link stays valid for 60 minutes, so you can try again later." This is the transient path students self-serve by re-opening the link (acad-9s3.2).
4.7 Each state sets its document title and is keyboard reachable with visible focus (DS-A-08).

## 5. Forgot password flow

5.1 Route /forgot-password. One form, one field: email. No domain restriction: the reset serves every role through one flow (acad-9s3.2), and staff emails are Admin-set and need not be university addresses.
5.2 Submit: "Send reset link". Pending: spinner contract as login. 422 inline; 429 (2/min per email, 10/h per IP, acad-9s3.2) renders "Too many attempts. Try again in a minute." inline.
5.3 Sent confirmation replaces the form on 200: "If an account exists for {email}, we sent a link to set a new password. The link expires after 60 minutes." The response is identical whether or not the email matches an account (contract; acad-9s3.2 generic responses), and the copy must not reveal existence. Actions: "Send again" (resubmits; 429 renders inline) and "Back to sign in".
5.4 Reset completion: the contract defines no POST /api/reset-password and no landing for the signed one-time link, so the SPA's flow honestly ends at the confirmation and the copy directs to the email: "Open the link in the email to set a new password." The reset screen is missing from the contract; flag 3 records it with the proposed /reset-password design for when the backend adds the endpoint (fields: new password + confirmation; success routes to /login with "Password updated. Sign in with your new password."). Per acad-9s3.2 the reset revokes all tokens, stays independent of email verification, and its links expire after 60 minutes.

## 6. Session expiry and 401 recovery

6.1 This restates acad-abl.3 and acad-abl.13 conventions 6, 11, and 36 as UX; nothing new is invented. One global axios response interceptor owns 401: clear the token, redirect to /login?redirectTo={path+search}&reason=expired. The reason parameter drives an info Banner at the top of the login form: "Your session ended. Sign in again to continue." (DS-W-02 order; DS-A-09: banner, never toast-only).
6.2 After the next successful login the client honors redirectTo so deep links survive (acad-abl.3). No form state survives the redirect; the redirectTo flow restores the route, not the draft (convention 36).
6.3 Components never see a 401 and never toast one (conventions 6 and 11). Wrong credentials stay inline field errors; an expired session is the banner. The two never blend.

## 7. Logout

7.1 Entry: the "Sign out" item in the topbar account menu. No confirm dialog: logout is low risk and fully recoverable, and a modal here needs neither interruption nor protected focus (craft-floor refuse list).
7.2 Sequence: best-effort POST /api/logout; in a finally block remove the token from localStorage, clear the react-query cache, and navigate to /login (acad-abl.3). If the POST 401s because the token already died, the logout flow swallows it and navigates once; the api-client suppresses the interceptor redirect for the in-flight logout call so the user never sees reason=expired on a self-initiated logout.
7.3 Feedback: the menu item shows the spinner while pending (aria-busy); the landing on /login is the confirmation; no toast (DP-06, calm).

## 8. Accessibility and craft rules for X1

8.1 Forms (DS-A-04): every input has a visible label wired with htmlFor/id; helper and error text connect through aria-describedby; error containers announce with role="alert" (ui-ux-pro-max: errors must be announced; never color alone, DS-A-05). Failed submit focuses the first errored field (convention 31).
8.2 Authentication must not depend on cognitive tests: no captcha, no OTP transcription, paste allowed, password managers allowed via correct autocomplete tokens (ui-ux-pro-max result: WCAG 2.2 accessible authentication).
8.3 Targets and type: 44px controls on touch viewports (DS-S-01); input text 16px to stop iOS zoom (design.md 5.2); labels text-sm weight 500.
8.4 Page structure (DS-A-08): one h1 per surface ("Sign in", "Create your account", "Reset your password", "Email verification"), landmark main inside auth-layout, per-route document title and html lang/dir updates.
8.5 RTL and themes (DS-L-03, DS-C-03): logical properties only; the language toggle mirrors; both themes render with token flips only; focus ring is the one --ring token (DS-C-05).
8.6 Craft floor: calm institutional Operate surface (DP-01); one card panel, no nested cards, no decoration without a job, no gradient text, one primary action per surface (DP-03); buttons are verbs in three words or fewer (DS-W-04); no exclamation marks, no emoji, no em dashes, curly quotes (DS-W-05); Latin numerals (DS-W-06); every string lives in the EN/AR dictionary before merge (DS-W-01). States shipped per surface: default, hover, focus-visible, disabled, loading, plus each surface's error and terminal states named above.
8.7 Implementation rides the existing pieces: form, button, banner, link from src/components/ui per design.md 6.2 X1 row; new UI components follow DS-CP-01 through DS-CP-03.

## Flags for the owner

1. Contract drift on POST /api/register: RegisterInput requires name and carries no student_id and no password_confirmation. acad-9s3.2 says the platform stores no hand-typed name (SIS supplies it at verification) and makes student ID a required self-supplied field. The contract needs a fix; acad-abl.20 territory.
2. Resend path: POST /api/email/verification-notification documents 401, yet a user pending verification cannot log in to hold a token. The only map-backed resend is re-registering with the same email and student ID (acad-9s3.2). Confirm the mechanism, or make the endpoint accept an unauthenticated, throttled email parameter.
3. Missing reset screen: no POST /api/reset-password exists and no landing for the signed reset link is defined anywhere. Until the backend adds it, the SPA ends forgot-password at the sent confirmation (decision 5.4). Proposed SPA design: /reset-password?token=&email= with new password plus confirmation, success to /login.
4. The email link must target the SPA (decision 4.1), but the contract documents no signature or expires query parameters on GET /api/verify-email/{id}/{hash}. The backend must document how the signed-link signature is validated when the link points at the SPA route.
5. design.md 6.2 X1 lists only /login and /signup. Decisions 1.1 and 5.1 add /forgot-password and /verify-email/:id/:hash. Add both to the next design.md maintenance pass, the same pass acad-abl.8 already flagged.
6. Parked accounts at verification: decision 4.4 assumes a 200 whose user envelope carries pending_admin_at; the contract's 200 description says "binding complete" only. Confirm the parked response shape.
7. acad-abl.3 wrote /auth/login; acad-abl.8 decision 3 renamed the X1 routes to /login and /signup. This resolution follows acad-abl.8; acad-abl.3's paths are superseded.
close_reason: Auth and account UX resolved: 8 numbered decisions covering login, signup with student-ID binding, verification landing, forgot password, 401 recovery, logout, and X1 a11y craft; 7 owner flags on contract drift

title: API and state conventions
description:
## Question

What are the client conventions for API access, error handling, caching, and forms?

## Context

Inputs: the resolutions of "Client API inventory from the OpenAPI contract", "Frontend constraint digest from backend decisions", and "Mock server generated from the OpenAPI contract". Decide: the axios instance and envelope unwrap; the error taxonomy and its UX mapping (422 slugs to inline or toast, 401, 403, 409, the 503 SIS outage banner, X-Request-Id surfacing); the query-key factory and invalidation policy; where optimistic updates are safe; form patterns with React Hook Form + zod for nested plan drafts; the notification polling cadence; the MSW dev workflow.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with the grilling and domain-modeling skills.

## Record

Numbered conventions, each stated as a one-line rule the spec can quote.
notes:
# API and state conventions

RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; feature answers cited from the backend map)

Resolution for acad-abl.13 (wayfinder:grilling). Rules are numbered so the spec can quote them. Sources: acad-abl.2 (API inventory), acad-abl.1 (constraint digest), acad-abl.3 (token storage), acad-abl.7 (mock server), design.md sections 4, 8, 9, and backend map acad-9s3 settled decisions 7, 8, 10, 17, 19, 20.

## 1. Axios instance and request pipeline

1. One axios instance lives in src/lib/api-client.ts with baseURL from env.API_URL; features import it and never create their own instances.
2. The request interceptor attaches Authorization: Bearer from the localStorage token plus Accept: application/json, and drops withCredentials because the client runs Sanctum token mode (acad-abl.3).
3. The response interceptor returns response.data, the envelope body, and nothing more; envelope unwrapping stays in four shared fetcher helpers: unwrap for single resources, unwrapList for the five plain arrays, unwrapPage for the three paginated lists, and the SSE reader for the two stream endpoints (acad-abl.2).
4. The interceptor normalizes every failure into one ApiError type with status, key, fields (the 422 errors record), message, and requestId; components never read axios error objects.
5. The interceptor captures X-Request-Id from success and error responses into ApiError.requestId; destructive banners print it as a muted reference line so support can trace the request (acad-abl.2).
6. The interceptor owns 401 alone: clear the token, redirect to /auth/login with redirectTo set to path plus search, and let the login screen show the session-expired banner; never toast a 401 (acad-abl.3).
7. The interceptor never toasts on its own; the blanket toast in the current api-client.ts dies, and every status surfaces through section 2.
8. No client-side TTL on the token exists because TokenResponse carries no expiry; 401 is the single expiry signal (acad-abl.3).

## 2. Error status taxonomy and copy

Copy follows design.md 8: DS-W-02 orders errors as what happened, why, what to do; buttons are verbs; every string sits in the i18n dictionary in EN and AR (DS-W-01). Server error messages are localized en/ar (decision 7), so the client renders the server message when one exists and never invents copy for API failures.

9. 422 maps the errors record onto fields: form errors go inline under their field through react-hook-form setError; plan gate errors render in the ValidationPanel and under plan lines (DS-ST-09, DS-ST-11); a 422 whose key matches no visible field falls back to a toast with the server message.
10. The four plan gate keys have fixed surfaces: allowance, map_membership, and prerequisite_chain list per course line with the server text; window (plan.window_closed, submit only) renders the WindowClosedBanner pattern at the submit CTA (design.md 4.3, acad-abl.1).
11. Components treat 401 as unreachable; the interceptor has already redirected (acad-abl.3).
12. 403 renders the permission-denied state: a calm panel with a role reminder and a way back ("This area is for advisors. Go to your dashboard."), never an error aesthetic, never a toast (design.md 4.3).
13. 404 renders the not-found page at the route level and EmptyState at the data level, naming the missing thing and the first step per DS-W-07.
14. 409 is prevented by UI state guards: chips and DS-ST-05 disabled affordances decide what is pressable; a 409 that still arrives means stale UI, so the client invalidates the touched entity root, re-renders the true state, and toasts one calm line ("That action is no longer available. Your view is up to date.").
15. 429 with advisor.quota_exhausted renders inline in the chat panel, disables the composer, and offers no retry: "You have used your conversation limit for this term. You can still edit and submit your plan in the Plan Builder." The quota is 100 turns per term and retry means a new turn, which cannot succeed this term (decision 20, acad-abl.1).
16. 429 throttle on login, resend, and registration resend renders an inline field error: "Too many attempts. Try again in a minute."
17. 503 with service slugs (plan.sis_unavailable, plan.window_unavailable, plan.term_unavailable, visit.term_unavailable) renders a global destructive Banner with Retry: "The university data service is unavailable. Your data may be out of date. Retry in a moment." At the submit gate the same pattern sits next to the CTA and blocks submission; any undocumented 5xx follows this pattern.
18. SSE error frames (advisor.turn_failed, advisor.turn_timeout) render as an inline failed-turn row in the conversation with a Retry action when retryable is true; applied tool effects stay and the conversation history is the recovery surface (decision 20, acad-abl.1).
19. No surface ever shows a raw status code, an axios message, or a server string outside the dictionary flow; when the server message is missing, the client falls back to the dictionary key for that status family.

## 3. Query keys

20. The client adopts the acad-abl.2 scheme: one root key per entity, request params as the second element, detail keys nested under the root, and every mutation invalidates the root of each entity it touches, with scoped invalidation only where a detail cache exists.
21. Each feature owns a queryKeys factory and queryOptions helpers in src/features/<feature>/api/; raw key arrays never appear in components.
22. Canonical roots: ['me'], ['academic-record'], ['advisor-profile'], ['notifications', { perPage }], ['plan'], ['plan', 'comments'], ['plan-conversations', params] with ['plan-conversations', conversationId] nested, the ['advisor', ...] subtree, ['visit-requests'] (student side, invalidation only), ['governance'], and the ['admin', ...] subtree (acad-abl.2).
23. Plan mutations apply server truth with setQueryData(['plan'], returnedPlan) instead of a blind invalidate because every plan mutation returns the full plan, and they invalidate ['plan', 'comments'] where comments are affected (acad-abl.2).

## 4. Staleness, focus, and polling

24. Global defaults stay as the repo sets them: staleTime 60 seconds, refetchOnWindowFocus false, retry false; Retry is an explicit button per design.md 4.3.
25. Per-family overrides: ['me'] staleTime Infinity with invalidation on login, logout, and 401; ['plan'] and ['plan', 'comments'] staleTime 0 because the advisor and the AI mutate server side; ['plan-conversations'] list 30 seconds and the open conversation 0; ['academic-record'] 5 minutes; ['advisor', 'queue'] and ['advisor', 'caseload'] 30 seconds with refetchOnWindowFocus true; ['advisor', 'availability'], ['governance'], and ['admin'] 5 minutes with no polling.
26. Notifications poll every 30 seconds in the foreground through refetchInterval and pause when the tab hides; the poll endpoint is the only delivery and there is no SSE for notifications (decision 8); unread_count from the same response drives the topbar badge.
27. SIS staleness never triggers refetch loops: the client renders last_synced_at plus the three staleness booleans as the StaleDataBanner ("Data as of {date, time}. Retry.") and lets the user pull (acad-abl.1, design.md 4.3).

## 5. Optimistic updates

28. Optimistic updates are allowed only for notification read and read-all because both return 204 and carry no server state a client can contradict.
29. Plan course edits are never optimistic: the mutation waits for the server, then setQueryData(['plan'], serverPlan) applies the response, because the shared mutation surface enforces draft-only and map guards server side (decision 19).
30. Every optimistic write snapshots the previous cache in onMutate, restores it in onError, and refetches in onSettled; an optimistic value never outlives its mutation.

## 6. Forms

31. Every form runs react-hook-form with a zod resolver, mode onBlur, and revalidation on change after first submit; failed submit focuses the first errored field through the focus API (DS-A-04).
32. Zod schemas live in the feature that owns the form beside its fetcher, and each schema exports its type with z.infer so schema and type cannot drift.
33. Nested plan course drafts use useFieldArray over z.array(courseDraftSchema) with code, group, and section; the client never sends a reason because reasons are AI-only (decision 19; 422 plan.reason_forbidden).
34. Zod messages come from the i18n dictionary so EN and AR ship final per DS-W-01, and they pass the no-label test per DS-W-03.
35. On 422 the form merges server errors over client errors with setError, and server messages win because they carry the authoritative slug context in the user's language (decision 7).
36. No form state survives a 401: the redirect unmounts the form and the redirectTo flow restores the route, not the draft (acad-abl.2 gap 1, acad-abl.3).

## 7. Mock server workflow

37. One MSW 2 handler set serves all three surfaces: the browser worker under ENABLE_API_MOCKING=true npm run dev, node server.ts for vitest, and the express standalone server via npm run run-mock-server under pm2 for Playwright (acad-abl.7).
38. Handlers are typed through openapi-typescript types plus openapi-msw createOpenApiHttp over @mswjs/data models; no random-data generators live in the tree (acad-abl.7).
39. Scenarios are named seed functions: happy (default), empty, error, permission-denied, stale-sis, registration-closed, quota-exhausted; browser dev switches with ?scenario= persisted to sessionStorage, tests switch with server.use overrides, and e2e switches with POST /__mocks/scenario before navigation (acad-abl.7).
40. SSE mocks use sse() from msw/sse in the browser with the seven typed frames, and two express stream routes in mock-server.ts on the standalone path; the quota-exhausted scenario returns JSON 429 before the stream opens (acad-abl.7, decision 20).
41. Vitest routes every network call through MSW; tests never stub fetch or axios directly.

## Flags for the owner

- No window dates exist anywhere in the contract (acad-abl.1 contradiction 8): WindowClosedBanner cannot be data-driven and renders only on the submit 422 window key, the 503 plan.window_unavailable, and window notification deep links. A current-term read endpoint would fix the dashboard countdown.
- Notification.deep_link is an unformatted string (acad-abl.2 gap 7): notification routing needs its fixed shape, SPA route or API path, before the notification center can be built.
- No page query parameter is documented (acad-abl.2 gap 3): tables follow links.next when present; confirm the param name so clients can request arbitrary pages.
- No language preference write endpoint exists (acad-abl.2 gap 6): the language toggle persists client side only and seeds from user.language_preference until a PATCH /api/me lands.
- No endpoint exposes the remaining turn quota (acad-abl.2 gap 9): the chat UI shows quota state only at 429; a live counter needs an endpoint.
- Students cannot list their own visit requests (acad-abl.2 gap 4): the delete affordance has no id source and no open-request status surface.
close_reason: 41 numbered conventions set: axios pipeline with ApiError and X-Request-Id, status-to-UX taxonomy per design.md 8, acad-abl.2 query keys, per-family staleness with 30s notification polling, opt-in optimism for notification reads only, RHF+zod rules, one MSW handler set with scenarios; 6 owner flags recorded

title: App skeleton and demo demolition
description:
## Question

What stays and what goes from the bulletproof-react demo, and what skeleton does the Advaisor client build on?

## Context

The repo is a single Vite app (no monorepo, despite AGENTS.md). Demo features: auth, discussions, comments, teams, users. design.md 6.1 defines role-scoped rails; 6.2 defines the route inventory (23 surfaces plus modals). Decide: which demo parts survive as scaffolding (api client, form, notifications, testing setup) and which are deleted; the feature-folder layout for Advaisor features; router structure with role guards per the permission matrix; per-role layouts; env and config; plop generators. Trusted package installs are authorized with a stated reason.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with the grilling and domain-modeling skills and the grilling-session setup.

## Record

The kept/deleted list, the feature layout convention, the router and guard design, and the env variable list, as numbered decisions.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01; design decided per design.md, feature answers cited from the backend map)

Ticket: acad-abl.8 App skeleton and demo demolition
Inputs: design.md 0.5, 3.7, 5, 6; docs/product/01-PRODUCT-FOUNDATION.md 8 and 14; backend map acad-9s3 (settled decisions 1-23); repo src/, router, config, plop, package.json. Impeccable (Operate mode) informed craft judgment only; structure follows design.md.

## Decision 1: Demo demolition and survival list

Delete:
- src/features/comments, discussions, teams, users (all api and components).
- src/app/routes/app/discussions, dashboard.tsx, users.tsx, profile.tsx (demo pages that import deleted features).
- src/app/routes/landing.tsx. Advaisor has no marketing surface; `/` becomes a role redirect (Decision 4).
- Demo MSW handlers (comments, discussions, teams, users) and the demo factories in src/testing/mocks/db.ts. Keep browser.ts, server.ts, index.ts, utils.ts, data-generators.ts, setup-tests.ts, test-utils.tsx. Advaisor fixtures land with the first feature ticket.
- authorization.tsx ROLES (ADMIN/USER) and the comment POLICIES entry. The Authorization component mechanism stays and gains the five real roles (Decision 5).
- The demo nav inside components/layouts/dashboard-layout.tsx; the shell is rebuilt as app-shell (Decision 6). Delete content-layout.tsx once nothing imports it (knip confirms).
- The teamId/teamName branch in registerInputSchema (src/lib/auth.tsx). It references the deleted teams feature.

Keep as-is:
- src/lib/api-client.ts (axios), react-query.ts, react-query-auth wiring in auth.tsx. Bearer auth matches backend decision 1 (Sanctum personal access tokens).
- src/components/ui: button, dialog, drawer, dropdown, form, link, md-preview, notifications, spinner, table. design.md 5.2 marks all of these "exists". md-preview plus dompurify serves AI chat markdown later.
- src/components/errors, seo (Head), src/hooks/use-disclosure, src/utils (cn, format).
- mock-server.ts, the run-mock-server script, pm2 e2e wiring, playwright config.
- Storybook with the a11y addon, stryker, knip, husky, lint-staged, eslint gates, npm run verify. No gate weakens.
- src/features/auth as the one surviving feature; its forms keep compiling after the team-field strip. The real X1 rework (email verification, student ID binding, language preference per backend decision 2) is feature work, not skeleton work.

## Decision 2: Feature folder convention

Features follow the bulletproof-react layout (api, components, hooks, stores, types, utils inside each folder) and never import from each other. The twelve Advaisor feature folders, names from design.md 6.2:

| Folder | Owns | Backend map citations |
|---|---|---|
| auth | X1 login, signup, session | decisions 1, 2 |
| plan | S2 My Plan: plan detail, advisor comments, Seen, verification result | decisions 6, 10, 11, 17 |
| plan-builder | S3 Builder: planned-course rows, shared mutation surface client, validation panel, submit gate | decisions 3, 17, 19 |
| ai-chat | S5 Chat: SSE turns, conversations list, Goal Suggestions, submit confirmation | decisions 4, 5, 13, 14, 20 |
| advisor-queue | A1 Queue: queue table, review drawer, return reason, visit requests in queue | decisions 11, 22, 23 |
| advisor-students | A2 Student explorer (advisor caseload only) | decision 22 |
| advisor-meetings | A3 Meetings: Proposed to Done visit requests | decision 23 |
| advisor-hours | A4 Office hours: availability windows, max 5 | decision 23 |
| governance | D1, D2 dean and V1, V2 VP aggregate surfaces, exports | decisions 9, 15, 22 |
| admin | Accounts, caseloads, rules, system log | decision 18 |
| notifications | Shared notification center for S6, A5, D4 | decisions 8, 11 notification list |
| profile | S4 Profile: CGPA, remaining requirements, prereq map, history | academic record decision (map note: acad-9s3.8) |

Cross-feature domain components (PlanStateChip, StaleDataBanner, WindowClosedBanner and anything design.md 5.4 that more than one feature renders) live in a new src/components/domain/ folder. One feature owning them would force banned cross-feature imports. This is a new base folder, so it takes effect when the owner approves this resolution.

## Decision 3: Route tree

Paths live in src/config/paths.ts with getHref builders. The tree follows design.md 6.2 with two backend-map corrections (see Flags):

- `/` RoleRedirect: unauthenticated to `/login`, otherwise to the role landing.
- X1: `/login`, `/signup` under auth-layout (design.md 6.2 route names; replaces the current `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`).
- `/app` student section (spacious shell): index S1 dashboard, `/app/plan` S2, `/app/builder` S3, `/app/profile` S4, `/app/chat` S5, `/app/notifications` S6.
- `/advisor` section (compact shell): index A1 queue, `/advisor/students` A2, `/advisor/meetings` A3, `/advisor/hours` A4, `/advisor/notifications` A5.
- `/dean` section (compact shell): index D1 overview, `/dean/advisors/:id` D2, `/dean/notifications` D4. No `/dean/students`: the dean reads aggregates only with no student explorer (backend decisions 15, 22).
- `/vp` section (compact shell): index V1 scorecard, `/vp/drilldown` V2.
- `/admin` section (compact shell): index M1 accounts, `/admin/caseloads` M2, `/admin/rules` M4, `/admin/log` M5. No `/admin/structure`: no org tree is stored and the admin console holds exactly six capabilities (backend decisions 15, 18). The queue-aging threshold renders on `/admin/rules` as a platform-config parameter beside the SIS-sourced values, distinguished by source badge.
- `*` not-found.

## Decision 4: Guards and role redirect

- ROLES becomes STUDENT, ADVISOR, DEAN, VP, ADMIN (design.md 1.2, foundation 5).
- ProtectedRoute stays as the authentication gate for all five sections.
- A new RoleRoute component in src/lib/authorization.tsx wraps each section layout: it reads the role from useUser and renders the permission-denied state (design.md 4.3, calm panel with a way back) on direct URL hits. DS-L-01 holds: navigation is role-scoped at the route level.
- POLICIES starts empty; permission checks derive from the foundation 8 matrix as features land.
- RoleRedirect and post-login redirect both go to the role landing: student `/app`, advisor `/advisor`, dean `/dean`, vp `/vp`, admin `/admin` (design.md 6.1 landing column).

## Decision 5: Per-role layout shells and density

One app-shell per design.md 5.5 (left rail + topbar) replaces dashboard-layout. The shell reads the role, renders that role's rail items from a single role-to-items config map, and applies the density variant from design.md 3.7: spacious (p-4/p-6, 44px controls) for the student shell, compact (p-3/p-4, 36px desktop controls behind pointer-fine) for the four staff shells. The topbar carries language toggle, theme toggle, notification bell with unread badge, account menu. AI chat appears only in the student rail (PR-08). auth-layout stays for X1. The E-JUST logo mark replaces the bulletproof logo in the shell per the superdesign logo invariant; the asset swap is a later design ticket.

## Decision 6: Lazy loading

Keep the current pattern: every route lazy-loads through convert(queryClient) with clientLoader/clientAction support. Each of the five sections lazy-loads its own shell module, so a student never downloads staff code. Route-level splitting per design.md 0.5; no splitting below route level.

## Decision 7: Env and config

Keep the src/config/env.ts mechanism (VITE_APP_ prefix stripped, zod validated). Exactly four variables:

| Variable | Purpose | Example default |
|---|---|---|
| VITE_APP_API_URL | Advaisor API base | http://localhost:8000/api (no version prefix per backend API conventions, acad-9s3.17) |
| VITE_APP_ENABLE_API_MOCKING | MSW browser worker switch for dev and tests | true in development, false in e2e |
| VITE_APP_APP_URL | App origin, used by mock-server CORS | http://localhost:3000 |
| VITE_APP_APP_MOCK_API_PORT | Mock server port | 8080 |

No new variables. SSE chat streams over the same API_URL base (backend decision 4). Language comes from the per-student preference record (backend decision 7), never from env. Update .env.example to these values (the current file carries a stray `true.env` artifact to remove).

## Decision 8: Generators

- The component generator already lists src/features dynamically, so it picks up the new feature names with no code change.
- Extend the component generator to emit a `<name>.test.tsx` alongside index, component, and story. DS-CP-03 requires a story and a test on every ui component; the generator should not let either be forgotten.
- Add a `feature` generator that scaffolds src/features/<name>/ with api, components, hooks, stores, types, utils and .gitkeep files, so the twelve folders stay uniform.
- Register both in plopfile.cjs.

## Verification note

Implementation of this skeleton lands in build tickets, each staged and run through npm run verify per AGENTS.md. This resolution records decisions only (DS-AI-07).

## Flags for the owner

1. design.md 6.1 and 6.2, and foundation 14, still list a dean student explorer (D3, rail item, `/dean/students`). Backend decisions 15 and 22 removed it: the dean reads aggregates only. This resolution omits the route; both docs need a maintenance pass.
2. design.md 6.2 lists Admin M3 "Structure". Backend decisions 15 and 18 store no org tree and cap the admin console at six capabilities with no structure editor. The route is omitted; the docs need the same pass.
3. design.md 5.4 DraftPlanCard and foundation 12/14 describe an AI draft handoff card. Backend decision 13 removed the draft artifact: the AI edits the one plan through tools. Rework the S1/S5 design when ai-chat is built.
4. design.md 5.4 VisitRequestCard (Accept/Decline) and foundation 8, 10, 11 (visit approve/deny, related triggers) contradict backend decision 23: visits are Proposed to Done with no approval, denial, slot picking, or booking. Rework the visit design when advisor-meetings is built.
5. Dean keeps a notification center (D4) in both frontend docs, but the backend trigger list names no dean recipient. The page is kept as role-scoped and empty-capable. Confirm whether D4 survives v1.
6. src/components/domain/ is a new base folder and needs the owner's standing approval per repo rules; it takes effect with this resolution's approval.
close_reason: Resolved: demo features and routes deleted, 12 Advaisor feature folders fixed, role-guarded route tree per design.md 6.2 with backend-map corrections (no dean explorer, no admin structure), four env vars kept, plop gains test and feature generators.

title: Component primitive gap list
description:
## Question

Which UI primitives does the client add beyond the existing set, and on which base?

## Context

design.md 5 lists what exists (button, dialog, drawer, dropdown, form, table, spinner, notifications, link, md-preview) versus what to build. Surfaces will likely need: combobox (course search), tabs, toast, a time grid or calendar (office hours), popover, command palette, badge or chip (PlanStateChip), skeleton, tooltip. Decide: shadcn-style copies on Radix per AGENTS.md, the concrete add list, the date/time utility stance (dayjs is installed), and icon rules (lucide-react is installed). Revisit after the surface tickets if they surface more needs.

HITL: resolves only with the map owner. Open with grilling and domain-modeling.

## Record

The ordered add list, each mapped to the Radix primitive it builds on.
notes:
RESOLUTION (agent, owner-delegated 2026-10-01)

# acad-abl.9: Component primitive gap list

Question: which UI primitives does the client add beyond the existing set, and on which base?

Existing set (design.md 5.2, verified in src/components/ui/): button, dialog, drawer, dropdown, form (field, input, select, textarea), table + pagination, spinner, notifications, link, md-preview. Installed Radix packages: dialog, dropdown-menu, label, slot, switch.

## Derivation from the 23 surfaces (design.md 6.2)

Needs that repeat across surfaces, and the primitive each one requires:

| Need (surfaces) | Primitive verdict |
|---|---|
| Card containers, scorecard cells (S1, S4, D1, D2, V1) | card, kpi-card |
| Rule source badges (M1-M5), aging badge (A1), "AI draft" badge (S1, S5) | badge |
| Plan state display on every plan surface (S1-S3, A1) | chip (anatomy base of PlanStateChip) |
| Error, stale SIS, window closed notices (X1, S1-S3, all) | banner |
| Loading state on every surface (4.3, DS-M-05) | skeleton |
| Empty state on every surface (4.3) | empty-state |
| Student identity in queue rows and drawers (A1-A3, D3) | avatar |
| Destructive and consequential confirms (A1, S1, S2, M1-M5) | confirm-dialog |
| Queue filters, profile sections (A1, S4, design.md 5.3) | tabs |
| Dense staff tables, icon-only controls (A1, D1-D3, V1-V2, M1-M5) | tooltip |
| Course picker (S3), visit slot picker (A1) | popover + combobox |
| Plan progress line (S1, S2 plan-card) | progress |
| Course search data | client-side filter over the student's prerequisite_map (see D3) |
| Office hours editing (A4) | form rows on existing form primitives, no calendar (see D2) |
| Transient action feedback (all) | existing notifications layer, no new toast (see D4) |
| Side panels (A1, A2, D3) | existing drawer, no separate sheet |
| Funnel and trends (D1, D2) | recharts, per acad-abl.5, blocked on approval (see D6) |

No surface in 6.2 needs: command palette, accordion, breadcrumb, checkbox, radio group (pending one X1 question), calendar or time grid, separate toast, separate sheet.

## D1. Ordered add list (14 items)

Build order: pure components first (no dependency approval, unblock the most surfaces), compositions next, Radix-backed last in dependency order. Every item lands in the base library now, each with story and test (DS-CP-03).

| # | Primitive | Base | Surfaces |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | card | compose (no Radix); `rounded-lg border bg-card`, per 5.3 | S1, S4, S5, base of kpi-card and plan-card |
| 2 | badge | compose; 3.3 tint pairs, dot + text per 5.3 | M1-M5, A1 aging badge, S1/S5 source badge |
| 3 | chip | compose on badge anatomy; interactive, 44px remove target per 5.3 | anatomy base of PlanStateChip (S1-S3, A1) |
| 4 | banner | compose; variants info, warning, destructive, stale, window-closed per 5.3 | X1 plus the error/stale/window states of every surface (4.3) |
| 5 | skeleton | compose; `animate-pulse` on `bg-muted`, shape-matched per 5.3 | every surface loading state (DS-M-05) |
| 6 | empty-state | compose; icon 24px, title, one line body, one action per 5.3 | every surface (4.3) |
| 7 | avatar | compose; initials, role tints, sizes 24/32/40 per 5.3 | A1, A2, A3, D3 |
| 8 | confirm-dialog | compose on existing dialog; focus starts on cancel, verb-specific confirm per 5.3 | A1 approve/return, S1 discard draft, S2 seen, M1-M5 |
| 9 | kpi-card | compose on card; tabular-nums value, dense variant per 5.3 | D1, D2, V1, S4 |
| 10 | tabs | @radix-ui/react-tabs; underline indicator per 5.3 | A1 queue filters, S4 profile sections |
| 11 | tooltip | @radix-ui/react-tooltip; 300ms delay, dark inverse surface per 5.3 | staff tables, topbar icon controls |
| 12 | popover | @radix-ui/react-popover | base of combobox (S3), A1 slot picker |
| 13 | combobox | compose on popover + existing form input + listbox; no cmdk | S3 course picker |
| 14 | progress | @radix-ui/react-progress; plan-state colors allowed here per DS-C-09 | S1, S2 plan progress line |

Table enhancements (dense mode, `tabular-nums`, sticky header, `aria-sort`, page sizes 10/20/50/All) are an in-place upgrade of the existing table per 5.2, not a new primitive. Pagination exists. Select and textarea exist in the form wrappers. Switch is installed for the theme and language toggles.

New Radix dependencies, one DS-G-07 approval each before the item lands: react-tabs, react-tooltip, react-popover, react-progress.

## D2. Blocked on later tickets versus base library now

Land now: all 14 items in D1. They serve every role and block no surface ticket.

Deferred to surface tickets:

- Time grid or calendar: not a primitive in v1. The contract serves availability as day plus naive H:i rows, at most five per window (openapi.json AvailabilityWindowInput, maxItems 5). A4 SlotEditor is form rows on the existing form primitives. If a visual week grid is ever wanted, it is an advisor domain component under acad-abl.16, not a ui/ primitive.
- Charts: recharts is the one external chart dependency (acad-abl.5). It lands with acad-abl.17 after DS-G-07 approval, route-split to /dean and /vp. Funnel and trend sparklines only; scoreboard, scorecard, and drill-down stay plain HTML; the heatmap is a hand-rolled token grid.
- Command palette, accordion, breadcrumb: no surface in 6.2 needs them. DP-02 says cut what has no job. Revisit only if a surface ticket proves the need.
- Radio group: the X1 language preference choice may want one; decide at acad-abl.12.
- Checkbox: no surface spec names one.

## D3. PlanStateChip approach

The contract is the source of truth for states: openapi.json PlanStatus and backend app/Enums/PlanStatus.php hold nine values, and `discarded` is the ninth terminal (DiscardPlanController, POST /api/plan/discard).

- Component: domain component in src/features/plan/components/, built on the chip anatomy. DS-C-09 confines plan-state colors to PlanStateChip, plan-state banners, and plan progress visuals.
- Variants per 5.4: chip (default), dot-only (dense tables), banner-size (page headers). Anatomy: dot + state label + lock icon on locked states (DS-ST-05). SR text "Plan status: {state}" (DS-A-03). `chip-in` 150ms on change, polite live region (DS-ST-06). Labels bilingual (DS-W-01).
- Token mapping (design.md 3.4 and Appendix B, 8 pairs):

| Contract value | Token pair |
|---|---|
| draft | state-draft |
| submitted | state-submitted |
| under_review | state-under-review |
| returned | state-returned + lock icon |
| approved | state-approved + lock icon |
| expired | state-failed + border-dashed |
| closed | state-closed |
| withdrawn | state-closed |
| discarded | state-closed, own label, slate dot |

- `discarded` reuses the state-closed pair with its own label. A dedicated token pair is a DS-G-02 change and needs a human-approved proposal; the gray terminal family is the honest default until then.
- The type map keeps state-confirmed (Registration Confirmed) and state-failed (Verification Failed) entries so that a contract fix is a one-line enum addition. See flag 1.

## D4. Date and time stance on dayjs

- dayjs stays the only date library (DS-L-07). No new date dependency.
- Add the utc and timezone plugins when the first ISO date-time renders: visit request slots (starts_at, ends_at), academic record last_synced_at for the stale banner. The backend serves UTC (config/app.php `'timezone' => 'UTC'`), and Africa/Cairo observes DST, so conversion is real. Display converts to Africa/Cairo, then renders 24h HH:mm with no zone suffix (DS-W-06).
- Availability window rows are naive day + H:i strings in the contract. Render as written; never convert them.
- Queue aging (3+ days, PR-13) uses dayjs core diff. The duration and relativeTime plugins stay out until a surface needs them; notification timestamps render absolute per DS-W-06.
- All formatting runs through src/lib/i18n/format.ts with the ar locale clone without digit postformat, per acad-abl.6. Numerals stay Latin (DS-T-03).

## D5. Icon rules

- lucide-react is the only icon family (DS-I-01, Appendix A confirms it over phosphor). No emoji anywhere.
- strokeWidth 2. Sizes: 16 inline and in tables, 20 on controls and nav, 24 in empty states. No other sizes.
- Decorative icons get aria-hidden (DS-I-01). Directional icons flip under RTL (DS-L-04); when unclear, add the flip.
- Primitives take a size prop constrained to the three values, never arbitrary numbers.

## D6. Naming, file conventions, and the dependency rule

- Location and shape: src/components/ui/<name>/ with <name>.tsx, <name>.stories.tsx, <name>.test.tsx, generated by npm run generate (design.md 5.1). Kebab-case files, PascalCase components.
- Build method: shadcn-style copies on Radix primitives, CVA variants, cn() (tailwind-merge), forwardRef + displayName (design.md 5.1, 0.5). Components are copied into the repo, never installed as a package.
- Gate order per component (DS-CP-02, DS-CP-01, DS-G-03): reuse check against 5.2, design-it-twice prop shapes, spec added to design.md section 5, story plus test, then build.
- Every primitive inherits the binding constraints: semantic tokens only (DS-C-01), one focus ring token (DS-C-05), one radius system (DS-R-01), borders over shadows (DS-R-02), z-scale 3.9 (DS-Z-01), motion tokens with prefers-reduced-motion (DS-M-01..03), 44px touch targets (DS-S-01), full state cycle (4.1), logical properties with rtl: reserved for icon flips (DS-L-03, acad-abl.6), dictionary-only copy (DS-W-01).
- recharts is the single external chart dependency, per the acad-abl.5 decision. Nothing else chart-related enters the tree. Recharts itself still needs DS-G-07 human approval before install.

## Flags for the owner

1. Contract gap: openapi.json PlanStatus lacks registration_confirmed and verification_failed, which design.md 3.4 and product foundation transitions 8 and 9 require (SIS verification stages). The chip keeps both token pairs mapped. Belongs on acad-abl.20.
2. discarded has no token pair in design.md. The chip reuses state-closed until a DS-G-02 token proposal (with contrast math) adds one, if a distinct visual is wanted.
3. Contract gap: no endpoint carries registration window open and close dates, so WindowClosedBanner cannot show dates yet (design.md 4.3 copy pattern shows dates). Belongs on acad-abl.20.
4. Approval queue (DS-G-07): react-tabs, react-tooltip, react-popover, react-progress now; recharts before acad-abl.17.
5. Contract gap: no course catalog search endpoint. The S3 combobox filters the student's prerequisite_map from GET /api/academic-record client-side (backend invariant: a student plans only courses in their Course Map). If the map grows past client-side filter comfort, raise it on acad-abl.20.

## Sources

- design.md: 3 (tokens, icons, motion, z-scale), 4 (states), 5.1-5.4 (component inventory and specs), 6.1-6.2 (shell and 23 surfaces), 7 (accessibility), 8 (writing), 9 (gates), 10 (DS-AI-01, DS-Q-01), 11 (DS-G-02, DS-G-03, DS-G-07), Appendix A and B
- acad-abl.5 (closed): recharts for funnel and trends only, tables stay HTML, heatmap hand-rolled
- acad-abl.6 (closed): logical properties, format.ts as the single formatting entry point, dayjs ar locale clone
- Backend contract: openapi.json (PlanStatus, AvailabilityWindowInput and Row, VisitRequestSlot, AcademicRecord.prerequisite_map, AddPlanCourseInput); app/Enums/PlanStatus.php (discarded terminal); app/Http/Controllers/Plan/DiscardPlanController.php; config/app.php (UTC); CONTEXT.md (Availability Window, Course Map invariants); docs/adr/0001-sis-owned-validation
- Skills: ui-ux-pro-max (priority order DS-Q-01), impeccable (craft floor: state cycles, depth from borders, bounded verification DS-0-03)

title: AI Advisor composer: textarea shows a scrollbar at rest (height sizing off by the border)
description:
The 'Message your AI advisor' textarea (src/features/ai-chat/components/composer.tsx) displays a scrollbar even when empty. The auto-grow effect sets element.style.height = min(element.scrollHeight, 160)px, but scrollHeight excludes the element's 1px top/bottom borders while the assigned height is border-box - so the element is sized 2px short of its padding + line height (44px assigned, 44px of inner content needed) and the browser overflows. Confirmed live: empty textarea at height: 44px with a visible scrollbar.

Fix:
- Account for the borders when sizing from scrollHeight (scrollHeight + borderTopWidth + borderBottomWidth), or
- set the initial height from a non-overflowing baseline (e.g. rows=1 without forcing height until text exceeds one line) or hide overflow until the COMPOSER_MAX_HEIGHT cap is reached.

Desired behavior: no scrollbar at rest and through single-line input; growth continues to the 160px cap; only text beyond the cap scrolls (that part is correct).

Check the same auto-grow pattern is not duplicated in other textareas (grep scrollHeight in src/) and fix them in one pass if identical.
